On 31 January 2024, for the second consecutive day, about 30 farmers blocked the roundabout of the Beneluxlaan in Kortrijk (Vlaanderen) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration by farmers against EU agricultural regulations, their national government's nitrogen policy, a lack of consideration for their work, and low production prices.

On 31 January 2024, an unknown number of tractors blocked access to the logistical centre of the supermarket company Lidl near Marche-en-Famenne (Wallonie) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration by farmers against EU agricultural regulations, their national government's nitrogen policy, a lack of consideration for their work, and low production prices.

On 18 June 2020, an unknown number of health workers staged a protest at several locations in Deinze in the context of a national action day against the underfunding of the health sector. The action was organized by ACV Puls.

On 2 February 2024, about 150 tractors paraded in Sint-Katelijne-Waver (Vlaanderen) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration by farmers against EU agricultural regulations, their national government's nitrogen policy, a lack of consideration for their work, and low production prices.

On 29 January 2024, an unknown number of farmers, including FJA members, blocked the highways E429 and E19 near the exits around Halle (Vlaanderen) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration by farmers against EU agricultural regulations, their national government's nitrogen policy, a lack of consideration for their work, and low production prices.

On 30 January 2024, about 30 people marching from France crossed the border in Baisieux and stopped in Tournai (Wallonie) to demand an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. It is part of an action rallying Paris to Brussels.

On 23 February 2024, an unknown number of Greenpeace activists plastered the facades of different companies and political parties in Brussels (Brussels) to call for a thorough reform of the economic model behind the food system, asking that more respect would be given to health and the environment. Greenpeace activists targeted the following political parties headquarters: CD&V: Flemish Christian Democrats; Open Flemish Liberals and Democrats, MR: Reformative Movement; and the European People's Party. The targeted companies were the European agricultural umbrella organization Copa-Cogeca, trade federations Comeos and EuroCommerce, and food industry federations Fevia and FoodDrinkEurope.

Around 18 June 2020, an unknown number of health workers staged a protest in Brussels - Woluwe-Saint-Lambert in the context of a national action day against the underfunding of the health sector. The action was organized by ACV Puls.

On 5 March 2024, CSC members blocked access to the prison of Lantin (Wallonie) to denounce overcrowding. The event followed the decision taken by the Hasselt prison on 2 March 2024 not to take any new prisoner, also to denounce overcrowding.

On 21 March 2024, about 50 activists protested during a nuclear summit in Brussels (Brussels) to argue for more nuclear energy as part of a solution to the climate crisis. There were protesters from 15 different countries, among which Belgium, Sweden, and the United States. The event was organized by Stand Up for Nuclear. Another group of protesters, among which members of Greenpeace International and Greenpeace France, tried to block access to the summit and to climb the building to denounce the illusory solution that nuclear energy was.

On 10 May 2024, about 300 students protested in the entrance hall of the University of Liege in Liege (Wallonie) to call on their university to cut ties with Israel and demand an 'academic boycott' of the country, while expressing solidarity with Palestinians. The event was organized by the collective Students of Liege for Palestine (Etudiants de Liege pour la Palestine). An encampment was set up and the protest lasted until 21 June 2024.

On 3 June 2024, an unknown number of protesters tried to disturb a conference on the future of Israel and Palestine in Brussels - Ixelles (Brussels) to oppose the presence of a former ambassador for Israel. The protesters have opposed the event for weeks and on 3 June 2024, the Free University of Brussels (ULB) announced that the conference was moved to Flagey Square. There, the police had sealed the neighborhood and did not allow the protesters near the event. Some protesters stayed in the surrounding streets, some went back to the university and some headed to the Israeli Embassy in Brussels - Uccle. Police arrested nine people.

On 22 June 2024, more than a thousand people protested in Gent (Vlaanderen) to express their support to the Palestinian people and to call for sanctions against Israel and for a ceasefire in Gaza. The event was organized by various civil society organizations, among which CNCD-11.11.11, Peace, the Ambassadors and the Ghent Coalition for Palestine. The Green federal deputy Prime Minister Petra de Sutter was present too.

On 26 June 2024, several dozen people, among which students from the Free University of Brussels (VUB), tried to occupy the Flemish Interuniversity Council (VLIR) building in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to demand the universities to end all collaborations with Israeli universities. They entered the building but the police immediately intervened to take them outside. There was pushing and shoving, and footage taken by students shows an officer using his pepper spray canister to knock a student's phone out of her hands. Some seated students were dragged down the stairs. The protesters were not allowed in the Ravenstein Gallery anymore and demonstrated in the street, where further confrontation occurred with the police.

On 5 July 2024, an unknown number of nursery teachers protested in Arlon (Wallonie) against the 'Excellence Pact' of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation that led to significant changes in the distribution of jobs, leaving 4 nursery teachers jobless. They denounced that the uneven distribution of new jobs and strict criteria left some municipalities like Arlon in difficulty.

On 25 August 2024, about 1,500 people participated in the Yser vigil (IJverwake) in the hamlet of Steenstroate (Vlaanderen) to pay tribute to the Flemish soldiers who died during the First World War and to advocate for Flemish independence from Belgium.

On 3 September 2024, about 80 residents protested in Kapelle-op-den-Bos (Vlaanderen) against plans to build a small water treatment plant on nearby plots of land, denouncing the way in which the plan was established by authorities.

On 22 October 2024, a protest took place in front of the city hall in Gent (Vlaanderen), where a few hundred supporters of the Green party gathered to protest against their sidelining by Mayor Mathias De Clercq and the 'Voor Gent' party (formed by Open VLD: Open Flemish Liberals and Democrats, and Vooruit), which chose to negotiate with the New Flemish Alliance (N-VA) instead.

On 26 November 2024, teachers and staff supported by unions protested in Hannut (Wallonie), as part of a wider strike of teachers and administrative staff on this day in the Federation Wallonie-Bruxelles to protest budget cuts imposed by the new MR-Engages majority government. The unions, including FGTB, CSC, and CGSLB, are concerned about the impact of these cuts on the quality and accessibility of education. The strike involved picket lines and flyer distributions at schools across Wallonia.

On 13 December 2024, several dozen people, including the families of the victims of the 2011 Liege shooting, gathered at Saint-Lambert Square in Liege (Wallonie) to pay tribute to their loved ones and demonstrate. The gathering came shortly after the families lost their appeal against the Belgian state, with the court ruling that the state held no responsibility for the conditions leading to the release of Nordine Amrani, the gunman who killed six people and injured dozens more. The families expressed frustration and disappointment with the justice system.

On 18 February 2025, in the evening, at the call of pro-Palestinian activists, around 10 people gathered near the Viage casino in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest the lecture of Israeli comedian Yohay Sponder. The protestors shouted 'Free Palestine,' and the police intervened forcefully, using tear gas to disperse the group, but conducting no arrests.

On 4 April 2025, in the afternoon, around 15 parents protested loudly in front of the Egied van Broeckhoven school in Brussels - Molenbeek-Saint-Jean (Brussels) against what they denounce as the school's excessive use of student suspensions. They accused the director of ignoring parental concerns and acting arbitrarily, citing several recent expulsions.

On 22 March 2025, in the evening, at the call of Mechelen city council, around 250 people, including a Palestinian refugee and the mayor (Open VLD), gathered on the Grote Markt in Mechelen (Vlaanderen) to hold a wake in solidarity with the victims of the Israel-Hamas conflict, expressing support for a boycott of Israeli products from occupied territories and calling for the recognition of the state of Palestine.

On 31 March 2025, between 40 to 90 striking workers and union representatives set up a checkpoint roadblock at the Havenlaan and Industrieweg intersection, blocking two key roundabouts and preventing access to about twenty companies such as Borealis and Chevron, at the Ravenshout industrial zone in Beringen (Vlaanderen), to protest the federal government's austerity measures and pension reforms. This action was part of a national general strike led by FGTB and CSC, disrupting transport, postal services, ports, and shops, in protest against the new government (Arizona) coalition's policies, particularly criticizing measures on pensions and purchasing power.

On 31 March 2025, striking workers and union representatives set up a picket line outside Tenneco in Sint-Truiden (Vlaanderen). This action was part of a national general strike led by FGTB and CSC, disrupting transport, postal services, ports, and shops, in protest against the new government (Arizona) coalition's policies, particularly criticizing measures on pensions and purchasing power.

On 30 April 2025, in the evening, during a debate between the three rector candidates for KU Leuven university in Leuven (Vlaanderen), a pro-Palestinian protest occurred regarding the university's collaboration with Israeli institutions. A group of students stood up with signs and addressed the candidates, demanding that KU Leuven take a clearer stance on its ties with Israel.

On 10 May 2025, in the afternoon, around 40 members of Bite Back demonstrated at Boudewijn Seapark in Brugge (Vlaanderen) to demand an earlier closure of the dolphinarium, currently scheduled for 2037. The protest was part of the international 'Empty the Tanks' campaign, calling for a legal ban on dolphinariums and highlighting the stress experienced by the seven dolphins kept there. Activists handed out flyers to visitors and urged companies to stop promoting visits to the park in order to make it financially unviable.

On 16 May 2025, in the evening, an unknown amount of pro-Palestinian protesters held their daily protest at the Beurs in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels), expressing support for the Palestinian people.
On 7 June 2025, activists gathered for a rally in front of a local high-end fashion boutique in Knokke-Heist (Vlaanderen), protesting against using fur for clothing and emphasizing animal rights.

On 15 January 2025, in the afternoon, around 10 CGSP Teaching (CGSP Enseignement) union delegates protested in Mons (Wallonie) by distributing flyers and engaging with the public, denouncing the government's austerity measures due to the risk of losing an estimated 500 jobs and a degradation in teaching quality, as part of a larger action of school staff across La Louviere, the Centre and Mons-Borinage.

On 25 June 2020, an unknown number of health workers staged a protest at the Terrasses du Bois retirement home in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles against the underfunding of the health sector. The protest was organized by ACV-CSC.

On 12 March 2025, in the evening, at the call of the residents' group The Barracks (De Barakken), around 20 residents of the Zuidstraat area protested at the city hall in Menen (Vlaanderen) against the development of a store, storage space, and 38 parking spots on a green recreational area, emphasizing the need to preserve the neighborhood's limited green space. Correction to BEL4401, last submitted by DG on 24 August 2025, with ID 59.

Around 25 June 2020 (weekend of), 3 activists of Schild en Vrienden staged a protest march through Trois-Ponts after municipal authorities had confiscated a Flemish flag from a youth movement camping in the neighborhood.
On 26 June 2020, an unknown number of people joined a protest organized by PVDA-PTB in Liege to denounce femicide, after the murder of a young woman earlier that week.

On 28 June 2020, at least 4 activists of 11.11.11 and Greenpeace staged a protest action in front of the Finance Tower in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to demand a more just fiscal system in Belgium, by attaching 850 pictures of online protesters at the building.

On 25 August 2025, in the evening, around 100 people gathered on the Grand-Place in Huy (Wallonie) for a pro-Palestine demonstration organized to coincide with the municipal council meeting. The protesters demanded official recognition of Palestine and the raising of the Palestinian flag on the city hall.

On 29 April 2025, in the morning, at the call of FGTB and CSC, an unspecified number of people protested at the Clown square in Eupen (Wallonie), blocking traffic and demonstrating as part of the national day of action against the federal government's pension reforms, wage norm law, and increasing work pressure.

On 29 April 2025, at the call of ACV and ABVV, several dozen people demonstrated in Leuven (Vlaanderen) as part of the national day of action against the De Wever government's pension reforms, wage norm law, and increasing work pressure. The protesters criticized excessive defense spending, with participants demanding fair reforms and greater investment in healthcare, education, and public services.

On 15 October 2025, around 50 technical employees of the Brussels electricity and gas distribution operator Sibelga began a strike and sit-in protest outside the company's headquarters in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to demand better pay and greater recognition for their profession. The strike and sit-in protest continued until at least 20 October 2025.

On 31 October 2025, around 200 teachers and CGSP Education (CGSP Enseignement) members gathered on Place Saint-Lambert in Liege (Wallonie) to protest government measures announced. Protesters highlighted concerns over a projected 10% increase in workload, job cuts, reduced supervision for students, and higher responsibilities for the same salary. The protest also addressed broader issues, including threats to free primary education, increased university tuition fees, and long-term underfunding of the education sector.

On 27 October 2025, in the evening, 20 pro-Palestinian activists from the Antwerp Coalition for Palestine (Antwerpse Coalitie voor Palestina) demonstrated at Suikerrui in Antwerpen (Vlaanderen) to support Palestine. Police arrested the demonstrators after they refused to move their protest to Steenplein, where the municipality had allowed for the demonstration to take place.

On 9 November 2025, Flemish Interest and Voorpost members protested at Sint-Andries in Brugge (Vlaanderen) to protest the purchase of the building complex by the Islamic Cultural Center (Het Islamitisch Cultureel Centrum) to build a new mosque. Demonstrators carried Flemish flags and banners reading 'raise the flag.'

On 26 November 2025, about a hundred protesters gathered in front of the supermarket Albert Heijn in Kuringen (Vlaanderen) against ongoing flexibilization and franchising in super market chains. The event was part of a three-day nationwide strike across the public and private sectors called by ABVV-FGTB, ACV-CSC and ACLVB-CGSLB to protest against the Federal Government's reform plans. Participants feared that the reform plans would lead to staff shortages, increased workloads, and reduced social protection.

On 23 November 2025, in the morning, residents and representatives of the political parties Green and N-VA protested in Sint-Kruis in Brugge (Vlaanderen) against the municipal plans for a neighborhood parking site in a current green zone, which will be voted on in an upcoming municipal council meeting.

On 15 December 2025, in the evening, more than 200 social workers, among them members of ACV-CSC and the Social Work Action Network (Sociaal Werk Actie Netwerk - SWAN), protested on the St Jansvliet in Antwerpen (Vlaanderen) against the planned budget cuts in the social and welfare sector. Protesters feared that the cuts would damage service quality in the sector and asserted they had not been involved in the decision-making.
On 18 December 2025, nature group Groot-Staden protested in Staden (Vlaanderen) against the felling of a tree.

On 25 July 2020, dozens of people staged a protest action in Aalter against the coronavirus protection measures and mouth mask obligation imposed by the Belgian authorities, with the intention of forming a protest movement.

On 24 January 2026, around 1,000 Kurdish people gathered at the Opera square and marched to Sint-Jans square in Antwerpen (Vlaanderen) to call attention to the situation of Kurdish people in northeast Syria. Protesters chanted slogans against Turkish President Erdogan and 'Women, Life, Freedom'.

On 13 February 2026, a hundred residents of the neighborhood gathered on the streets in Lemonnierwijk in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the demolition of the Zuiderpaleis for the building of metro line 3, which had been ongoing for 7 years. Residents opposed the project and feared that the new Belgian government mlight restart the work in an aim to gentrify the neighborhood.

On 18 February 2026, protesters from right-wing party VB gathered outside the center of Zele (Vlaanderen) to protest against the lights for Ramadan festivities in the city. The mayor had forbidden the protest in the city center.

On 5 March 2026, in the evening, at the call of Pax Christi, Intal, Act for Peace (Agir pour la paix), Attac Brussels, National Coordination of Action for Peace and Democracy (Coordination Nationale d'Action pour la Paix et la Democratie - CNAPD), Christian Worker Movement (Mouvement Ouvrier Chretien - MOC), Peace (Vrede), Vredesactie, ABVV-FGTB, and the youth of ABVV-FGTB and ACV-CSC unions, protesters gathered on the Schumanplein in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the American-Israeli war on Iran. Protesters denounced this war as against international law, and for sanctions on Iran to be lifted and refugees and asylum seekers to be received and taken care of. Protesters reaffirmed they did not support the Islamic regime in Iran, but said 'Democracy cannot be brought with bombs'. The protest was joined by MEP Marc Botenga (PTB) and Brussels MP Kalvin Soiresse (Ecolo).

On 7 April 2026, at the call of non-profit sector unions CNE and SETCa, more than 200 protesters gathered in front of the office of the Walloon Minister of Solidarity Yves Coppieters (Les Engages) in Namur (Wallonie) to denounce the increasing commercialization of the non-profit sector and its consequences on access to essential services. Organizers said the protest was part of the European Day against Commercialization of Health.

On 14 May 2026, overnight until 8:30 am, around hundred protesters from the collective Stop House Visits (Stop Visites Domiciliaires) gathered and set up tents in front of political party Les Engages office in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the draft law supported by the party that would allow law enforcement to enter living quarters of people who are staying in Belgium illegally and take them into administrative detention. Participants opposed the criminalization of undocumented migrants.

On 6 September 2020, around 350 people joined a protest organized by Viruswaanzin at the Finance Tower in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles against the coronavirus protection measures of the Belgian government and its impact on individual freedom. As the coronavirus social distancing rules were not respected, police forces intervened to end the protest, resulting in two arrests. One police officer was hit in the face by a demonstrator and brought to the hospital. The remainder of the protesters joined in with the action of the event sector taking place simultaneously on Mont des Arts in Brussels.
On 15 September 2020, an unknown number of Bpost workers staged a protest in Charleroi in the context of a strike within Bpost against high work load in the company.

On 24 September 2020, an unknown number of fairground operators staged a protest in Meeuwen to demand the municipal coronavirus restrictions for fairgrounds to be lifted, by blocking the road in front of the community hall for hours.
On 2 February 2020, around 500 greyhound owners staged a silent protest with their dogs in Gent against the mass slaughter of greyhounds in Spain after the hunting season.

On 16 October 2020, an unknown number of people from Armenian descent staged a protest at the border crossing between Belgium and the Netherlands on the E19 highway in Meer, to raise awareness for the ensuing war between Armenia and Azerbaijan and to demand measures from the EU.

On 11 February 2020, around 200 people joined a protest organized by Vlaams Belang in Kalmthout against a planned asylum facility in Kalmthout. At the same time and location, around 20 people staged a silent counterprotest.
Around 7 December 2020 (as reported), an unknown number of health workers staged a protest outside a retirement home in Vottem to denounce a lack of resources to do their job successfully.

On 26 December 2020, an unknown number of workers staged a protest in the Westland Shopping Center in Brussels - Anderlecht to denounce the imminent closure of several stores of the WE clothing branch, blocking access to the local WE store. The protest was organized by ACV-CSC.

On 19 February 2021, an unknown number of people staged a protest at the city hall of Gent against the imminent establishment of a new gas energy facility of Luminus in Wondelgem. The action was an initiative of Gents Tegengas.

On 22 February 2021, an unknown number of activists of the No Profit On Pandemic coalition staged a protest flash mob at Schuman Square in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to demand action from the European Commission against the patent on the coronavirus vaccine of the major pharmaceutical companies.
On 15 July 2020, residents took to the streets in Gabrovo, demanding the resignation of the Bulgarian Prime Minister and chief prosecutor, accusing them of corruption and links to criminal groups.

On 16 July 2020, residents participated in a protest march in Haskovo, demanding the resignation of the Bulgarian Prime Minister and chief prosecutor, accusing them of corruption and links to criminal groups.

On 24 July 2020, thousands of residents staged a demonstration in Sofia, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and Chief Prosecutor Geshev accusing them of corruption and links to criminal groups. There were clashes with police, who escorted the chairman of GERB and the leader of BSP, after they had taken part in a TV broadcast, while people shouted slogans against them.
On 26 August 2020, residents stage a protest, including an exhibition and dance, in Veliko Tarnovo, demanding the resignation of government over alleged corruption and support for oligarchy.

On 25 August 2020, trade and transport companies representatives from Gotse Delchev staged a protest at the border of Greece in Ilinden, demanding that the border checkpoint, which is closed until August 31, be open to trucks.
On 23 August 2020, residents staged a protest in Plovdiv, demanding the resignation of government over alleged corruption and support for oligarchy.
On 8 September 2020, about 20 people protested in Pleven against corruption.
On 9 September 2020, thousands of people protested in Sofia demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and chief prosecutor Geshev over alleged corruption and links to mafia.

On 19 October 2020, hundreds of people protested in Sofia demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and chief prosecutor Geshev over alleged corruption and links to mafia. The protesters threw eggs and tomatoes at the building of the Ministry of Defence.
On 31 October 2020, people protested in Sofia demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and chief prosecutor Geshev over alleged corruption and links to mafia.
On 22 November 2020, dozens of people protested in Omurtag due to the prolonged water shortage in the town.
On 19 January 2021, residents protested in Rakitovo against the closure of the local bank and the lack of public transportation in the village.
On 25 January 2021, people protested in Sofia, demanding the resignations of the government cabinet and Prosecutor General Geshev.

On 17 February 2021, people protested in Sofia, demanding the resignation of the government cabinet and Prosecutor General Geshev due to alleged corruption. Separately, people protested outside the municipality building in Sofia, demanding the resignation of Mayor Fandukova over the recent electrical accident in which a 16 year old died.
On 17 March 2021, people from various art and culture organizations protested in Lovech against the coronavirus measures, demanding the lifting of the ban that prevents them from working.

On 13 August 2021, about 300 employees of the 'Motorways - Black Sea' stood in the road and blocked the road junction of the Hemus Motorway near Belokopitovo village, Bulgaria protesting over unpaid salaries for road construction.
On 22 October 2021, supporters of the nuclear power plant protested in Belene demanding its construction be completed soon in light of rising energy prices.
On 23 October 2021, residents of Sofia protested against coronavirus measures and the mandatory vaccination certificates, demanding the resignation of the minister of health.

On 4 November 2021, the family and friends of two men who lost their lives in a traffic accident protested in front of the court in Plovdiv, claiming the survivors of the crash lied about the circumstances of the crash and demanding a fair trial.
On 1 November 2021, parents and schoolteachers protested in Veliko Tarnovo against the requirement that children undergo regular coronavirus tests in order to resume in-person classes.
On 25 November 2021, protesters gathered in front of the ministry of health in Sofia demanding a return to normal life and for coronavirus measures, such as the vaccination certificates, be lifted.
On 7 December 2021, protesters gathered in front of the Special Court and Prosecution in Sofia demanding the resignation of the main judge in the case against a Bulgarian bank.
On 15 December 2021, the residents of Burgas protested against the construction of a crematorium in their city, claiming that it would pollute the air and the water.

On 7 February 2022, residents of the village of Belashtitsa protested and blocked the main road, detaining more than 20 trucks loaded with ore. The protests are against the extension of the concession for the stone quarry in their area, which they claim is a big source of pollution.
On 10 March 2022, employees of the interior ministry including policemen protested in Yambol demanding a reform of their sector and higher wages in accordance with their workload.

On 19 March 2022, members of the Boec civic organization protested in Sofia in support of Bulgaria's role in NATO and in support of Ukraine in the ongoing war, as a response to those protesting against Bulgaria's involvement ahead of a visit by US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin in order to strengthen NATO's presence in the country.

On 31 March 2022, doctors protested in front of the Queen Joanna Hospital in Sofia, citing the low salaries of health workers and concerns that after the end of the epidemic situation in the country from April 1, they will be left without additional remuneration for work on the first line.

On 7 April 2022, protesters gathered in front of the municipality building in Sofia to protest against renaming the streets next to the Russian embassy to 'Heroes of Ukraine' and 'Boris Nemtsov,' and insisted that Bulgaria remain neutral in the conflict.

On 17 May 2022, protesters gathered in front of the government building in Sofia demanding the resignation of the government, while a meeting was underway to discuss anti-inflationary measures. The sharp rise in prices across all sectors has caused wide discontent in the country.

On 20 June 2022, protesters gathered in front of the water department in Kardzhali to protest against the 10-day water cuts in their area. The cuts are apparently due to a leak the local authorities cannot localize.
On 5 August 2022, residents of Razgrad protested against the high prices for water and plumbing services in their area, as prices for utilities continue to rise all over Bulgaria.

On 10 August 2022, protesters organized by IMRO-BNM gathered in Sofia to object to the return to gas supplies coming from Gazprom. President Rumen Radev has urged for closer ties to Russia and a reversal of Bulgaria's support for Ukraine since the war started, which a segment of the population vehemently opposes.

On 14 September 2022, grain producers and farmers protested in Dobrich demanding that the import of Ukrainian grain be properly regulated by the government, since its lower prices undercut the grain being produced locally in Bulgaria. A recent deal between western powers and Russia allowing for the export of Ukrainian grain from Black Sea ports has disrupted grain prices for local producers in Central and Southeastern Europe since the prices are significantly lower than for the grain produced in the rest of Europe due to gas and oil prices pushing up the costs.

On 14 September 2022, grain producers and farmers protested in Karnobat demanding that the import of Ukrainian grain be properly regulated by the government, since its lower prices undercut the grain being produced locally in Bulgaria. A recent deal between western powers and Russia allowing for the export of Ukrainian grain from Black Sea ports has disrupted grain prices for local producers in Central and Southeastern Europe since the prices are significantly lower than for the grain produced in the rest of Europe due to gas and oil prices pushing up the costs.
On Nov. 11, 2018: Citizens in vehicles blocked a road in Sopot linking Sofia and Burgas to protest against the high fuel prices.

On 18 October 2022, health workers protested in Plovdiv, demanding that higher bonuses and wage increases that had been promised to them be paid out. Protests were organized in several cities and towns around the country.

On 27 November 2022, residents of Kazichene protested on the main road in the area against what they claim is the 'death road.' They demand more pedestrian crossings be incorporated to bring down the number of deaths caused by car accidents.

On 19 December 2022, protesters gathered in front of the municipality in Plovdiv demanding that the mayor and his administration resign due to his handling of development projects and permits in the city.

On 20 December 2022, residents of Velingrad protested against granting their local park embankment being to a concession, which would mean non-local investors would decide the fate of the Kleptuza landmark.

On 8 January 2023, residents of Plovdiv protested against a businessman being granted significant shares in the Plovdiv International Fair, which is an important platform for local businesses to promote their work and products.

On 13 January 2023, residents of the village of Buzovgrad and settlements in the municipality of Kazanlak protested against the decision of the supervising prosecutor from the District Prosecutor's Office in Stara Zagora to release a 57-year-old man, responsible for the serious road accident on November in which a 14-year-old boy died, on bail.

On 2 February 2023, hundreds of fans of the Botev football club protested in Plovdiv to express their dissatisfaction with the delay and uncertainty surrounding the construction of the Hristo Botev stadium.

On 19 March 2023, residents of several villages in the Trilistnik area protested demanding that the riverbed of the local Stryama river be reinforced, and for it to be cleaned up. They have been demanding the river be cleaned up and its embankment be reinforced by local authorities since last year.

On 26 April 2023, employees of the state archive protested in Sofia demanding higher salaries starting from July. The protesters claim their salaries are 'shamefully' low for the specialized work that they do.

On 2 May 2023, prosecutors, investigators, and court officials protested in Smolyan following the assassination attempt on the chief prosecutor. Law enforcers and judiciary employees from the entire country were protesting against what they perceived as an attack on their entire sector.

On 25 May 2023, employees of the National Insurance Institute protested in Plovdiv demanding larger salaries. They insist that their job is an important part of providing services for the country and that they should be recognized for it.

On 22 May 2023, residents of Sofia protested against the increase of deaths caused by traffic accidents and demanded harsher sentences for the perpetrators. Protests were held nationwide, under the motto 'Stop Bulgaria's Children from Dying.'

On 31 July 2023, protesters gathered in Burgas to demand more police oversight and judicial accountability for perpetrators of domestic and partner violence after an 18-year-old girl barely survived an knife attack from her boyfriend, who cut her several times. While the incident took place in June, details of the attack have only recently been made public, and launched protests across all of Bulgaria.

On 7 September 2023, residents of a Sofia neighborhood protested against a green area and part of a road in front of their residential building being bought and given to local developers for further construction. They claim the area is right on the path they cross every day and that they were not consulted and saw excavators appear overnight.

On 9 September 2023, protesters gathered in front of the Soviet Memorial in Sofia voice their support for the monument to stay standing. This comes during a period of deep polarization in Bulgaria, with part of the country being strongly in support of Ukraine while the other side insisting that it is in Bulgaria's best interest to not get involved in the ongoing invasion of Ukraine.

On 18 September 2023, Bulgarian farmers gathered in Trud to protest against Ukrainian grain imports being allowed in their country. Protests were held all across the country, as grain producers accuse both their country and Brussels of not defending their interests.

On 24 November 2023, citizens organized around the Boec civil society organization protested in Sofia in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs demanding that police violence against protesters be taken seriously. Last week, a protest by football fans turned violent and several protesters had to be hospitalized due to perceived police brutality.

On 6 December 2023, protesters gathered in Plovdiv to demand a bigger budget for cultural institutions that would ensure stability and fair wages. Protests were held in several locations in Bulgaria, with both cultural workers and their supporters taking place.

On 27 December 2023, protesters gathered in front of the Bulgarian National Radio (BNR) in Sofia to honor recently deceased photographer Cvetan Tomchev, who fought to try and keep the BNR away from pro-Russian influences in its programming. The protesters directed their demands particularly at a presenter whose programs have promoted pro-Kremlin talking points over the years.
On 26 November 2018, hundreds of citizens protested against gender-based violence at Eagles Bridge in Sofia and demanded preventive measures against domestic violence.

On 7 February 2024, farmers and agricultural workers gathered in Pernik to protest against what they claim are unfair EU policies toward farmers, livestock breeders and grain producers, especially with regard to grain import policies toward Ukraine which they claim is undercutting their profits. Protests were held in around 80 locations all over Bulgaria.
On 28 November 2018, Around 300 pensioners protested in front of the National Assembly in Sofia demanding a bigger increase in their pensions than planned by the government.

On 5 March 2024, protesters gathered in Yambol to protest what they claim is the unacceptable condition of the road in their area. They say they pay taxes, vignettes and other fund that should be used to maintain the road yet despite this the potholes and bad state of the road continues to be a safety risk for the region.

On 18 March 2024, residents of Dobrich protested in front of the courthouse demanding that the recent murder of an elderly man in a local park is not being investigated and tried properly. They also demand local police treat cases of violence more seriously.

On 27 March 2024, employees of the Automobile Administration Agency protested in Pernik demanding more road and transport safety measures be implemented by the government, as well as a 30 percent salary increase and more road monitors to be hired. Protests are taking place in several locations across Bulgaria.

On 3 August 2024, residents of Hadjidimitrovo protested due to the continuous lack of water supply in the area and demand that authorities remedy this issue, particularly as the wider Balkan peninsula faces a heatwave and some of the highest summer temperatures registered in modern history.

On 30 August 2024, supporters of a Bulgarian oligarch and honorary president of the Movement for Rights and Freedoms gathered in front one of his properties in Sofia as the Bulgarian prosecution considers the possibility of stripping him of some of his land and acquisitions. Protesters have been camping in front of the properties and even tried to stop police from entering and inspecting the lot.

On 4 September 2024, dozens of protesters gathered in Plovdiv to draw attention to the large number of fatal traffic accidents across the country, demanding that authorities take the issue more seriously and penalize those responsible for them.

On 12 October 2024, residents of the villages of Rogosh protested because of the delay in the construction of the new road overpass in the area, claiming that the high volume of traffic is preventing them from having access to basic services such as pharmacies and healthcare institutions.

On 16 January 2025, workers and employees of the 'Khan Krum' military equipment production plant in Targovishte held a protest at the enterprise's gate, demanding the payment of their salaries for November and December 2024 and ensuring employment at the enterprise for the rest of the year.

On 2 April 2025, protests against violence against children and paedophilia took place in Veliko Tarnovo, provoked by the widespread discontent in the country over what they claim are the increasing cases of child abuse after five men were arrested for sexually exploiting children between the ages of two months and 14 years online.
On Mar. 1, 2019: Nurses and other health workers protested in front of the state hospital in Yambol demanding increase in their salaries and better work conditions.
On Feb. 9, 2018: Citizens protested in Sofia against the construction of a building in the neighborhood Krasno selo, which was not announced to the people living in the vicinity.

On 12 April 2025, protesters gathered in Troyan as well as all across the country in a nation-wide protest against careless driving, unsafe roads and lack of harsher punishment and oversight of reckless drivers. This comes as another young girl was killed during a traffic accident, launching a Bulgaria-wide response and calls for definitive action.

On 14 April 2025, public transport workers protested in Sofia demanding higher salaries, claiming that no matter how many promises they get the general conditions of their employment do not get better year after year.

On 19 May 2025, the relatives and friends of those killed in a serious accident on the Pleven-Lovech road protested in front of the courthouse in Veliko Tarnovo. They insisted that the person responsible for the accident receive the maximum sentence - life imprisonment. Fatal traffic accidents continue to be common in the country and constant cause for protest.

On 21 May 2025, parents protested in Sofia due to their children not being accepted in state and municipal nurseries and kindergartens, and due to the fact that the compensations for not having their child in a daycare facility that they are entitled to by law have not been paid for months.

On 26 June 2025, the Parents for a Shared Childhood movement protested in front of the GERB party headquarters in Sofia demanding amendments to the law on shared parenting that would carry heavier punishments for when the mother violates the rights of the father and demand a minimum time be set by the courts for child-sharing. Protests by those who want fathers to be allowed to have a greater role in a child's life have been taking place regularly over the past year.

On 5 July 2025, hundreds of cars, part of a motorcade protest organized by the Revival party, circled through Yambol in protest calling for the government's resignation over cost-of-living increases and NATO's Ukraine policy. The protesters sought snap elections and the scrapping of military aid to Kyiv.

On 11 September 2025, protests were held in Ruse called for the resignation of the interior minister and justice in the case of the beaten Ruse police chief. Civic activists from BOEC and local supporters joined, pressing for political responsibility and transparent, impartial court proceedings.

On 21 September 2025, protesters formed convoys and blockades on key roads including the Sofia-Varna route near Pleven to highlight a deepening water crisis. Led by a local activist, the groups demanded urgent replacement of aging pipelines and repairs to the 'Telish,' 'Gorni Dabnik,' and 'Dolni Dabnik' facilities as well as the Sopot dam.

On 26 September 2025, a protest outside the headquarters of the DPS-New Beginning party in Sofia ended with demonstrators throwing eggs and small firecrackers at the building. Organized by the civic movement BOEC, participants denounced what they call oligarchic influence linked to Delyan Peevski and demanded a Bulgaria free from mafia-style corruption.

On 8 December 2025, protesters gathered at the Apriltsi Memorial Complex in Panagyurishte demanding the government's resignation. The civic protest included chants of 'Resignation' and a torch-light ritual symbolizing solidarity and peaceful civic expression.

On 9 December 2025, pro-government protesters gathered in Provadiya to oppose the resignation of the government as demanded by opposition parties in the country. The motto of the protests was 'Love not hate,' 'Respect, do not divide,' and 'We want security and stability.'

On 9 December 2025, pro-government protesters gathered in Sarnitsa to oppose the resignation of the government as demanded by opposition parties in the country. The motto of the protests was 'Love not hate,' 'Respect, do not divide,' and 'We want security and stability.'

On 6 February 2026, relatives, colleagues and citizens protested in front of the district court in Sandanski in support of a truck driver involved in a fatal crash near Telish. Protesters demanded an objective investigation and accountability for road infrastructure conditions.

On 4 March 2026, a protest demanding the resignation of Bulgarian wrestling federation president took place in front of the Ministry of Youth and Sports in Sofia. Participants gathered outside the ministry calling for her removal from the leadership of the federation.
On 15 July 2019, residents of Elin Pelin blocked a road in their town protesting against heavy traffic and lack of water supply.
On 6 August 2019, pig owners blocked the Yambol-Sliven road in protest against the government's decision to slaughter their pigs due to a swine fever epidemic.
On 7 September 2019, parents held a protest in front of the municipality in Burgas against the New Strategy of the Child over its lack of consideration for family values.

On 5 December 2019, doctors and health workers of Aleksandrovska Hospital held a protest in Sofia against the delay in signing of a collective agreement and the poor condition of their hospital building.
On 26 January 2020, residents held a protest in Botevgrad in support of their former Mayor, after Court decided to remove him over conflict of interest, saying that the trial was not based on facts.
On 21 May 2020, tens of residents held a protest in Haskovo against tree cutting and construction plans in the Yamacha park.

On 7 July 2020, over 50 citizens, organized by the coalition 'For the Nature,' took to the streets of Burgas to protest against over-construction on the Black Sea coast and amendments to the Biodiversity Act, which will harm protected zones, delay protective measures, and introduce commercial construction work to those areas.

On 7 July 2020, citizens, organized by the coalition 'For the Nature,' took to the streets of Razgrad to protest against over-construction on the Black Sea coast and amendments to the Biodiversity Act, which will harm protected zones, delay protective measures, and introduce commercial construction work to those areas.

On 30 May 2018, 2018 in Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina, fans of the Borac soccer club held a protest walk over the club's failure to receive the licence to compete in the Bosnian Premier League because of debt.
On 11 November 2023, residents of local villages protested in Gorazde, demanding that the city authorities resolve their issue with water scarcity.

On 1 September 2025, truck drivers blocked a road in Ormanica in Gradacac. This action was part of a nationwide blockade of roads and customs terminals, which disrupted major transport routes and supply chains. They protested unfulfilled government promises on licensing reforms, protection of professional drivers' rights, unlawful detentions, financial losses, lack of digitalization, bilateral transport disputes, and inspection coordination.

On 5 January 2026, over 200 dairy farmers held peaceful tractor drives across eight municipalities in Republika Srpska (coded to Banja Luka, Grad Banja Luka) to protest the crisis in the dairy sector and lack of response from authorities. There were no traffic blockades; the farmers sought dialogue with officials at all levels of government.

On 6 February 2026, citizens and associations of war victims protested against the alleged obstruction of war crimes cases within the State Prosecutor's Office, in Kljuc near Sanski Most. The protest was triggered by a public rift between a Bosniak prosecutor and the Serb Chief Prosecutor, whom protesters accuse of intentionally blocking indictments related to crimes against Bosniaks in the Sana River Valley to protect suspects. Protesters demanded the resignation of the Chief Prosecutor, citing ethnic bias and systemic obstruction of justice.

On 6 March 2026, about 100 young people gathered for a protest march from the Canton Government building to Bascarsija in Sarajevo-Stari Grad. Protesters demanded the Cantonal Government's resignation, an independent international investigation into the recent fatal tram accident, and a complete overhaul of the GRAS public transport company to ensure safety and end political appointments.

On 28 April 2026, activists from the Atelier for Community Transformation (ACT) organized a protest performance in front of the Federation Government building in Sarajevo (Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina) to highlight the 17-year absence of a valid Law on Forests, following a 2009 Constitutional Court ruling that struck down previous legislation. Activists denounced the lack of a legislative framework to protect the country's forests and criticized political parties for failing to prioritize the issue.
On 7 September 2018, 2018 in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina parents of the children with developmental difficulties protested over the problems with education of their children.
On 10 September 2018, 2018 in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina workers in education protested asking for higher salaries.
On 21 September 2018, 2018 in Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina citizens protested the unresolved death of a youngster David Dragicevic, pointing at the flaws in the judicial system of the country.
On 14 February 2019, in Gorazde, Bosnia and Herzegovina citizens organized a dance performance as a part of the 'One Billion Rising' campaign in order to protest violence against women and girls.

On 18 July 2019, about 100 citizens protested in Uborak, near Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina, demanding the federal government not to renew the permit for a waste site because, according to protesters, the site is at its full capacity.
On 11 December 2019, a protest was held in the centre of Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina, in order to draw attention to the fact that the local landfill does not have the necessary permits to operate.
On 23 August 2020, LGBTQI activists held a vehicular protest in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, in lieu of a Pride March, alerting to the problems their community faces.

On 18 September 2020, local residents protested in Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina, after an old cinema building was demolished. They claim new plans for the space are not in line with building regulations.
On 1 April 2021, coal miners protested in Banovici, Bosnia and Herzegovina, demanding an investigation and preservation of work places after the mine caught on fire the previous week.
On 7 July 2021, a union of state administration workers organized a protest in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, demanding a collective contract which would improve their labor rights.
On 17 November 2021, unionized miners protested in Tuzla, Bosnia and Herzegovina, demanding higher wages.

On 8 January 2022, Serbian nationalists drove around Gacko playing nationalist songs and using pyrotechnics ahead of a Bosnian Serb holiday that has been declared unconstitutional in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
On 19 March 2022, workers of the Croatian post participated in a protest strike and a rally in Mostar (Grad Mostar), demanding better working conditions and increased salaries.
On 8 March 2023, feminist and LGBT activists and citizens marched through Sarajevo on International Women's Day, denouncing patriarchal values and discrimination against women.
On 13 April 2023, doctors, medical technicians, and other workers from the Brcko Health Center marched through Brcko, demanding improved working conditions.

On 9 May 2023, persons with disabilities protested in front of the federal government in Sarajevo, voicing their dissatisfaction with their status and systemic discrimination. The protesters demanded improving the situation and urged the government to enact legislation protecting their dignity.

On 3 June 2025, pro-Palestinian activists gathered at the Eynard Palace at the university in Geneva (Geneve) to call on the university to end all diplomatic, economic, and academic ties with Israel, and to denounce what they described as a 'genocide' by the Israeli army in Gaza, on the occasion of a meeting with donors.

On 28 July 2025, activists of the Swiss branch of the Russia of the Future (Russie du Futur) gathered in front of the UN building in Geneva (Geneve) to protest against the participation of Russian officials at the Inter-Parliamentary Union assembly and to denounce the international legitimization of authoritarian regimes.

On 19 September 2025, in the afternoon, around 200 pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered in Bellinzona (Ticino) to disrupt a conference on EU relations where Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis was speaking. Protesters accused the government of failing to act against what they described as genocide in Gaza. Cassis was evacuated under boos and jeers, leaving the event about 90 minutes later than scheduled.

On 25 September 2025, in the evening, speech therapists and psychomotor educators gathered outside the town hall in Geneva (Geneve) to demand higher salaries and better recognition of their profession. Demonstrators highlighted that their fees had been frozen since 2009 and that around a quarter of their work, carried out outside patient sessions, remained unpaid.

On 15 November 2025, at the call of around 50 associations, including the Swiss Climate Alliance (Alliance Climatique Suisse), around 500 people demonstrated in Bern (Bern) to protest the lack of action by the Swiss government to curb emissions and demand more climate and social justice. The event took place during the COP30 climate conference in Belem, Brazil.

On 17 September 2020, people, including politicians, doctors and artists, demonstrated in Fribourg (Fribourg). They denounced the investments by Credit Suisse in fossil fuels, and asked a famous tennis champion, who is sponsored by the company, to commit to the climate.

On 4 January 2026, at the call of the local Labor Party, the Communist Youth of Bern, the Swiss-Cuba Association and several pro-Palestinian organizations, around 200 people spontaneously gathered in Bern (Bern) under the banner 'Hands off Venezuela,' to condemn the military intervention the Unites States carried out in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 7 March 2026, around 1,000 people, Iranian and Kurdish women and pro-Palestinian affiliates, gathered on Paradeplatz for an unauthorized demonstration in Zurich (Zurich) to protest for International Women's Day. No further demands were reported. The police forces used tear gas and rubber bullets against protesters to prevent them from breaching a police cordon. Protesters threw fireworks at the police forces and a small part of the protesters threw paint bottles at the Italian consulate. Other protesters blocked the tram traffic in the city. No injuries were reported.

On 21 March 2026, around 300 people gathered in Basel (Basel-Stadt) to demonstrate their solidarity with an asylum seeker who was assaulted by a police officer. The protest took place as the police officer was on trial for aggravated assault on the victim, and on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.
On 31 March 2021, demonstrators gathered in front of the courthouse in Lausanne. They called for justice after a police officer who killed a black man was released with a fine.
On 24 September 2021, Youth for Climate activists protested in Geneva to raise awareness of adults about the environmental and social consequences of global warming.

On 25 September 2021, at least 300 persons demonstrated in Lausanne. They denounced police repression against demonstrators during protests. The police was present but did not engaged in interactions with demonstrators.

On 18 May 2020, several demonstrators gathered in front of the Tuiliere prison in Lonay, near Morges. They protested against the detention conditions of prisoners amid the coronavirus crisis at the call of the 'Make noise for prisoners' collective.
On 15 May 2022, as part of the 'Kidical Mass' event, a group of people rode on their bikes in Thun. They asked authorities to take into account the security of children and aged bicycle users.

On 17 May 2022, members of the LBGT community interrupted a conference at Uni-Bastions Unige in Geneva. They denounced the alleged homophobic and transphobic nature of the speech given by the participants.

On 14 June 2022, at the call of feminist groups and the Swiss Labor Union, people demonstrated in Neuchatel to call for gender equality in salaries and denounce a pension reform that will increase women's retirement age.

On 14 June 2022, at the call of feminist groups and the Swiss Labor Union, between 5,000 and 10,000 people demonstrated in Bern to call for gender equality in salaries and denounce a pension reform that will increase women's retirement age.

On 9 February 2023, in the morning, around 20 people occupied a building in the Paquis neighborhood of Geneva. They denounced real estate speculation in Geneva and called for collective housing and social and cultural alternatives. Police forces dispersed the demonstration in the early afternoon, and several demonstrators, including a 'Ensemble a gauche' MP, were injured. Several people were arrested.

On 6 March 2023, at the call of Juso, around 70 people, including the president of The Green Youth, demonstrated at Bahnhofplatz in Aarau against the action of the far-right group 'Junge Tat' on 4 March 2023, as well as against fascism and racism.

On 1 May 2023, on the occasion of International Workers' Day, about 2,000 people, including feminist activists, took to the streets of Geneva, calling for wealth equality, more purchasing power amid rising costs, as well as increased salaries.

On 20 May 2023, around 100 people gathered in front of the entrance to the Oerlikon library of Zurich, on the occasion of a reading for children about gender identity, animated by drag-queen artists to support the event and LGBTQ+ rights. People gathered for a counter-protest.

On 10 June 2023, nearly 35,000 people, including members of the LGBTQ+ community, took to the streets of Geneva (Geneve) as part of a pride march to defend the right of their community and against discrimination.
On 22 November 2023, at the call of Unia, health workers gathered for flash mobs, information stands, and speeches in Olten (Solothurn) to demand better working conditions in hospitals.
On 5 March 2024, at the call of Unia, around 30 Micarna employees demonstrated in Lausanne (Vaud) to protest against the Ecublens factory's closure and the release of all employees.

On 28 September 2024, at the call of the association Solidarity Without Borders (Solidarite Sans Frontieres), around 1,000 people demonstrated in Bern (Bern) to defend the right to asylum and condemn racism towards migrants.
On 9 March 2022, on the occasion of International Women's Day on 8 March, hundreds of protesters organized by the CTP Women's Organization marched in Northern Nicosia for women's rights.

On 13 March 2022, hundreds of women of Cyprus protested in Larnaca with their children against Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The protesters called for the passing of an EU law on the special status of refugees of Ukraine in Cyprus, as well as the safety of the Ukrainian sky. This was part of a protest in all Cyprus cities organized by 'Women of the World to protect the sky of Ukraine'.

On 9 April 2022, residents of Dipkarpaz, Turkish Cypriots, including the mayor and members of the municipality council, rallied at the entrance of the village carrying banners and flags to protest against the government's proposed municipality reforms in Northern Cyprus, which would mean the closure and merging of their municipality. The protesters briefly blocked the road.

On 9 April 2022, the parents and relatives of female military non-commanding officers rallied outside the Presidential Palace in Nicosia to protest over the discrimination of women officers with regard to their promotion compared to their male colleagues and demanded that women officers be promoted and that they receive the additional income retroactively.

On 10 June 2022, the Cyprus Journalists Turkish Union, which had started a campaign on social media with the slogan 'Freedom is greater than you, Do Not Touch!', unfurled banners with the same slogan at the junction near the Prime Minister's office in Northern Nicosia to protest for a second day against 3 draft laws urgently brought to parliament for discussion on 6 June. The demonstrators protested against the proposed amendments for restricting fundamental rights and freedoms of Turkish Cypriots and aiming at preventing individuals and institutions, including social media, from expressing their free thought.

On 6 July 2022, potato farmers lined up their tractors and held banners to protest over the high cost of fertilizer and fuel ahead of a presidential visit in Xylofagou. The President met with the farmers and promised support.

On 13 October 2022, members of the Turkish Cypriot Electricity Authority Employees' Union (EL-SEN) rallied outside the Turkish Cypriot Electricity Authority (KIB-TEK) in Northern Nicosia during a strike-protest over chronic problems of the power company.

On 20 October 2022, Turkish Cypriot school janitors supported by their union set-up tents outside parliament in Northern Nicosia during an indefinite strike-protest demanding their unpaid wages for 50 days and to sign a collective bargaining agreement.

On 24 November 2022, members of the union Isotita, including staff of AHK (EAC), the electricity authority of Cyprus, and contractual staff on open-ended contracts in the wider public sector, as well as the independent union of technical and labour staff (Astepaik) rallied outside offices of the electricity authority (AHK) in Limassol district over their wages among other issues.

On 20 March 2023, dozens of members of the Kurdish cultural center Theophilos rallied outside the Justice Ministry in Nicosia carrying placards to protest the ongoing trial of Kurdish politician Kenan Ayaz, a recognized refugee in Cyprus, following his arrest on accusations of international terrorism for being a member of PKK stemming from Germany. Their representatives met with the justice ministry's director general pointing out that according to the extradition treaty between Germany and Turkey, should the court approve Ayaz's extradition request to Germany, he would likely be sent from there to Turkey.

On 24 April 2019, members of the Kurdistan Cultural Centre Theophilos supported by the Cyprus Green Party, AKEL and EDEK, protested once more against the arrest of a recognised Kurdish political refugee and resident of Cyprus after Germany issued a European arrest warrant on alleged terrorism-related charges. The protesters gathered in front of the Larnaca district court holding Cyprus flags, a photograph of Kurdish leader Abdullah Ocalan and banners reading among other slogans 'Europe fulfil your democratic values'.

On 22 May 2023, Turkish Cypriot teachers, organized by KTOS and KTOEOS, rallied in Northern Nicosia amid ongoing strikes in primary schools, to protest against the reintroduction of a draft amendment law that they stated would cause more problems instead of finding solutions to the lack of infrastructure, the lack of funding for education and general chaos in schools of Northern Cyprus, including overpopulated schools and overcrowded classrooms, and a large number of foreign students not speaking the Turkish language. The protesters left a black wreath outside the Education Ministry.

On 28 October 2023, the Secular Democratic Education Struggle Movement, established by parents to draw attention to the problems experienced in education, organized a protest in Gonyeli junction in Northern Nicosia. Parents rallied carrying banners.

On 9 November 2023, Turkish Cypriot teachers, organized by KTOEOS, rallied outside parliament and the education ministry in Northern Nicosia, calling on the education minister to resign. They protested the teaching of lessons in portacabins and unsafe buildings, and a departure from secular education that came with controversial new textbooks. Trade union leaders, local government leaders and opposition politicians, including CTP, held speeches. They carried flags and placards, and a number of demonstrators also carried a corrugated iron shack on the march, representing the temporary structures which had been erected in the playgrounds of some schools after their buildings were deemed unsafe following inspections.
On 17 November 2023, KTAMS protested outside Famagusta court over understaffing in courts and other issues facing courts and prisons in Northern Cyprus. The leader of KTAMS made statements.

On 23 February 2024, the academic staff and student unions of the Cyprus University of Technology (Tepak) in Nicosia rallied in the forecourt of the university rector's building to protest budget cuts, claiming that budget cuts for public universities are intended to shrink them.
On 29 February 2024, Turkish Cypriot protesters organized by the Environment Platform rallied in Lefke to protest over the risks that beetle insects were posing to forests.

On 9 July 2024, Ukrainians and Cypriots rallied in Pafos following the 8 July Russian missile attack on Ukraine and demanded an end to the 'Russian terror'. Children were carrying a banner reading 'Help Ukraine. Save us from Russia'.

On 2 September 2024, on the occasion of World Peace Day on 1 September, Turkish Cypriots organized by Independence Road, Anonymous Youth and Baraka Cultural Center, marched in northern Nicosia for peace in Cyprus. They chanted slogans such as 'Peace is in our hands', 'Long live the brotherhood of peoples', 'No passage to Zionism, fascism, Sharia'.

On 7 September 2024, residents from villages in Limassol district rallied in the village of Agios Mamas and blocked the road for 15 minutes to protest against motorcyclists competing with each other and speeding along the road between the villages of Trimiklini and Ayia Eirini. The leaders of the communities made a joint statement.

On 11 January 2025, hunters from all over Cyprus, organized by the Movement of Cyprus Hunters, rallied outside the presidential palace in Nicosia, where they submitted a memorandum, demanding stricter measures against poaching and the strengthening of the police poaching squad. They were joined by the Association of Amateur Fishers, the 'Indignant Hunters' and 'Cyprus Hunting SOS', who also protested over the cost of issuing licenses. Their leaders held speeches.

On 2 April 2025, about 30 protesters rallied spontaneously outside the presidential palace in Nicosia against solar panel shutdowns imposed by the transmission system operator (TSO) on solar panels based at residential properties. The rally, which started after a call on social media by an independent MP, lasted for about 40 minutes. The protesters submitted their demands in writing to President Christodoulides.

On 18 August 2025, during the second week of an indefinite strike and demonstration, Turkish Cypriot employees of the Koop Bank and its subsidiaries rallied outside the cooperative companies' registrar office in Northern Nicosia protesting plans for 44 workers to be laid off and a list of austerity measures. A trade union Koop-Sen leader held a speech.

On 27 September 2025, protesters from all over Cyprus, Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot members of the LGBTQI+ community in a joint effort, participated in the bi-communal Pride March with the title 'United by Pride'. Marchers from both sides of divided Nicosia marched to the Home for Cooperation in the buffer zone.

On 29 January 2026, members of the Kurdish community in Cyprus and Greek Cypriot activists marched through central Nicosia, protesting attacks on Rojava, while parliament was voting on a resolution calling on the European Union to halt funding to the Damascus regime. The House resolution passed with a unanimous vote, noting the 'crucial role' played by the Kurds in Syria in fighting the Islamic State, and expressed concern over the recent release of thousands of Islamic State prisoners from the Al-Hol camp. The demonstrators carried flags of a unified Kurdistan and marched to the Ledra Palace checkpoint, where they delivered a resolution to United Nations representatives. They also chanted slogans against Syrian leader al-Sharaa and against Turkish President Erdogan. The leader of the PYD branch in Cyprus held a speech saying what was happening in Rojava was an attack on coexistence, democracy and the rights of women and minorities and that this was an attack on civilians. He also made particular references to Kobani. Representatives of the Cyprus Green Party and AKEL, including an AKEL MP, joined the protest.

On 1 May 2026, Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot workers and members of the trade union movement held their annual march to Ledra Palace in the Nicosia (Nicosia) buffer zone with marches beginning from either side of Cyprus' divided capital to mark May Day and call for unity, fair wages and social justice with the central message 'common struggle for a common homeland, against wars and exploitation'. The leaders of PEO, WFTU and other unions held speeches. They also protested against the US intervention in Iran. Journalists also protested for their rights.
On 1 May 2026, Cyprus workers organized by PEO rallied in Pafos (Paphos) to mark May Day calling for unity, fair wages and social justice.
On 18 November 2019, students in Nicosia marched against fascism to mark the anniversary of the 1973 Polytechnic uprising in Athens.

On 14 June 2018, a Cypriot mother and her family protested in front of the Law Office of the Republic of Cyprus to highlight the fact that after 13 years of her son's death during his military service there are no definitive findings by the police investigation into the cause of death. The mother of the soldier was holding placards with police photographs of her dead son and shouted that he was murdered and there was a cover-up.

On 15 March 2020, relatives of Turkish Cypriot prisoners demonstrated outside the Central Prison in Nicosia in solidarity with prisoners on hunger strike over being held in an overcrowded environment during the coronavirus crisis. There were some arrests of prisoners' family members, while the latter also claimed that their relatives in the prison were beaten.

On 20 February 2021, about 10,000 protesters, responding to the call of tens of organizations, marched in Nicosia against government corruption and against police violence, demanding the President's resignation. This is a follow-up to a demonstration the week before, also titled 'Os Dame' (loosely translated 'enough'), which was dispersed by police. The protesters, including families with children and Gate 9 football fans, protested holding flowers and banners, many of them in the Turkish language, demanding the island's reunification.
On 7 July 2021, employees of the Famagusta Turkish Municipality (GMB) protested over unpaid salaries.
On 2 August 2021, employees of DP World Limassol went on strike and protested spontaneously at the entrance of the Limassol port terminal, demanding the renewal of their collective contracts.

On 1 December 2021, around 300 parents demonstrating against rapid tests, vaccination of children and the government's new coronavirus measures making mask-wearing at school compulsory for children aged 6 and over rallied outside the Philoxenia conference center in Aglandja, where parliament committees meet, during a session of the House education committee that was discussing coronavirus measures in schools and recent incidents of individual violence by parents attacking teachers and staff in many schools. The protesters held banners and shouted slogans demanding the President's resignation and the abolition of the measures, while they were observed by strong police forces. They insisted for their representatives to enter parliament, but they were denied.
On 3 August 2023, activists gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against a sentence given to their fellow for spreading coronavirus-related disinformation during the pandemic.
On 19 September 2023, Greenpeace activists protested in Chomutov against illegal wood cutting.

On 8 October 2023, about 70 activists gathered with pickets at a diary production plant in Dolany (Pardubice district), protesting against alleged animal cruelty within the facility. They peacefully left the building when police ordered them to do so.
On 28 October 2023, Palestinian activists gathered for a march in Prague, protesting against violence committed by Israel against Palestinian civilians.

On 22 February 2024, farmers with their vehicles organized demonstrative rides across the Jindrichuv Hradec district. The gathering was a part of nation-wide protest against persisting problems in the agricultural sectors, including the so-called Green Deal restrictions or the ongoing imports of grain from Ukraine.
On 9 July 2020, Czech and Belarusian activists gathered in Brno, declaring their support for democratic reforms in Belarus and supporting their local counterparts.

On 20 March 2024, farmers with their machines gathered for a demonstrative ride across the Trebic district, protesting against what they see as a low state support to the national agriculture. Rallies, rides and gatherings took place at other locations across the country as well.

On 24 March 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Prague, commemorating the outbreak of the NATO bombardment of Yugoslavia and protesting against the current NATO actions, which they deem being violent and imperialistic.
On 10 August 2020, several dozen Czech and Belarusian activists gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against post-election violence in Belarus and supporting their counterparts.

On 1 September 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Prague, demanding end of all wars around the world, including the conflicts in Ukraine and Gaza, Yemen and others. They mostly blamed the US for fuelling global conflicts and supported Russian narratives.

On 10 January 2025, Czech and Slovak activists, including members of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, gathered for a rally in Prague in front of the Slovak embassy, protesting against violations of democratic principles in Slovakia. In particular they criticized the PM's recent unscheduled visit to Russia and asserted their support to Ukraine.

On 7 February 2025, several hundred Slovak activists, including student associations, gathered in Prague, protesting against the anti-western and anti-democratic behavior of the current government and the PM (Smer party) in particular.
On 11 April 2025, several dozen activists, mostly students affiliated with the FFF movement, gathered for a rally in Prague, demanding immediate climate action.
