People gathered for a counter-protest against the project.

On 20 April 2024, at the call of 'Heart instead of Hate' (Herz statt Hetze) and a cross-party alliance, around 500 people gathered in Buchen (Schleswig-Holstein), to protest for humanity and against right-wingideologies.

On 1 May 2024, on the occasion of International Workers' Day, at the call of the DGB, thousands of people gathered in Rostock (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), to protest for workers' rights and core demands such as increased wages, and improved job security. Around 50 members of the left-radical 'Red Youth' (Rote Jugend Rostock) joined the protest but were later excluded from the demonstration after chanting anti-Semitic slogans.

On 27 April 2024, under the motto 'Never again 1932' and at the call of 'Alliance Dessau Nazi-free' (Bundnis Dessau nazifrei), about 80 people, including a State Parliament member (The Left), participated in a protest in Dessau-Rosslau (Sachsen-Anhalt) against the AfD and fascism and to raise awareness for the similarities between historical and current developments.

On 4 May 2024, at the call of ADFC, over 100 cyclists, including families with children, participated in the Kidical Mass bike demonstration in Bad Segeberg (Schleswig-Holstein), to protest against the poor quality of cycling infrastructure in the city.

On 11 May 2024, under the motto 'Protest Democracy - Against Hatred, Agitation and Violence' and at the call of 2 members of the Greens, about 170 people, including a city council member (CDU), the mayor (Independent), a State Parliament member (SPD), representatives of the church and the Greens, participated in a protest in Frankenberg (Eder) (Hessen) for democracy, diversity, freedom and human rights and against right-wing tendencies and ideologies, violence and agitation.
On 11 May 2024, people participated in a historical revisionist protest at the memorial Feld des Jammers in Bretzenheim (Rheinland-Pfalz) whereby anti-Semitic conspiracy myths were used.

On 30 May 2024, under the motto 'Never again is now' and at the call of the Alliance 'Democratic Mecklenburg Vorpommern' (Demokratisches MV), 360 people, including Minister-President Manuela Schlesig (SPD), participated in a protest in Schwerin (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) for democracy and tolerance, against racism and right-wing extremism, and to call on people to vote in the upcoming elections. The protest was part of a state-wide action day for democracy and tolerance.

On 31 May 2024, at the call of FFF, about 150 people participated in a protest in Greifswald (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) for climate protection and democracy, against right-wing extremism, and to draw attention to the importance of the EU in tackling the climate crisis. The protest was organized as part of FFF's international climate strike to call for an EU-wide phase-out of coal, oil and gas by 2035, and a doubling of investments in renewable energies and climate-neutral industries.

On 1 June 2024, under the motto 'Be loud against right-wing extremism', about 10 people belonging to the left spectrum participated in a protest in Westerland (Schleswig-Holstein) against right-wing extremism, for human rights, and in favor of migration.

Around 14 June 2020, around 70 people protested in Stolberg (Rhineland) against racism and police violence under the motto 'Black Lives Matter'. The protest was sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a policer officer in the United States.

On 8 June 2024, under the motto 'Climate Protection Instead of War! Climate Protection Instead of Isolation!', around 100 people, including left-wing affiliates, pro-Palestinian groups, and climate activists, gathered in Bonn (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to criticize the EU for its perceived warmongering. The event also aimed to show support for the Palestinian population and climate action.

On 14 June 2024, environmental activists set up a protest camp and wooden platforms in the Gremberger Waldchen area of Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen), fastening themselves to tree trunks, to oppose the planned expansion of the A4 highway and denounce the potential deforestation and loss of wildlife it would entail.

On 26 June 2024, around 70 members of the 'Citizens' Solar Society' (Burger-Solar-Gesellschaft) gathered outside the town hall in Rosrath (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest against the temporary closure of the indoor swimming pool and for compensation to the elementary school Hoffnungsthal GbR for the removal of their solar system. The protesters demanded the pool remain open for children's swimming lessons and highlighted a loss of around 40,000 euros due to the solar system's removal.

On 20 July 2024, at the call of VVN-BdA, around 70 people gathered outside the Saarland Museum in Saarbrucken (Saarland), expressing solidarity with artist Candice Breitz and demanding the resignation of Saarland Culture Minister Christine Streichert-Clivot (SPD). The demonstration was in response to the cancellation of the artist's exhibition after she was reported to have made anti-Zionist comments, accusing the minister of political interference and infringement on artistic and free speech rights.

On 26 July 2024, during the evening, around 100 people, including craftspeople, business owners, and nurses, wearing yellow safety vests and carrying German flags gathered on the bridge over the B30 towards Hochstetter Hof near Mettenberg in Biberach (Baden-Wurttemberg) against the German government. They accused the media and politics of lying.

On 9 August 2024, around 150 people, including members of various antifascist organizations and local groups, participated in a counter-protest, organized by the Grannies Against the Right (Germany), in Bad Salzungen (Thuringen) against an AfD summer festival where Bjorn Hocke, chairman of the AfD parliamentary group in the Landtag of Thuringia (Thuringian state parliament), was scheduled to speak.

On 10 August 2024, around 400 people staged a protest under the Motto 'No Nayi Center in Munich' in the city district of Perlach in Munchen (Bayern), marching from Neuperlach shopping center to the Pfanzelplatz and Sebastian-Bauer-Strase, against the opening of a new constituency office for the AfD, voicing their opposition to the presence of the far-right party in their neighborhood, emphasizing the importance of resisting the normalization of far-right ideologies.

On 17 August 2024, around 21,000 gathered in Leipzig (Sachsen) on the occasion of Christopher Street Day (CSD) and to promote the LGBT community's rights. Before the demonstration, around 300 to 400 far-right and neo-Nazi protesters had gathered at the train station under the motto 'proud, German, national' with the purpose of staging a counter-protest. However, they were cordoned off by the police, who also carried out identity checks, and their march did not take place.

On 31 August 2024, at the call of the NSP, 22 people gathered in Rostock (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), while at the call of the Alliance 'Rostock nazifree' (Rostock nazifrei), around 130 people gathered for a counter-demonstration, opposing the NSP's extremist views and promoting anti-racism. 15 masked individuals attempted to disrupt the NSP rally with posters and loudly chanted slogans. When officers intervened, they were attacked by a 24-year-old. The suspect was detained. He is being investigated on suspicion of assaulting law enforcement officers. An investigation has also been initiated against three other participants, aged 19 to 34, on suspicion of violating assembly laws.

On 31 August 2024, at the call of the 'Allgau Pride Association' (Verein Allgau Pride), hundreds of people, including Grannies Against the Right, Mayor Stefan Bosse (CDU), The Greens members, gathered in Kaufbeuren (Bayern), to protest for LGBTQ+ rights on Christopher Street Day (CSD), while promoting tolerance and social unity, celebrating diversity and opposing intolerance in their community.

On 1 September 2024, around 150 people gathered in Bad Bramstedt (Schleswig-Holstein), to protest against right-wing ideologies and threats to democracy, in response to the rising influence of the AfD and recent right-wing activities in Germany.

On 31 August 2024, around 1,000 people participated in the 'Reclaim Hamburg' Demo-Rave, marching through St. Pauli in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), to protest gentrification and for the preservation of local culture. The protest, which featured music trucks and colorful banners, highlighted issues such as rising costs and the lack of support for the club scene.

On 20 September 2024, around 700 people, led by Fridays for Future, gathered in Halle (Saale) (Sachsen-Anhalt) to call for urgent climate action and urge the German government to adopt effective and socially just climate policies. This protest was part of a nationwide and global climate strike.

On 3 October 2024, around 50 people affiliated with the Citizen's Forum Against Right-wing Extremism from Esens, Grannies Against the Right, and other organizations gathered on the side of the road in Werdum (Niedersachsen) to protest against the AfD party congress of the AfD District Associations Friesland and Wittmund.

On 24 October 2024, at the call of the 'Life Assistance Dessau' (Lebenshilfe Dessau) organization, along with other disability support groups, many hundred people gathered in Magdeburg (Sachsen-Anhalt), to protest against anticipated cuts to assistance for individuals with disabilities. The protesters held signs with slogans such as 'Inclusion instead of illusion' and 'No job cuts in disability services'.

On 15 November 2024, around 50 people, including CSU Member of Parliament Alexander Dietrich and CSU City Councillor Hans Theiss, gathered in the district of Feldmoching in Munchen (Bayern), to protest against the planned construction of a refugee accommodation on a greenfield site at Schrederwiese and to oppose the project citing lack of integration opportunities, infrastructure, and environmental concerns.
On 24 June 2020, Thai activists protested outside a hotel in Garmisch-Partenkirchen against the Thai King. The King allegedly resided at the hotel at that time.

On 17 November 2024, around 400 people, including those affected and members of groups like the Council of Those Affected and the Federation of German Catholic Youth, protested at Elisenbrunnen in Aachen (Nordrhein-Westfalen). The protesters demanded moral accountability, fair reparations and justice for abuse victims in the Diocese of Aachen and criticized Bishop Helmut Dieser for dismissing cases based on legal time limits. Bishop Helmut Dieser was present at the protest.

On 23 November 2024, at the call of the group 'Hand in Hand for Our Country' (Hand in Hand fur unser Land), around 1,000 people, including farmers with around 23 tractors and numerous cars, staged a protest at the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), demanding 'speech rights' in the Bundestag. The protesters protested for energy security and agricultural policies, and expressed opposition to the SPD-FDP-Green coalition government, with demonstrators waving German and peace flags. While the demonstration initially aimed to address agricultural policies, it quickly expanded to a broad range of grievances, including opposition to the war in Ukraine, coronavirus measures, and Donald Trump. The protest was also marked by a diverse set of political views, with some speakers expressing far-right ideologies, while others focused on agricultural issues like EU trade deals.

On 6 December 2024, at the call of IGM, Bosch employees, including software experts and engineers gathered at the company's sites in the Feuerbach district in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) to protest against job cuts and reduced working hours in the research and development sector amid restructuring efforts in the automotive industry. The protest was part of a widespread warning strike by IGM against cost-cutting plans.

On 13 December 2024, around 250 people participated in a protest, organized by anarchist, autonomous, anti-fascist, and Antifa affiliates, in solidarity with Palestine and in opposition to Israel on Warschauer Strasse in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin). At the same time, a smaller counterprotest, with about 30-40 people, took place at the intersection of Warschauer Strasse and Grunberger Strasse.

On 6 January 2025, people, including CDU District Chairman and Bundestag candidate Steffen Roschek, gathered for a protest organized by the 'Vigil Bautzen' in Bautzen (Sachsen), focusing on issues such as coronavirus, energy policies, and the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

On 27 June 2020, up to 600 people protested in Mannheim under the motto 'Black Lives Matter' against racism and police violence. The protest was sparked by the death of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 31 December 2024, people gathered for a protest in front of the Ossendorf prison in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to advocate prison abolition and in solidarity with prisoners, using fireworks. This protest was part of a series of protests in Germany in solidarity with prisoners.
On 18 January 2025, around 100 wind energy opponents held a protest in Ebersberg (Bayern), criticizing various political and media policies.

On 18 January 2025, under the motto 'Solidarity with Palestine: Stop the Gaza Genocide - No weapons for Israel', around 350 people demonstrated in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin), waving Palestinian and some Lebanese flags to oppose weapons deliveries to Israel and express solidarity with Gaza. Demonstrators shouted banned slogans and threw pyrotechnics and bottles at the police. Police carried out temporary detentions for identification and one arrest for assault. Around 15 people participated in a bike rally from Gorlitzer Park to Werderscher Markt under the motto 'Never Again Applies to All - Stop the Genocide in Gaza.'

On 30 January 2025, between 400 and 2,000 people gathered in Bamberg (Bayern) to protest against Friedrich Merz's (CDU) proposed migration plan and far-right ideologies. The event was part of a wider protest movement against far-right politics in response to the CDU's migration plan, which was supported by the AfD.
On 31 January 2025, in the afternoon, over 100 people gathered in Essen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against hate and incitement and for diversity and inclusion.

On 31 January 2025, between 1,400 and 1,500 people gathered in front of the Messe Congress Center in Erfurt (Thuringen) to protest against the CDU's proposed migration policy and its cooperation with the AfD. Protesters chanted slogans such as 'Shame on you!', following the rejection of the CDU/CSU's migration bill by the Federal Parliamentt. The event was part of a wider protest movement against far-right politics in response to the CDU's migration plan, which was supported by the AfD.

On 30 January 2025, around 350 to 400 people gathered in Illertissen (Bayern) to protest against the AfD. The event was part of a wider protest movement against far-right politics in response to the CDU's migration plan, which was supported by the AfD.
On 14 February 2025, around 30 people gathered in Halle (Saale) (Sachsen-Anhalt) to participate in the global protest action 'One Billion Rising' against gender-based violence.

On 8 February 2025, in the evening, at the call of various local groups, including FFF, around 3,000 people gathered in Duisburg (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against far-right ideologies. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the elections.

On 14 February 2025, at the call of FFF, between 8,000 and 10,000 people, including members of Greenpeace, staged a protest at the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) for climate neutrality by 2035 and other climate protection measures. The event was part of a wider protest movement focused on climate protection ahead of the elections.

On 20 January 2020, between 70-80 people demonstrated against an event by an AfD politician in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), in front of the City Hall, . First it was a peaceful event, but as the activists were demanded by the police to leave, demonstrators started firing pyrotechnics.

On 8 February 2025, people gathered in Unna (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against the rise of far-right ideologies. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the elections.

On 16 February 2025, around 500 people participated in a protest for climate protection in Lindau (Bodensee) (Bayern), organized by a broad alliance of local organizations, such as Fridays for Future and Grannies Against the Right. The protest marched from Karl-Bever-Platz through the island to the Alte Rathaus, calling for climate action and the protection of democracy and equality.

On 16 February 2025, around 600 to 700 participants gathered for a protest organized by the alliance 'Colorful instead of Brown' in Traunstein (Bayern), expressing their opposition to the far-right shift in society and denouncing recent attacks in Aschaffenburg, Munich, and Karnten. The primary message was a firm stand against fascism, with the slogan 'We are the firewall - No inch to fascism!'
On 2 July 2020, around 20 activists squatted The Left office in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg to protest for the preservation of the far left housing project Liebig34.

On 15 February 2025, around 2,000 people participated in a right-wing 'Make Peace' rally, initiated by the Munchen' Querdenker' scene in Munchen (Bayern). The protesters criticized NATO and the war in Ukraine, expressing support for peace with Russia.

On 22 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of 'Harburg Against the Right' (Harburg gegen Rechts), and the Alliance 'Together Against the Right' (Einig gegen Rechts), the SPD, and left-wing affiliates, and under the motto 'Hargurg together against the right', between 950 to 1,300 people gathered in the Heimfeld district of Hamburg - Harburg (Hamburg) to participate in several demonstrations against the AfD's campaign closing event. During the event, demonstrators confronted a man who was filming them and in response, police used pepper spray against the demonstrators and arrested a dozen of them. A demonstrator also hit a police officer on the head with a cardboard sign. The event was part of a nationwide movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the 2025 federal elections.

On 24 February 2025, at around 4:30 pm, at the call of a local citizens' alliance and Grannies Against the Right, under the motto 'For Democracy - Schweringen is Colorful!', around 450 people staged a protest in Schweringen (Niedersachsen) against a meeting of the AfD district association Nienburg-Schaumburg, following the 23 February 2025 federal election results. Some participants held signs with slogans such as 'Human rights instead of right-wing people,' 'For diversity,' and 'Red card for the AfD.'

On 7 March 2025, at the call of Ver.di, around 300 public sector workers, including healthcare and daycare workers gathered in Lubeck (Schleswig-Holstein) to protest for higher wages and better working conditions. Additionally, 150 workers participated in a bicycle protest. The protest was part of a wider strike and protest movement in the public sector amid ongoing negotiations.

On 8 March 2025, at the call of the MLPD, around 1,000 people gathered in Essen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against an AfD event, which was held on International Women's Day and featured speeches including one by Parliament member Beatrix von Storch (AfD). The event aimed to challenge the far-right party's involvement in a day dedicated to women's rights, with protesters expressing their opposition to the AfD's stance on gender issues, highlighting the contrast between their support for women's rights and the party's political agenda.

On 13 March 2025, at the call of Ver.di and GEW, several thousand public service employees gathered in Saarbrucken (Saarland). They began their protests at multiple locations-including Landwehrplatz, Schlossplatz, and the Congresshalle-and then marched together to the Staatstheater for a common rally. This rally was as part of a broader strike to demand an eight percent wage increase and highlight issues like staff shortages and increased workloads amid the ongoing public service wage negotiations.

On 12 March 2025, at the call of Ver.di, 4,000 people gathered for a rally in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen), marching from the Haus des Deutschen Gewerkschaftsbundes near the Hauptbahnhof to the Burgplatz in the Altstadt. This rally was as part of a broader strike to demand an eight percent wage increase and highlight issues like staff shortages and increased workloads amid the ongoing public service wage negotiations.

On 12 March 2025, at the call of Ver.di, people, including employees from Laupheim city administration, gathered for a rally in Ulm (Baden-Wurttemberg). This rally was as part of a broader strike to demand an eight percent wage increase and highlight issues like staff shortages and increased workloads amid the ongoing public service wage negotiations.

On 8 March 2025, under the motto 'Women fight internationally against fascism, war, and capitalism', between 2,200 and 3,000 people gathered in Nurnberg (Bayern) to protest for women's choice over their body and demand an end to violence against women. This event was part of a broader mobilization on the occasion of International Women's Day.

On 18 March 2025, at the call of Ver.di, around 1,500 participants gathered at the Nordmark Sports Field (Nordmarksportfeld) in Kiel (Schleswig-Holstein) for a rally held as part of a spontaneous strike. The demonstration was organized in response to the failure of the third round of wage negotiations between the union and public employers, with protesters demanding better working conditions and fair compensation, particularly for apprentices and interns.

On 28 March 2025, in the morning, at the call of several local citizens' initiatives, around 50 people gathered outside the City Hall in Markkleeberg (Sachsen) to protest against the planned wind power site allocations discussed by the Regional Planning Association of West Saxony (RPV). Protesters criticized current legal requirements mandating the designation of two percent of state land for wind energy development, arguing this would endanger farmland and forest areas, thereby undermining the environment.

On 29 March 2025, a few people protested gathered for a protest in Munchen (Bayern) as part of the international TeslaTakeDown action day. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.
On 4 April 2025, under the motto 'Education instead of Bombs', students staged a protest in Gotha (Thuringen) against military recruitment by the German Armed Forces at their school.

On 11 April 2025, at the call of Fridays for Future, nearly 500 people took part in a bicycle protest in Freiburg im Breisgau (Baden-Wurttemberg). As part of a global action day, protesters demanded more climate protection.

On 6 April 2025, dozens of people, including business owners, staged a protest in Potsdam (Brandenburg) against the city's plans to turn the street into a pedestrian zone due to concerns over the loss of parking spaces and the potential increase in noise due to new restaurants.

On 21 April 2025, around 30 people gathered in Freising (Bayern) calling for an end to rearmament and wars, particularly in Ukraine and the Middle East. The event was part of the broader series of Easter peace marches.

On 1 May 2025, on the occasion of Labor and International Workers' Day, at the call of the DGB, around 80 people staged a protest in Bad Hersfeld (Hessen) demanding fair wages, solidarity, and opposition to far-right ideologies.

On 5 May 2025, around 47 teachers and students at Werner-Heisenberg School staged a protest in Riesa (Sachsen) opposing the education reform plans proposed by the Ministry of Education, voicing concerns about increased workload and decreasing motivation due to the proposed changes.

On 11 May 2025, people gathered in Braunschweig (Niedersachsen) as part of a nationwide day of protest, demanding the initiation of a ban procedure against the AfD. The protest was part of a nationwide day of action demanding a ban on the AfD, following the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution's decision to classify the party as a 'confirmed right-wing extremist'.

On 11 May 2025, around 350 participants gathered at the Marktplatz in Lubeck (Schleswig-Holstein) to protest against the far-right ideolgy and activity and to advocate for an AfD ban. The protest was part of a nationwide day of action demanding a ban on the AfD, following the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution's decision to classify the party as a 'confirmed right-wing extremist'.

On 11 May 2025, at the call of the Network Together Against the Right (Netzwerk Zusammen gegen Rechts) and the Initiative Protest Human Dignity - AfD-ban jetzt (Initiative Menschenwurde verteidigen - AfD-Verbot jetzt), around 150 people gathered for a protest on the Market Square in Bremen (Bremen), demanding that the federal government immediately initiate a ban procedure against the AfD. The protest was part of a nationwide day of action demanding a ban on the AfD, following the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution's decision to classify the party as a 'confirmed right-wing extremist'.
On 8 July 2020, employees of Airbus protested in Nordenham against planned job cuts due to the coronavirus pandemic. The protest was organised by IGM.
On 9 July 2020, medical assistants protested in Munchen for more appreciation and equal treatment of medical assistants and nurses.

On 6 June 2025, people gathered for a bicycle protest in Halle (Saale) (Sachsen-Anhalt) under the motto 'World Bicycle Day, mobility transition, transport infrastructure,' concluding at the August-Bebel Square after a 13-kilometer ride through the city.

On 31 May 2025, at the call of Queer Pride Dresden, over 10,000 people marched through Dresden (Sachsen) to advocate LGBTQ+ rights. A far-right counter-protest with between 120 to 150 people, including members of JN and the Elblandrevolte was temporarily halted by police due to criminal offenses, including the use of unconstitutional symbols and hate speech. Protesters also blocked the far-right march.

On 31 May 2025, in the morning, at the call of the Network Against the Right (Netzwerk gegen Rechts), supported by parties and unions including The Greens, SPD, The Left, Ver.di and IGM, under the motto 'Disrupt the AfD - for a united Heilbronn', between 500 and 700 people staged a protest in Heilbronn (Baden-Wurttemberg) against the AfD state party congress and far-right politics.

On 11 June 2025, under the motto 'Stop the contract!', midwives staged a protest in Weimar (Thuringen) during the Health Ministers' Conference, opposing a new contract they fear will worsen their working conditions.

On 17 June 2025, around 200 ThyssenKrupp Hohenlimburg workers, alongside MLPD members, protested in Hohenlimburg (Nordrhein-Westfalen) ahead of a company assembly to oppose the ThyssenKrupp board's plans to break up the company and cut thousands of jobs. Protesters denounced the expected renewal of the CEO's contract and called for stronger resistance to the restructuring plans.

On 27 June 2025, at the call of IGM, employees staged a protest rally in front of the Bosch research campus in Renningen (Baden-Wurttemberg) to oppose the company's decision to eliminate anniversary bonuses and special leaves starting next year.

On 28 June 2025, at around 1 pm, under the motto 'Schleswig goes more colorful', people gathered for the Christopher Street Day parade in Schleswig (Schleswig-Holstein) to promote and defend LGBTQ+ rights and visibility.

On 25 July 2025, activists set up a protest camp in Oldenburg (Niedersachsen) to oppose the construction of a relief road through the Heidbrook area, a protected natural habitat home to endangered amphibians.

On 20 July 2025, in the morning, at the call of the Grannies Against the Right, several hundred people gathered in front of the parliament building in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) demanding that the rainbow flag be shown at the Parliament during the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade as well as LGBTQ+ rights, and defending democracy against recent restrictions imposed by Parliament leadership on flying the flag.

On 26 July 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of Animal Rebellion and Vegan connected (Vegan vernetzt), between 120 and 300 people staged a protest in Nurnberg (Bayern) against the planned killing of Guinea baboons in the local zoo due to overcrowding, calling for an end to baboon breeding and for surplus animals to be relocated to a sanctuary in Wales.
On 31 July 2025, over 100 people, including medical staff, staged a protest in Wittstock/Dosse (Brandenburg) against the planned closure of the local KMG clinic.

On 10 August 2025, about 20 citizens and members of Jewish groups marched near the Aussenalster lake in Hamburg - Hamburg-Nord (Hamburg) with banners reading 'Free the hostages' and Israeli flags to demand the release of Israeli hostages held captive by Hamas. The protest, part of the global 'Run for Their Lives' initiative, was held under police protection. While most passersby expressed support, some individuals shouted 'child murderers' at participants.

On 13 August 2025, several dozen people from the International Youth (Internationale Jugend), the Communist Youth Association (Kommunistischer Jugendverband), Women's Revolution (Frauenrevolution), MLPD and VVN-BdA, staged a protest in front of the Central Station in Wuppertal (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against the ban on the planned 'Disarm Rheinmetall' protest camp in Koln at the end of August 2025, with participants criticizing the police's justification that the camp would be 'unpeaceful' and condemning the criminalization of antimilitarist slogans like 'War on War'.

On 20 August 2025, 160 residents and feminist activists gathered in a park in the Reudnitz district of Leipzig (Sachsen) to protest a femicide in which a 37-year-old man killed his former partner and seriously injured their 10-year-old son. Demonstrators also condemned femicides more broadly. The protest was held near the crime scene.

On 20 September 2025, at the call of FFF, between 80 (police) and 300-400 (organizers) people, including citizens and environmental activists, gathered in front of the Uberseemuseum in Bremen (Niedersachsen) under the motto 'Exit Gas, Enter Future' as part of the Global Climate Action Day. Demonstrators opposed the federal government's gas infrastructure plans, demanded an immediate exit from fossil fuels, and called for investments in renewable energy, transport, and heating alternatives.

On 27 September 2025, at the call of an alliance of around 50 organizations, including REBELL, Medico International, AI, The Left, DKP, MLPD, migrant and leftist small groups such as the Israeli peace movement Standing Together, the Labour Party of Turkey (Arbeiterpartei der Turkei), VVN-BdA and pro-Palestinian organizations, under the motto 'All Eyes of Gaza', between 60,000 and more than 120,000 people, including Co-President of The Left and MP Ines Schwerdtner, was as Israeli and Palestinian nationals, staged a protest marching from the Red town hall to Tiergarten in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) against the Israeli war in Gaza, chanting 'Free, free Palestine', while calling for an end to German arms exports to Israel, the provision of humanitarian goods to Gaza, and EU sanctions on Israel. At the same time, at Lust Garden, a small counter-protest took place, featuring Israeli flags. Protesters then chanted slogans like 'Fuck Israel'.

On 28 September 2025, members of the Malagasy diaspora gathered in Munchen (Bayern) to express solidarity with the protest movement led by the 'Gen Z' in Madagascar against recurring power and water cuts and demand the resignation of President Andry Rajoelina.
On 6 November 2025, in the evening, people staged a protest in Grossefehn (Niedersachsen) against the planned construction of an industrial chicken farm.

On 14 November 2025, at the call of FFF, around 3,000 people staged a protest in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen) demanding stronger government action on climate change, criticizing continued support for fossil fuels. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement linked to the COP30 climate summit in Belem, Brazil, highlighting frustration with the EU for weakening its 2040 climate goals.

On 11 November 2025, at around 5:30 pm, at the call of Democrateam (Demokrateam) and the Bonn Alliance Against the Right, under the motto 'Carnival free of fascists', between 60 and 70 people staged a protest in front of the student Fraternity of the Raczeks in Bonn (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against a lecture by an AfD member, who had been invited to speak about his involvement in Ukraine, denouncing giving a platform to far-right figures.

On 17 November 2025, in the evening, around 25 people staged a protest in front of the house Greiffenhorst in Krefeld (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against an AfD citizens' dialogue event, criticizing the party's use of a municipally owned venue.

On 7 January 2025, at the call of CGT, around 30 striking Bio 17 employees gathered for a picket line outside their workplace in Lagord (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand better working conditions and protest against the reorganization of their work schedule.

On 26 December 2024, at the call of the Climbers' Collective of Aquitaine (Collectif des Grimpeurs et Grimpeuses d'Aquitaine), Attac, XR, SLT, the Stop THT Collective (Collectif Stop THT), and around 40 other unspecified organizations and businesses, six climate activists climbed up trees outside the town hall and set up camp on the branches in Capbreton (Nouvelle-Aquitaine), where they spent the night, to protest against the construction of a high-voltage line between Spain and France, citing environmental concerns, particularly regarding biodiversity and the destruction of local ecosystems.

On 24 December 2024, around 10 affiliates of the environmental collective Basins No Thank You gathered outside the Court of Justice in Niort (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to support a fellow activist on trial on charges of injuring a police officer and assaulting farmers during a protest on 18 December 2024. The demonstrators argued that the charges were baseless and demanded the closure of all agricultural mega-basins, citing their detrimental impact on local biodiversity.

On 14 December 2024, at the call of COLBAC - Biterrois Liaison Committee for the Abolition of Corrida (Comite de Liaison Biterrois pour l'Abolition de la Corrida), people gathered in Beziers (Occitanie) to demand a ban on Spanish-style bull-fighting (corrida), which they deemed cruel to bulls. The protest followed International Animal Rights Day on 10 December.

On 13 January 2025, at the call of CP, four farmers gathered in Saint-Antoine-de-Breuilh (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) and blocked access to excavators at an archaeological dig site to protest against the destruction of a wheat crop planted by a farmer who claimed to have received verbal permission to cultivate the land. The protesters denounced the artificialization of soil and accused local authorities of mismanaging the land's use.

On 15 January 2025, around 50 striking healthcare workers gathered in front of the hospital's main entrance in Auch (Occitanie) to demonstrate against staff shortages, excessive workloads, and poor working conditions.

On 13 January 2025, students, Senator Remi Cardon (PS), and National Deputy Francois Ruffin (LFI/NFP) gathered in Amiens (Hauts-de-France) to demand that all schools in Amiens be adequately heated during wintertime. The protest, held outside the Cite scolaire complex, was prompted by ongoing heating issues affecting classrooms and dormitories, with students claiming to endure temperatures as low as 6C.

On 22 January 2025, about 30 CP members protested outside the Agricultural Chamber in Mende (Occitanie), by constructing a symbolic wall of beehives across the entrance. This action was meant to criticize the perceived closed nature of the chamber and a voting system they argued was dominated by the FDSEA and JA, claiming they controlled local agricultural representation. The protest highlighted ongoing tensions within the agricultural community over political representation and influence in the region.

On 19 January 2025, around 60 members of the Catholic community gathered in Bourg-en-Bresse (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the legalization of abortion and assisted suicide, which was proposed by the previous government in France. The protest took place on the 50-year anniversary of the legalization of abortion in France. Participants, primarily from the Marlieux parish and Saint-Jean Bosco school, marched from the Sacred Heart Church to the Church of Our Lady of the Annunciation.

On 18 January 2025, at the call of AFPS, around 40 people gathered outside the town hall in Saint-Quentin (Hauts-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn Israeli airstrikes on Gaza, and demand that the ceasefire between Hamas and Israel be upheld by both parties. Protesters voiced concerns about the sustainability of the truce and called for increased humanitarian aid to Palestine.

On 29 January 2025, at the call of CGT and #MeTooTheatre, around 80 people, mostly women, gathered outside the French Comedy (Comedie Francaise) in Paris (Ile-de-France) to condemn the institution's slow reaction to rape allegations against the actor Nazim Boudjenah, who was convicted for rape in 2021 but only recently sanctioned by the French Comedy after sending out death threats to national deputy Sandrine Rousseau.

On 31 January 2025, at the call of SNAPE-FO, employees of the French Office of Biodiversity (OFB) gathered outside the Prefecture in Clermont-Ferrand (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of French Office of Biodiversity (OFB) workers demanding more support from authorities after farmers threatened to attack OFB workers who would inspect farms and Prime Minister Francois Bayrou dismissed the OFB's work as a 'humiliation for farmers'.

On 28 January 2025, at the call of LAB and other organizations, several hundred people, including migrants, gathered outside the Court of Justice in Bayonne (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to express solidarity with 7 people who were on trial for illegally helping migrants cross the Spanish-French border during the Korrika race in March 2024. The protesters demanded more solidarity for migrants and condemned what they perceived as an unfair trial.

On 7 February 2025, in the morning, striking Lidl workers gathered outside their workplace in Carignan (Grand Est) to demonstrate. The event was part of a national day of strike and demonstration called by CGT, CFDT, FO, CFE-CGC, and CFTC to denounce poor working conditions, low staffing levels, and management's plan to open all stores every Sunday starting from 1 June 2025.

On 7 February 2025, striking Lidl workers gathered in Saint-Etienne (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demonstrate. The event was part of a national day of strike and demonstration called by CGT, CFDT, FO, CFE-CGC, and CFTC to denounce poor working conditions, low staffing levels, and management's plan to open all stores every Sunday starting from 1 June 2025.
On 21 October 2020, members of Aiutu Paisanu demonstrated in Corte in support of political prisoners and their families.

On 1 February 2025, at the call of CGT and the local Hospital Defense Committees (Comite de Defense de l'Hopital), between 350 and 400 people, including health workers, demonstrated in Lannion (Bretagne) to protest against the closure of the local hospital's emergency and ophthalmological units and demand better access to healthcare for everyone.

On 31 January 2025, in the morning, at the call of local parents' groups and municipal leaders (political affiliation not specified), around 60 people, including parents, local elected officials, and residents, gathered outside the Maison des services in Latronquiere (Occitanie) to protest against the elimination of a teaching position at the RPI Lauresses institute, which serves the village's only school. The protest was part of a broader regional mobilization against educational cuts impacting schools in Lauresses, Saint-Sulpice, and Marcilhac.

On 14 February 2025, a few CFDT affiliates gathered on Forum Square in Reims (Grand Est) to protest against the release of a woman working for the 'Trattoria' restaurant, claiming her termination was illegal and unfair.

On 11 February 2025, hundreds of students demonstrated in Tours (Centre-Val de Loire). The demonstration was part of a nationwide mobilization of students and university staff called by Ue and UNEF to protest against a state-imposed €1 billion cut in funding for higher education and research.

On 12 January 2025, at the call of StopElon.eu, around 15 people gathered outside the Tesla factory in Hoenheim (Grand Est) to protest against Tesla and X owner Elon Musk, whom the protesters deemed responsible for spreading hate speech and disinformation online. They called on the European Union to sanction Musk.

On 11 February 2025, at the call of APF France Handicap, several dozen people gathered in Quimper (Bretagne) to support the rights of people with disabilities and demand a large-scale 'Marshall Plan for Disability', calling for increased support in accessibility, education, and home care services. Protesters held a banner reading 'The Republic is us too'. After the event, a dozen people spent the night in Saint-Corentin Square. The event took place on the 20th anniversary of the 2005 Law on Equal Opportunities for handicapped people, which the protesters considered only partially enforced.

On 21 February 2025, at the call of the local students' parents association, students' parents and local elected officials gathered in Champagnac-de-Belair (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against the closure of a class and the loss of a teaching position.

On 19 February 2025, at the call of CGT, CFE-CGC, SUD, and CFDT, AFPA employees staged a protest inside their workplace in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against what they perceived as toxic management and demand better working conditions.
On 21 October 2020, nearly 300 persons gathered in Paimpol. They demonstrated as part of a national tribute to a teacher, deadly attacked days before. They also demonstrated for freedom of speech.
On 21 October 2020, over 3,000 persons gathered in Brest. They demonstrated as part of a national tribute to a teacher, deadly attacked days before. They also demonstrated for freedom of speech.
On 16 January 2020, slightly less than 200 persons gathered in Sens to protest against the pension reform.

On 11 February 2025, around 50 AESH (assistants for students with disabilities) and teachers gathered outside the rectorate in Grenoble (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demand better working conditions and improved training. The event took place on the 20th anniversary of the 2005 Law on Equal Opportunities for handicapped people, which the protesters considered only partially enforced.

On 11 February 2025, people, including the national deputy Thierry Perez (RN), gathered in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against low-emission zones (ZFE), which, according to protesters, are unfair measures that disproportionately impact workers, particularly those commuting to Lyon and Grenoble.
On 25 February 2025, striking teachers and students' parents at Laennec College gathered in Pont-l'Abbe (Bretagne) to protest the planned closure of a class.

On 22 October 2020, around 60 journalists and MPs, including members of LFI, PCF, UDI and Generation.s, demonstrated in Belfort. They denounced cuts in the industrial sector employment caused by the sale of General Electric.

On 5 March 2025, at 12.30 pm, around 10 police officers gathered outside the police station in Aubenas (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The event was part of a nationwide mobilization in front of police stations, called by APN, to support a police officer facing trial for the murder of 17-year-old youth Nahel M. in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 4 March 2025, around 10 people, including municipal councilor Guillaume Auffret (RE), gathered in Vannes (Bretagne) to protest against the planned construction of a luxury hotel and at least 60 housing units on the former Greta school site. Protesters cited concerns over increased traffic, lack of green space, and insufficient consultation from local authorities.

On 26 February 2025, people gathered outside the C8 studios in Issy-les-Moulineaux (Ile-de-France) to protest in favor of the French Regulatory Authority for Audiovisual and Digital Communication's (ARCOM) decision to remove C8 and its show Touche pas a Mon Poste (TPMP), hosted by news anchor Cyril Hanouna, from the list of free programs on French TV. Protesters accused the show of spreading hate speech and far-right ideology.

On 28 October 2020, in the morning, between 300 and 400 members of the Armenian community blocked the highway toll near Vienne, in Isere. They demonstrated for the recognition of the independence of Artsakh. Clashes between demonstrators and members of the Turkish community from the surrounding area were reported.

On 6 March 2025, in the evening, local elected officials, students' parents, and students gathered outside the Francois-Marie Luzel school in Saint-Thegonnec (Bretagne) to protest against the announced closure of a class at the facility, denouncing the impact it would have on students and local education.
On 22 February 2025, around 20 people gathered at a roundabout in La Fare les Oliviers (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against a one-way traffic system.

On 21 March 2025, at 5:30 pm, around 60 people gathered in De la Republique Square in Metz (Grand Est) to express their support for the Palestinian people following the resumption of Israeli military strikes on Gaza, which were said to have killed over 500 Palestinians since 19 March 2025 at the time of reporting. Participants sought to raise awareness about the situation and reaffirm solidarity with Palestinians amid the escalating conflict.

On 22 March 2025, people took to the streets in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide day of demonstration called by several trade unions and organizations, including CGT, LDH, and La Cimade, coinciding with the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination, to denounce systemic racism and promote equality and justice.

On 22 March 2025, at the call of GE, PCF, PS and LFI, 200 people gathered in Perigueux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against fascism. The event was part of a nationwide day of demonstration called by several trade unions and organizations, including CGT, LDH, and La Cimade, coinciding with the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination, to denounce systemic racism and promote equality and justice.

On 26 March 2025, at the call of the Union for the University Struggle (Syndicat de Combat Universitaire - SCUM), students gathered outside a student housing facility in Montpellier (Occitanie) to protest against the planned increase in rent. The protest took place as Mayor Michael Delafosse was inaugurating the building.

On 1 November 2020, people, including an association for disabled people and their unions (CGT, CFDT, FO), demonstrated in Carcassonne against the project to reorganize working hours which they feel could threaten their work-life balance if there is not a clear separation between work hours and private life.

On 2 November 2020, driving school employees demonstrated in Orleans against the forced closure due to new coronavirus-related regulations such as lockdown. They warned the government about the possible permanent closure of their businesses due to lack of funds.

On 2 November 2020, a dozen hairdressers demonstrated in Carpentras against the forced closure of their businesses by the government due to coronavirus-related measures such as lockdown. They denounced what they perceive as unfair and unequal treatment between them and dominant companies allowed to stay open to the public.

On 6 April 2025, around 15 members of FFMC staged a protest in Villenave-d'Ornon (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) as part of a broader nationwide mobilization against the implementation of Low Emission Zones (ZFE). Protesters argued that the ZFE policies disproportionately impacted low-income individuals who could not afford to replace their older, more polluting vehicles. Demonstrators denounced the measures as socially discriminatory and called for their repeal.

On 8 April 2025, at the call of CGT and FO, between 100 and 150 employees staged a protest at the Merck site in the Technopole Bordeaux Montesquieu in Martillac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to denounce the planned elimination of 106 jobs. Protesters criticized the company's decision as a strategic failure, given recent investments and hiring efforts, and demanded improved severance conditions. The demonstration took place amid broader concerns about Merck's withdrawal from the site and uncertainty surrounding the planned transfer of operations to the American firm AbbVie.

On 6 April 2025, at the call of SUD and CGT, dozens of striking nursing assistants at the university hospital gathered in Rouen (Normandie) to protest against staff shortages and poor working conditions. Protesters wore white blouses with letters reading 'Angry' and 'On strike'.

On 15 April 2025, at the call of CGT, striking teachers held a protest outside the Paul Vallon school in Givors (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to denounce deteriorating working conditions and demand additional resources after a teacher was injured while intervening in a student brawl the previous week. The protest followed the return of two students involved in the incident, which staff said highlighted the lack of institutional support in the face of repeated violence.

On 15 April 2025, several hundred people, including local elected officials such as Nievre Departmental President Fabien Bazin (PS), Mayor of Clermont-Ferrand Olivier Bianchi (PS), and Mayor of Nevers Denis Thuriot (RE), gathered outside the Austerlitz train station in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand that the train line between Clermont-Ferrand and Paris be renovated, citing recurring delays of trains. The event was part of the 'train of anger' action, whereby residents and elected officials from towns on the Clermont-Paris line rode a train to Paris to voice their concerns to authorities and demand more state investments.

On 12 April 2025, at the call of CGT and FO, around 200 Eurokera and Keraglass employees, as well as local elected officials, demonstrated in Chateau-Thierry (Hauts-de-France) to protest against downsizing at their factories.
On 12 April 2025, L214 affiliates gathered outside a Leclerc supermarket in Migennes (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to protest against animal cruelty at pig slaughterhouses.

On 12 April 2025, 200 people gathered in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to demonstrate. The event was part of a demonstration movement called by several organizations, including Attac, APGL, La Cimade, CGT, FSU, Greenpeace, LDH, NT, MRAP, SOS Racism, SM, Ue, UNEF, and SUD, to support the rule of law and democracy after supporters of far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, who was convicted by a Paris court for embezzling 4.4 million euros in EU funds and barred from running in the 2027 presidential election, claimed that her trial was politically motivated and abused judges online.

On 12 April 2025, at least 2,000 people demonstrated in Nantes (Pays de la Loire). The event was part of a nationwide wave of protests to defend so-called 'free parties' (unannounced and unauthorized dance parties taking place in public spaces and spanning a few days) amid discussions on a proposed law seeking harsher penalties for organizing such gatherings.
On 16 April 2025, at the call of CR and JA, farmers gathered outside the Prefecture in Pau (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand the right to kill wolves to protect their livestock.

On 19 April 2025, at the call of StopMines 87-24, more than 300 people, including farmers, took to the streets in Saint-Yrieix-la-Perche (Nouvelle-Aquitaine), marching from the train station to the town hall, to protest against the construction of a gold mine in the area. Protesters warned that the project would threaten local agriculture, pollute soil and water with toxic substances, and undermine tourism and biodiversity.

On 29 April 2025, nearly 500 people, including medical students and doctors, took to the streets in Brest (Bretagne) to protest against the proposed Garot law regulating where new doctors can set up practice in the hopes of tackling 'medical deserts' across the country. The protest was part of a nationwide demonstration day called by several medical student associations and unions of liberal doctors, including ANEMF and FMF, who argue the bill would worsen healthcare access by discouraging young doctors from entering private practice.

On 28 April 2025, at the call of FCPE, 150 people gathered outside the town hall in Villefranche-de-Rouergue (Occitanie) to protest against local authorities' decision to trust a private company with the management of the local summer camp instead of FCPE.

On 30 April 2025, at the call of FO-INV, around 100 people gathered in front of the Arpe building in Paris (Ile-de-France) to call for rules about competition for VTC (vehicle-for-hire) drivers and for Arpe to be dissolved, arguing that the entity, which coordinated dialogue between Uber, Bolt, Heetch and the drivers, did not represent the drivers.

On 1 May 2025, in the morning, on the occasion of Labor and International Workers' Day, at the local call of CGT, FO, FSU and UNSA, around 150 people, including PCF, PS, LDH, and Corsica Palestina members gathered for a rally in front of the prefecture in Ajaccio (Corse) to demand better working conditions, higher wages, the repeal of pension reform and greater job security.
On 16 January 2020, people protested in Saint-Nazaire against the pension reform.

On 3 May 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of CFDT, dozens of Decathlon employees staged a protest inside the store at De la Madeleine Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand better pay and improved working conditions. Protesters denounced the deterioration of conditions during ongoing renovation works and criticized the company for refusing to close the store despite the disruptions. The demonstration was part of a broader nationwide mobilization by Decathlon employees.

On 3 May 2025, at 2:30 pm, half a dozen activists from PAZ and L214 staged a protest outside the Decathlon store in Vouneuil-sous-Biard (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) against the sale of live fish as bait. Protesters held banners and distributed leaflets to raise awareness about the suffering of live fish used for fishing.

On 7 May 2025, around 100 teachers gathered outside their high school in Saint-Tropez (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against the reinstatement of two students who had been evicted from the school for bullying.

On 10 May 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the 9 May Committee (Comite du 9 Mai), an association of far-right groups rooted in the dissolved GUD (Union Defense Group), around 1,000 far-right affiliates, including Marc de Caqueray-Valmenier, Raphael Ayma (Tenesoun), Alexandre Boumy (Towers and Lilies (Tours et Lys)), Jean-Eudes Gannat, and Axel Loustau, marched through the Montparnasse neighborhood in Paris (Ile-de-France) to commemorate the death of far-right activist Sebastien Deyzieu. Demonstrators chanted 'Europe, Youth, Revolution' and antisemitic slogans, carried Celtic Cross banners, and wore clothing bearing neo-Nazi symbols. Police repeatedly pushed back, sometimes violently, counter-demonstrators, including antifascist activists. Some far-right protesters also issued threats invoking the 'Great Replacement' and called for the deportation of immigrants.

On 12 May 2025, at the call of the Vita Alliance (Alliance Vita), around 20 people, including health workers and other supporters, staged a symbolic protest in Sable-sur-Sarthe (Pays de la Loire) against the planned legalization of assisted suicide in France. Dressed in hospital gowns, participants lay on the ground at Place de la Republique to demand improved palliative care and denounce the assisted dying bill being debated in the National Assembly.

On 13 May 2025, people, including SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered in Saint-Etienne (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of civil servants called by CGT, UNSA, FSU, SUD, and CFE-CGC to protest against state-imposed cuts in funding for public services and demand better working conditions.

On 13 May 2025, around 150 people, including teachers, health workers, and SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered in Belfort (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of civil servants called by CGT, UNSA, FSU, SUD, and CFE-CGC to protest against state-imposed cuts in funding for public services and demand better working conditions.

On 13 May 2025, around 120 people gathered in Strasbourg (Grand Est) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of civil servants called by CGT, UNSA, FSU, SUD, and CFE-CGC to protest against state-imposed cuts in funding for public services and demand better working conditions.

On 13 May 2025, around 30 people gathered in Saint-Lo (Normandie) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of civil servants called by CGT, UNSA, FSU, SUD, and CFE-CGC to protest against state-imposed cuts in funding for public services and demand better working conditions.

On 13 May 2025, around 150 people, including FO, CNT, and SNES-FSU affiliates, as well as prison guards, gathered in Perpignan (Occitanie) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of civil servants called by CGT, UNSA, FSU, SUD, and CFE-CGC to protest against state-imposed cuts in funding for public services and demand better working conditions.

On 5 November 2020, shop owners, members of the PCF, Attac, Generation's and independent politicians, gathered in front of the sub prefecture in Aix-en-Provence. They denounced the obligation to keep non-essential businesses closed during the lockdown, as a measure adopted by the government to address the coronavirus pandemic.

On 20 May 2025, around 160 taxi drivers carried out a checkpoint-style roadblock at the western and eastern entrances of the tunnel in Toulon (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur), selectively allowing vehicles to pass. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement led by FNAT and FNDT to demonstrate against the new Assurance Maladie (France's national health insurance system) convention cutting medical-transport fees, and against growing competition with VTC (vehicle-for-hire) drivers.

On 19 May 2025, at 9 am, around 50 taxi drivers gathered in front of the hospital and the A41 north access, then drove to the train station and the Primary Health Insurance Fund in Annecy (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement led by FNAT and FNDT to demonstrate against the new Assurance Maladie (France's national health insurance system) convention cutting medical-transport fees, and against growing competition with VTC (vehicle-for-hire) drivers.

On 19 May 2025, around 60 taxi drivers set off from Tulle (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) and split into two convoys, one slowly heading towards Ussel (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) and another driving along the RD 1089 towards Brive-la-Gaillarde (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) (coded as a separate event). The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement led by FNAT and FNDT to demonstrate against the new Assurance Maladie (France's national health insurance system) convention cutting medical-transport fees, and against growing competition with VTC (vehicle-for-hire) drivers.

On 28 May 2025, in the afternoon, around 10 farmers affiliated with CR, along with five tractors, gathered outside Lille (Hauts-de-France) to protest tighter fertilizer regulations under the revised Nitrates directive. Protesters wrote 'CR59, we won't give up' in fluorescent paint on a tractor, denouncing the new regulations and calling for immediate action to address their concerns.

On 26 May 2025, at the call of PCF, LE, and PS, hundreds of people, including LE Secretary General Marine Tondelier, PS Secretary General and National Deputy Olivier Faure, and PCF Secretary General and Mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux Fabien Roussel, gathered on Trocadero Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and condemn what they considered a 'genocide' of Palestinians by the Israeli army in Gaza.

On 28 May 2025, at the call of SLT, between 100 and 200 people, including members of local committees, gathered in front of the train station in Toulouse (Occitanie) to protest in favor of a court ruling demanding the end of the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres due to environmental concerns.

On 28 May 2025, around six members of the association Mouv'Enfants staged a protest outside the diocesan house in Arras (Hauts-de-France) to demand the closure of the Riaumont children's village in Lievin (Hauts-de-France), amid ongoing investigations into allegations of violence and sexual abuse. Protesters held banners condemning church silence and impunity, and accused the Bishop of Arras of minimizing the abuse suffered by former residents.

On 24 May 2025, at the call of the Palestine Collective (Collectif Palestine) and the Network for a Just Peace in the Near East (Reseau pour une Paix Juste au Proche-Orient), around 100 people gathered in Dole (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to condemn what they considered an Israeli 'genocide' of Palestinians and condemn the killing of Palestinian civilians by the Israeli army.

On 5 June 2025, around 60 people gathered in Cahors (Occitanie). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement called by CGT and FSU against the pension reform and in support of higher salaries.

On 5 June 2025, 200 people gathered in Pau (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement called by CGT and FSU against the pension reform and in support of higher salaries.

On 2 June 2025, farmers from several localities with around fifty tractors, staged a protest in front of the Palais des Congres in Arles (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) against the construction of an overhead high-voltage power line crossing protected natural areas, and to demand instead that the cables be buried to preserve their land and the environment. Protesters held banners reading 'Bury the line, no pylons', 'No to overhead lines', and 'No to the extra-high voltage'.
On 16 January 2020, nearly 250 persons protested in Montbard against the pension reform.

On 6 November 2020, around 100 high school students blocked the entrance of the Aristide-Briand high school in Saint-Nazaire. They denounced the inadequate sanitary protocol and the obligation for students to attend face-to-face lectures in schools, while the rest of the country is in lockdown, as a measure adopted by the government to address the coronavirus crisis. They threw projectiles at the police who responded with tear gas and arrested at least four students. One student was injured, while no fatalities were reported.

On 31 May 2025, at 2 pm, at the call of Le Girofard center, thousands of people took part in the Pride March in Bordeaux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand equal rights and recognition for the LGBTQ+ community and to denounce discrimination and inequality.

On 6 November 2020, dozens of students gathered at the Paix square in Draguignan. They denounced the inadequate sanitary protocol and the obligation for students to attend face-to-face lectures in schools, while the rest of the country is in lockdown, as a measure adopted by the government to address the coronavirus crisis.

On 13 June 2025, dozens of workers occupied and blocked the Tetra Pak factory in Longvic (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to protest against the planned closure of the site and demand fairer conditions in the proposed social plan.

On 6 November 2020, representatives of the teachers' unions gathered in front of the Clement-Marot high school in Cahors. They denounced the inadequate sanitary protocol and the obligation for teachers to give face-to-face lectures in schools while the rest of the country is in lockdown, a measure adopted by the government to address the coronavirus crisis.
On 7 June 2025, several hundred people, including members of the LGBTQ+ community, gathered for a Pride March in Ales (Occitanie) to demand more acceptance of queer people.

On 20 June 2025, at the call of Antifascist Action (Action Antifasciste), around 200 people gathered in Angouleme (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against police checks on undocumented migrants. The protesters expressed solidarity with migrants and condemned what they considered institutionalized racism.

On 19 June 2025, at the call of CGT, LFI, SUD, FO, and RP, around 100 social workers gathered outside the Departmental Council in Montpellier (Occitanie) to protest against cuts in state funding for social programs, a step they argued was unfair.

On 16 June 2025, around 100 people, including employees and local elected officials, marched in Sallanches (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the planned closure of the Dynastar ski factory, and to denounce job cuts affecting 57 workers.

On 14 June 2025, people, including SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered outside the Maison de la Culture in Amiens (Hauts-de-France) to protest against planned cuts to artistic workshops and options in educational curricula.

On 24 June 2025, striking teachers from the Fontenelle school gathered for a picket line in Rouen (Normandie) to protest against the temporary exclusion of a student who carried two knives into the school. The protesters deemed the sanction too lenient and called for more action against youth violence.
On 21 June 2025, at the call of FO, around 40 Ikea employees gathered for a picket line in La Maxe (Grand Est) to demand a pay rise.

On 7 November 2020, around 269 persons demonstrated in multiple cities including gathering in front of the city hall in Ciboure. They denounced the second lockdown of the year, a measure implemented by the government to address the new coronavirus outbreak.

On 28 June 2025, at the call of CP, around 80 farmers gathered in Avignon (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against the Duplomb Law, which aimed to legalize the use of certain previously banned pesticides, citing their potential environmental impact and health risks for both farmers and consumers.

On 30 June 2025, at the call of CGT and FO, health workers gathered outside the hospital in Laval (Pays de la Loire) against a restructuring plan by the Regional Health Agency that included cutting jobs and reducing services, and demanding the protection of public healthcare.

On 29 June 2025, people gathered in Rennes (Bretagne). The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement called by the collective Feed, comprising notably Greenpeace and WWF, as well as CP, CGT, and Cancer Anger (Cancer Colere) against the Duplomb Law, which aimed to legalize the use of certain previously banned pesticides, citing their potential environmental impact and health risks for both farmers and consumers.

On 30 June 2025, at the call of SUD, striking staff of the La Coustourelle elderly home (EHPAD) demonstrated in Sommieres (Occitanie) to protest against a proposed merger of their facility with others, and to denounce their working conditions.
