The event was part of a national day of protest called by Greenpeace, Friends of the Earth, International Movement ATD Fourth World, Attac, CARE, CCFD-Terre Solidaire (Catholic Committee against hunger and for development), XR, L214, FAGE, France Nature Environnement (French Nature Environment), Generations Futures (Future Generations), LDH, LPO - Ligue pour la protection des oiseaux (League for the Protection of Birds), Notre affaire a tous (Everyone's Business), OXFAM, SDN, EELV, Generation Ecologie (Ecology Generation), CFDT, and PS, before consideration by parliament of the government's climate and resilience bill, which they criticized.

On 27 March 2021, people, including Reinfo Covid members, protested in Les Sables-d'Olonne to call for a more democratic system where they could have the choice to respect or not coronavirus-related measures. They also protested against the government's management of the coronavirus health crisis.
On 28 January 2020, in the morning, around forty teachers gathered in front of the Clement Marot high school in Cahors. They protested against the education reform.

On 7 April 2021, around 40 people, mostly feminist collective activists and FSU union members, protested in Toulouse to call on authorities to implement concrete measures to tackle the issue of sexual and sexist violence in schools. They call for more training for school staff to be implemented and for them to spread more awareness among students.

On 6 April 2021, people, including elected officials, protested and blocked the entrance of a construction site in Regneville-sur-Mer against the future installation of a 5G antenna. They called on the company (Orange) to change the location of the antenna.
On 28 January 2020, students and teachers demonstrated and blocked their high school in Le Mans against the education reform.

On 3 April 2021, employees of two Carrefour supermarkets demonstrated in front of their working place in Nice at the call of the CFDT and CGT unions. They denounced the lack of consideration of the company towards its employees in terms of salary and reduction of the workforce.
On 29 January 2020, in the morning, students and teachers perturbated exams at the Malraux high school in Biarritz to protest against the education reform.
On 10 April 2021, yellow vest demonstrators gathered in Daumesnil-Villiers in Paris. They called for social and fiscal justice.
On 10 April 2021, between 350 and 400 persons demonstrated in Steenwerck. They denounced the project to implement a henhouse for intensive breeding.

On 10 April 2021, around 100 persons gathered on their motorbike in Montebourg at the call of the FFMC. They denounced the European reform aiming at extending compulsory periodic vehicle inspections to motorbikes by 2022.

On 13 April 2021, around 100 employees of SKF and FO union members protested in Avallon against the closure of the factory as well as the management's decision not to pay bonuses until the definitive closure of the site by 2022.

On 17 April 2021, more than 400 people, including union members (FSU, SUD, CGT), archeologists, yellow vests demonstrators, temporary workers of the entertainment and cultural industries, protested in Orleans against the forced closure of the arts sector due to coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government and unemployment benefit reforms. Protesters called for the right to reopen their businesses and better pay for all.

On 20 April 2021, around 50 police officers demonstrated in front of the courthouse in Bethune, at the national call of the National Police Alliance and UNSA unions. They denounced the outcome of the trial of demonstrators who attacked and severely injured police officers in Viry Chatillon in 2016.

On 17 April 2021, around 50 people protested in Sallanches against what they perceive as infringements of freedom due to coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government. A flash mob happened to denounce the government's policies. It was part of the national movement 'Keep Dancing' calling for people to sing the song 'Danser encore' to call for more freedom.

On 30 April 2021, several employees of the Carrefour supermarket in Le Millenaire mall demonstrated in Aubervilliers. They denounced the project to use a sub-contractor for the management of the store, and its consequences on the social rights of employees.

On 24 April 2021, around 300 people, including feminist collective activists and the LGBT community, protested in Lyon for a 'bioethics' bill extending access to Assisted Reproductive Technology to lesbian couples and single women. They protested against the Senate's vote to suppress this specific amendment. It was part of the national movement 'Lesbian March'. Around 40 far-right members demonstrate against the 'Lesbian March' and threw projectiles at the pro-LGBT demonstrators. Police forces intervened and used tear gas to disperse the rioters.
On 24 April 2021, around 50 people from all over the region protested in Pluvigner against the future installation of 5G antennas implemented by the company Orange.

On 24 April 2021, around 50 motorcyclists protested in Montlucon against the introduction of a vehicle safety inspection for motorcycles, the increase in the price of the registration card, against the 30km/h city speed limit, and the mandatory wearing of safety vests.
On 1 May 2021, around 1,000 persons demonstrated in Strasbourg on the occasion of Labour Day. They called for social justice and for the defense of public hospitals.

On 3 May 2021, students of the Malherbe high school blocked the entrance of their school in Caen at the call of the UNL union. They denounced the consequences of the coronavirus-related remote teaching on their education and called for the cancellation of baccalaureate exams.

On 3 May 2021, around 200 students of the Iris high school blocked the entrance of their school in Lormont at the call of the UNL union. They denounced the consequences of the coronavirus-related remote teaching on their education and called for the cancellation of baccalaureate exams.
On 1 May 2021, around 70 persons demonstrated in Le Treport on the occasion of Labour Day at the call of the CGT union. They called for social justice.
On 6 May 2021, around 30 people, including elected officials and CGT union members, protested in Somain against the closure of a state treasury.

On 3 May 2021, around 20 persons demonstrated in Sete. They denounced the lack of action of European countries regarding the death of migrants in the Mediterranean sea, and paid tribute to the 130 victims of the shipwreck of 22 April.

On 6 May 2021, around 70 people, including health workers, non-medical hospital staff, school assistants for students with disabilities, union members (FO, CGT), and hospital cleaners, protested in Dieppe because health workers, social workers, and non-medical hospital staff, are not entitled to a monthly salary increase that hospital health workers have been granted by the Segur agreements. Protesters called for better pay for all health workers and extended bonuses.

On 5 May 2021, students protested in Perpignan to call on the government to replace the traditional end of secondary school exam ('Baccalaureat') by continuous assessment because of the difficult study conditions due to the coronavirus health crisis.
On 1 May 2021, over 1,500 persons, including members of the SNES-FSU union, demonstrated in Rouen on the occasion of Labour Day. They called for social justice.

On 4 May 2021, teachers and school employees protested in Valdoie against the principal of the high school. They denounced 'organizational difficulties' due to how he is, according to them, unqualified in his duties.

On 6 May 2021, intensive care health workers protested in Nimes to call for better recognition, better pay, and a better status. They denounced poor working conditions due to exhaustion caused by the coronavirus health crisis.

On 6 May 2021, around 60 students protested in Deauville to call on the government to replace the end of secondary school exam ('Baccalaureat') by continuous assessment because of the difficult study conditions due to the coronavirus health crisis. They protested to show support to high schools that struggled more than theirs during the coronavirus health crisis.

On 11 May 2021, 65 intensive care health workers from all over the region protested in Beauvais at the call of CGT union for a specific bonus, more training, better recognition, better pay, and better status. Protesters called for more human resources. They denounced poor working conditions worsened by the coronavirus health crisis.

On 11 May 2021, intensive care health workers protested in Ales at the call of unions (CFDT, CGT) for a specific bonus, more training, better recognition, better pay, and better status. Protesters called for more human resources. They denounced poor working conditions worsened by the coronavirus health crisis.

On 11 May 2021, people, mostly temporary workers and employees of the entertainment and cultural industries from the 'Occupy Theaters' movement, protested in Dijon against the forced closure of the arts sector due to coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government and unemployment benefit reforms.

On 10 May 2021, around 20 employees of the Lapeyre group gathered in front of the commercial court of Paris at the call of the CGT union. They denounced the acquisition proposal submitted by a potential buyer.

On 9 May 2021, nearly 200 demonstrators, including students, gathered in Morlaix. They demanded actions to tackle the climate emergency and called for improvements in the 'Climate and Resilience' bill on global warming adopted by the French Parliament on 4 May.

On 10 May 2021, students demonstrated in Meylan and blocked the entrance of the Gresivaudan high school at the call of the UNL union. They denounced the consequences of the coronavirus-related remote teaching on their education and called for the cancellation of baccalaureate exams. Gendarmes officers were present but no violent interaction was reported.

On 11 May 2021, between 150 and 200 (according to the police) intensive care health workers protested in Marseille for a specific bonus, more training, better recognition, better pay, and better status. Protesters called for more human resources. They denounced poor working conditions worsened by the coronavirus health crisis.

On 9 May 2021, demonstrators gathered in Saint-Brieuc. They demanded actions to tackle the climate emergency and called for improvements in the 'Climate and Resilience' bill on global warming adopted by the French Parliament on 4 May.

On 15 May 2021, around 30 pro-Palestine protesters, including several activists (PCF, France-Palestine Solidarity Association, CGT, FSU, EELV, Generation.s), demonstrated in Cahors to call for sustainable peace in Palestine. They condemned the United Nations Security Council's inability to make a decision and the French government's silence regarding recent attacks from Israel.

On 17 May 2021, around 100 anesthetists and students protested in Toulon at the call of unions (CGT, FO) to demand a better status, more recognition, and better pay. They defended their profession's specific flexible skills. Protesters also demonstrated because they are not entitled to a monthly salary increase that hospital health workers have been granted by the Segur agreements.
On 17 May 2021, employees of the Foundry of Bretagne and Renault protested and slowed down traffic in Lorient against job cuts and the closure of the foundry.

On 17 May 2021, more than 150 police officers and APN members protested in Rive-de-Gier to support a police officer who was injured while on duty. They called on the government to be more responsive in dealing with violence against police officers. Protesters called for a more severe penal response.
On 15 May 2021, around 2000 pro-Palestine protesters demonstrated in Montpellier to call for an immediate end to the Israeli bombing in Palestine.
On 3 February 2020, around 100 lawyers, health workers and other professionals gathered in Marseille. They protested against the pension reform and the policy of the government.

On 22 May 2021, between 650 (according to the police) and 1000 (according to organizers) pro-Palestine protesters demonstrated in Lille against 'colonization, repression of Palestinians, and Israel's apartheid policy.' They called for a boycott of Israeli products.

On 2 June 2021, around 50 organic farmers, including CP and CR union members, protested in Marcay (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) against the reform of the EU's Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and the reduction of European financial aid to farmers.

On 3 June 2021, around 50 people, including elected officials, union members, and school assistants for students with disabilities, protested in Dieppe to call for better working conditions, better pay, more training, and recognition of their work.
On 3 June 2021, around 10 garbage collectors and FSU union members demonstrated in Marseille against the privatization of their services.

On 3 June 2021, nearly 200 non-medical employees of a clinic and health workers protested in Besancon to call for better working conditions and better pay. They felt concerned by the announced takeover by the Elsan group.

On 29 May 2021, rioters set around fifteen cars on fire and targeted the buildings of the gendarmerie in La Selle-la-Forge. They acted after gendarmes officers arrested a young man, while no fatalities nor injuries were reported.
On 5 June 2021, demonstrators gathered in front of the city hall in Metz. They denounced the femicide attempt against a woman days before and called for actions against violence against women.

On 12 June 2021, about 120 people, including CGT and FSU trade union affiliates and supporters, gathered outside the Labor Exchange in Narbonne (Narbonne, Aude, Occitanie) to protest against the rise of far-right ideas and denounce the government's social and security policies. The event was part of a national day of protest.

On 12 June 2021, people, including FSU affiliates, marched through the streets of Auch (Auch, Gers, Occitanie) to protest against the alleged rise of far-right ideas in France. The event was part of a national day of protest.

On 12 June 2021, around 60 people, including the mayors of La Souterraine and Saint-Sulpiece-le-Gueretois, an EELV regional councilor, and CGT, FSU and SNUIPP-FSU trade union affiliates, gathered and marched through the streets of Gueret (Gueret, Creuse, Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against the alleged rise of far-right ideas in France and denounce the role alleged played by the government in the process. The event was part of a national day of protest.
On 17 June 2021, civil servants demonstrated in Plouzane. They denounced the implementation of a bill reforming public services.

On 18 June 2021, nearly 30 employees of the Auchan supermarket demonstrated in Saint-Herblain at the call of the FO, CGT and CFDT unions. They called for a bonus for working during the coronavirus pandemic.

On 12 June 2021, over 250 people, including La Cimade, Attac, MRAP, RESF, CGT, EELV, FSU, Generation.s, LDH, LFI, PCF, PS, Occitanie Party, SUD and JC, marched through the streets of Pau (Pau, Pyrenees-Atlantiques, Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against far-right ideas and racism. The event was part of a national day of protest.

On 12 June 2021, between 300 and 500 people, including members of a Puy-de-Dome fight collective against the far-right, marched through the streets of Clermont-Ferrand (Clermont-Ferrand, Puy-de-Dome, Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the alleged rise of far-right ideas in France. The event was part of a national day of protest.

On 15 June 2021, parents of students demonstrated at the Jean-Moulin intermediate school in Montreuil at the call of the FCPE union. They staged a funerary march to denounce the suppression of three classes in the next school term.
On 6 February 2020, students blocked the Lyon 2 University. They protested against the pension reform and the reform of the academic research system.
On 23 June 2021, around 50 employees of the Ateliers company demonstrated in Flourens at the call of the CGT union. They called for a salary raise and better working conditions.
On 19 June 2021, people demonstrated in Saint-Lo against the increase of a waste collection tax.

On 17 June 2020, people gathered in Bearwood for a Black Lives Matter protest organized by Stand Up To Racism, demonstrating against police brutality and systemic racism after the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 24 June 2020, market traders gathered in Burnley to protest the local council's offer of 50% rent rates for three months due to coronavirus, which the traders say is not enough, demanding the reduction for the whole year.

On 25 June 2020, Extinction Rebellion activists held a demonstration in Forres town centre to deliver a letter to their local MP, demanding action on the climate crisis as part of the group's national campaign responding to the report publication by the Committee for Climate Change.

On 1 July 2020, several residents set up camp on Moredunvale Green in Edinburgh, staying overnight before being joined by further protesters the next morning as they demonstrated against a proposed housing development for the spot.

On 4 July 2020, campaigners from the group Keep our NHS Public staged a protest in front of Harrogate District Hospital in Harrogate, demanding a halt to the underfunding and privatization of healthcare to coincide with the 72nd anniversary of the NHS founding.

On 25 July 2020, around 35 people staged a protest organised by Cardiff & Vale Stand Up To Racism with Black Lives Matters outside the Civic Offices demanding that the Vale of Glamorgan Council re-name a Barry street they say has 'slavery' connotations.
On 25 July 2020, more than 60 cyclists and Extinction Rebellion members staged a bike ride protest in Nottingham to bring attention to the climate emergency.

On 8 August 2020, nurses carrying placards demonstrated at Merthyr fountain and outside the Princess of Wales Hospital in Bridgend protesting against being excluded from recent public sector pay rise deals. It was reported that thousands of health workers protested over the weekend across the country.

On 13 August 2020, protesters with flags and signs travelled across three constituencies in Staines-upon-Thames atop a open top bus as part of a demonstration against job cuts at British Airways. The bus also stopped at Hillingdon Conservative Club, Spelthorne Borough Council offices and Heathrow Airport.

On 28 August 2020, at least three Extinction Rebellion campaigners protested outside Shell Centre, the London headquarters of the major oil firm, in London - Lambeth and spray-painted the word 'LIES' by the entrance. At least one protester was arrested. Another Extinction Rebellion group marched by Southbank, Lambeth calling on the UK government to scrap the high-speed rail project and invest in sustainable projects.

On 29 August 2020, Extinction Rebellion activists held a bike ride in Barnstaple as part of a nationwide protest announcing the start of a rebellion and protesting against government inaction on the climate and the ecological emergency.

On 2 September 2020, hundreds of Extinction Rebellion activists staged the second day of protest in various locations in London - Westminster calling on politicians to back the Climate and Ecological Emergency Bill. Activists attempted to block Prime Minster Boris Johnson from getting to the Parliament in Westminster for the first Prime Minister's Questions since the summer recess. They were then taken away by police. Another group of activists protested outside Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs drawing attention to the government's 'failure' to act on the critical question of climate change. HS2 Rebellion, a sister group of Extinction Rebellion, occupied trees in Parliament Square protesting HS2 project. Hundreds of people and XR Doctors activists demonstrated on the square to highlight the health risks associated with climate change.

On 19 September 2020, members of Stand Up To Racism and Care4Calais held a rally in Glasgow as part of a day of action in solidarity with refugees in the UK. A MP and the PCS union also supported the event.

Around 20 September 2020, (weekend of) Save British Farming staged a go-slow tractor demonstration in Crymych, Pembrokeshire to protest against the Agriculture Bill, which they say would harm UK farming and food standards.

On 22 September 2020, Extinction Rebellion activists protested outside of local council offices in Llandrindod Wells, demanding the maintenance of the climate emergency declaration, which was going to vote that day.

On 22 September 2020, farmers and supporters of Save British Farming drove tractors down the high street in Northallerton, Hambleton and gathered in Market Place to rally against the proposed Agriculture Bill, which they say will harm the UK farming industry.

On 25 September 2020, members of UK Student Climate Network marched through Oxford as part of ongoing climate protests. They dropped banners in places, including outside the city council offices in St Aldates, the Radcliffe Camera, the Westgate Centre, and the Plain. Campaigners from Parents For Future Oxford also placed dozens of pairs of shoes in front of the Radcliffe Camera to represent all the children who will be affected by climate change.

On 30 September 2020, hundreds of pantomime art workers and theatre professionals marched in London - Westminster before gathering at the Parliament as part of the global #WeMakeEvents day of action to protest against the government's handling of the coronavirus pandemic and demanded sector-specific support to help theatre workers.
On 30 September 2020, soft play business owners demonstrated outside the Scottish Parliament in Edinburgh to demand indoor soft play centers to be allowed to reopen or receive government support.
On 8 October 2020, members of Oxford Friends of the Earth rallied in Henley-on-Thames calling for urgent action to cut the 'unacceptable' levels of pollution across Oxfordshire.

On 8 October 2020, protesters waving flags and chanting protested on The Slade in Headington against a housing development which they fear would cause the destruction of an 8,000 year old fen in the Lye Valley.

On 10 October 2020, around 75 protesters rallied outside Exeter Cathedral in Exeter to protest against the coronavirus restrictions. They were seen wearing T-shirts bearing the Qanon logo and Save Our Children hashtag, a viral campaign against child sexual exploitation.

On 17 October 2020, environmental campaigners gathered outside the Scottish Parliament in Edinburgh protesting against the environmental impact of Mossmorran petrochemical plant and call for its closure.
On 17 October 2020, campaigners protested with placards on New Street in Worcester to oppose the netting above the rear entrance to M&S that is regularly trapping and killing wild birds.

On 11 November 2020, people gathered in London - Westminster to protest against perceived inaction to tackle climate change. Members of Extinction Rebellion hung a wreath at the Cenotaph that had inscribed 'Honour Their Sacrificed, Climate Change Means War - Act Now'.

On 21 November 2020, language campaigners staged the 'Wales is not for Sale' rally in Llanberis calling the Welsh Government for emergency powers to control the housing market to ensure homes for local families.

On 19 December 2020, around 100 people joined the protest called by the Black Lives Matter Movement outside Tottenham, London - Haringey, police station in Tottenham after an police officer was filmed being involving in a perceived 'violent assault' against a black student outside a local school. The protesters demanded the release of the officer's body camera footage and the sacking of the police officer. Members of Extinction Rebellion and Stand Up To Racism also joined the event.
On 12 February 2020, at least seven members of the National Education Union (NEU) at Peter Symonds College in Winchester picketed as a part of the strike action to demand more funding.

On 27 March 2021, around 1000 anti-government protesters gathered in central Sheffield in opposition to the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Bill which seeks to give police increased powers to shut down peaceful protests. Protesters gathered on Devonshire Green before marching to Snig Hill and sitting in front of a police station. Police officers were present but did not intervene or make any arrests.

On 13 February 2020, two days after a man accused of murdering journalist Lyra McKee was charged for her murder in Derry in April 2019, a group of his supporters scuffled with police outside of his hearing at the Derry Magistrate Court in Derry - Cityside. The attacker is associated with the NIRA, who claimed responsibility for the attack. There were no injuries.

On 17 April 2021, 25 people gathered outside the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield as the World Snooker Championship was being held to protest against so called 'vaccine passports'. Protesters displayed signs that read 'Medical apartheid is wrong' and 'No Vaxx Passport - Inhumane'.

On 1 May 2021, more than 100 anti-government protesters, including trade union members and healthcare workers, gathered in York city center before marching through the city in a show of opposition to the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Bill which proposes to give police more powers to shutdown peaceful protests.

On 1 May 2021, hundreds of anti-government protesters including members of UCU and the Racial Justice Network gathered on the Woodhouse Moor in Leeds in a show of opposition to the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Bill, which proposes to give police more powers to shut down peaceful protests.

On 8 May 2021, 40 anti-government demonstrators including supporters of ACORN gathered in Newcastle upon Tyne to oppose the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Bill which seeks to give additional powers to police to intervene in peaceful protests.

On 11 May 2021, around 20 teachers and members of the National Education Union gathered outside the gates to the Nottingham Academy in West Bridgford as part of strike action against planned structure changes that will affect the roles of staff at the school.
On 20 May 2021, Extinction Rebellion activists protested outside the Coventry Cathedral in Coventry during a council meeting, calling on councilors to declare a climate emergency.

On 25 May 2021, 40 Black Lives Matter supporters gathered in Southampton, to hold a vigil marking the first anniversary of the murder of George Floyd which sparked an international protest movement. Also in attendance were supporters of SUTR: Stand Up To Racism.

On 15 May 2021, protesters with a poster attempted to storm a mobile testing coronavirus center at a car park in Aston University in Birmingham. They protested lockdown as part of the effort to slow the coronavirus spread, resulting in the center being closed early.

On 4 June 2021, Extinction Rebellion activists and doctors gathered outside the Clarendon Building on Broad Street, Oxford, to protest the second day of the G7 health summit. They carried plaques that read 'End Vaccine Apartheid, We Demand a People's Vaccine' and performed a 'die-on' protest on the steps of the building.

On 5 June 2021, racial equality campaigners, including Black Lives Matter supporters, gathered in Dudley town center to protest against government plans to deport Osime Brown, a black man, to Jamaica - the country he left as a small child. Brown is severely autistic and campaigners fear that he would be endangered if deported.

On 23 June 2021, airport workers staged a protest at Glasgow Airport in Paisley to call for further easing of coronavirus-related restrictions on air travel. Airport workers used vehicles to spell out the word 'help' on the runway.

On 18 February 2020, around a dozen people from the group Vegan Action Wales protested in front of a slaughterhouse in Haverfordwest calling for what they call animal justice. Protesters claim workers sprayed them with water as they demonstrated.
On 1 July 2021, animal welfare activists belonging to the League Against Cruel Sports gathered in Peterborough town center to demonstrate against a planned fox hunt on 21 July.

On 13 July 2021, over 200 people gathered outside the Coffee House Cafe in Fallowfield to stage an anti-racism demonstration after a nearby mural displaying the professional footballer Marcus Rashford had been vandalized following the England national football teams loss to Italy in the EURO 2020 final. This event was organized by Stand Up To Racism.

On 14 July 2021, members of Stand Up to Racism hold an anti-racism protest with placards in Bristol city center in support of three England footballers who had been subjected to racist abuse on social media following missing penalties in the Euro 2020 final.

On 13 July 2021, parents carried placards and lay 60 backpacks on the steps of Warwickshire County Council in Warwick to protest over perceived 'failings' for providing sufficient education supports for Special Educational Needs pupils by the local education authority.

On 28 August 2021, hundreds of campaigners marched the the Gay Village in Manchester as part of a 'Pride not profit' event calling for increased funding for the region's LGBTQ+ charities and community groups after a long-running safer sex scheme was discontinued due to inadequate funding earlier in the month.

On 20 February 2020, activists from the Smash Speciesism group protested outside a meat factory in Hurst, Tameside, demanding the company to change production to plant-based food. They blocked the factory's entrance and locked their arms in concrete blocks. Police arrested 11 people.

On 15 August 2021, around 40 Kashmiri activists belonging to the Freedom Protest campaign group gathered in Maidenhead to protest, calling for the Kashmir region to be returned to the status of a 'semi-autonomous region' under Indian administration.

On 27 August 2021, a fairly small crowd of Extinction Rebellion protesters gathered at Market Place before marching to Castle Street to deliver a letter to Rockhopper Exploration. They protested against the Salisbury-based oil and gas company since it sued the Italian government after ministers stopped them from drilling for oil off the Adriatic coast.

On 14 September 2021, disabled residents and their supporters gathered in Millennium Square in Leeds to protest against local government plans to move a taxi rank immediately outside the station further away. Campaigners say this will cause 'intolerable obstacles' for disabled users. This protest was attended by representatives of the Unite union.

On 22 September 2021, anti-vaccination protesters staged a motorway demonstration near a vaccination center at Pyramids Business Park in Bathgate, protesting coronavirus vaccinations for teenagers aged 12 to 15. The protest caused long traffic delays on the M8 motorway between Edinburgh and Glasgow.

On 22 February 2020, protesters from the groups Save Swansea Trees and Swansea Tree Forum wrapped themselves around eight trees in Swansea city centre to prevent them from being felled, arguing that they are too important for carbon storage.

On 29 September 2021, climate activists from Insulate Britain blocked Junction 3 of the M25 in Swanley twice on the day to demand the government funds the insulation of homes throughout the United Kingdom. About 20 activists in high-vis jackets blocked the roundabout during the second demonstration. Police ended both protests by arresting 27 people in total.

On 8 October 2021, a small group of anti-vaccine campaigners gathered outside Winterbourne Academy in Winterbourne, shouting messages such as 'just say no to this vaccine' and false claims about coronavirus. The protest came after the government decided to offer the coronavirus vaccine to 12-15-year-olds.
On 18 October 2021, doctors belonging to Extinction Rebellion gathered outside the offices of JPMorgan in London - Tower Hamlets to protest against the bank's role in funding fossil fuel industries.

On 23 October 2021, anti-racism activists belonging to Stand Up To Racism gathered outside the Italian embassy in London - Westminster to protest in support of the rights of refugees and to call for their better treatment. A Labour Party Councillor, Michelline Ngongo, address the crowd.

On 6 November 2021, more than 100 climate activists marched through Derby to protest demanding leaders gathered at the COP26 climate conference in Glasgow to take drastic action to counter climate change. The event was organised by the COP26 Coalition. Amongst the protesters were representatives of the Green Party and the Derby Climate Coalition.

On 6 November 2021, in the afternoon, at the call of the COP26 Coalition, hundreds of climate activists, including XR and Green New Deal affiliates, marched through Lowestoft (England) to demand strong action from world leaders gathered at the COP26 summit in Glasgow. Some participants called for urgent climate justice and a just transition away from fossil fuels. The demonstration was part of a nationwide mobilization coinciding with the COP26 conference.

On 21 November 2021, hundred midwives and their supporters gathered in York to protest against dangerous working conditions and staff shortages and called for greater support for maternity units. This protest was part of a co-ordinated series of protest across the country entitled 'A March with Midwives'. Labour MP for York Central, Rachael Maskell, was present and addressed the crowd.

On 20 November 2021, hundreds of climate activists belonging to Insulate Britain staged an occupy-style protest on Lambeth Bridge and Vauxhall Cross in London - Westminster demanding that the government invest in insulation for all homes in the UK as part of the their efforts to counter climate change. Extinction rebellion activists were also amongst the protesters. Police made a total of 124 arrests.
On 1 December 2021, RMT members protested outside Caledonian Sleeper operator Serco's offices in Victoria of London - Westminster to demand pay rise to the company's key workers.

Around 6 December 2021, climate activists belonging to Extinction Rebellion gathered in Reigate to protest in opposition to poor air quality in the area. Activists wore hazmat suits and displayed signs to passing motorists highlighting the area's high levels of air pollution.

On 7 December 2021, around 40 staff from the National Education Union operated picket lines at St Matthews Church of England Primary School in Preston to protest the school's academization plan to join the Cidari Multi Academy Trust from 1 February 2022.

On 17 December 2021, about 20 anti-vaccination demonstrators gathered at a newly-built prison in Wellingborough because they believed it is going to become a coronavirus quarantine camp for unvaccinated people.

On 12 January 2022, 3 anti-vaccination protesters against coronavirus vaccines gathered outside the biotech firm Pall Corporations in Ilfracombe as Chancellor of the Exchequer visited the factory. They carried signs that read 'Politicians follow the money, not the science' and 'say no to vax passports.'

On 15 January 2022, over 100 anti-government protesters marched through Brighton to protest in opposition to the government's Police, Crimes, Sentencing and Courts Bill which is currently being debated in the House of Lords which seeks to place greater restrictions on some types of peaceful protests and greatly increases custodial sentences with other crimes.

On 22 January 2022, anti-mandatory coronavirus vaccination protesters marched through central Newcastle upon Tyne in opposition to a government-set deadline requiring NHS staff to be fully vaccinated or risk losing their jobs or being subject to enforced changes of their duties. NHS workers were present at the event which was named the 'World Wide Rally for Freedom'.

On 22 January 2022, anti-vaccine and anti-government protesters gathered in Totnes to protest against the government-led coronavirus vaccination roll-out with some protesters also showing opposition for the Police, Crimes, Sentencing and Courts Bill which is being considered in parliament currently.

On 5 February 2022, at least 100 residents gathered in Plymouth to calling for more awareness of violence against women and girls and education for boys on the issue. Both Labour and Conservative party councillors were present.

On 12 February 2022, about a hundred local residents gathered outside Renfrewshire Council's headquarters in Paisley to protest against plans for a 179-home housing development near the University of West of Scotland's Thornly Park campus.

On 14 February 2022, Queen's University Belfast staff represented by UCU gathered outside the University in Belfast - South to strike in protest of proposed changes to pensions managed by the Universities Superannuation Scheme that protesters assert will strip up to 35% of their value.

On 17 February 2022, Queen's University Belfast staff represented by UCU gathered outside the University in Belfast - South to strike in protest of proposed changes to pensions managed by the Universities Superannuation Scheme that protesters assert will strip up to 35% of their value.

Around 22 February 2022, members of the Stonehenge Alliance staged a protest outside the British Museum in London - Camden to protest against plans to build a tunnel under the site on which Stonehenge is situated.

Protesters held banners and chanted to oppose the political party's policies and the presence of Farage's 'divisive rhetoric'.

On 21 March 2026, tenants from a building owned by the Partick Housing Association protested in front of the association's offices in Glasgow (Scotland) against a rent increase. The tenants also stated that requested repairs in the building had not taken place.

On 4 April 2026, at the call of Lakenheath Alliance for Peace, more than a hundred people gathered at a peace encampment outside of the airbase in Lakenheath (England), to protest against the use of the airbase by US military forces. Protesters erected a blockade outside of the airbase's main gate. The encampment was formed after a US fighter jet had taken off from the Lakenheath airbase and was later shot down in Iran. The encampment lasted for six days, ending on 6 April. Police intervened and arrested seven people, including two on suspicion of obstructing a public highway, and others on suspicion of supporting Palestine Action.

On 14 April 2026, farmers and haulers formed a slow-moving convoy of tractors and other vehicles in Toome (Northern Ireland), also blocking the A6, as part of a protest against rising energy bills, fuel prices and high taxes. The event was part of an ongoing series of nationwide demonstrations across Ireland and Northern Ireland, which began on 6 April 2026, in response to sharply rising fuel prices and broader cost-of-living pressures.

On 19 April 2026, at the call of Stand Up To Racism, well over a thousand residents gathered in Glasgow (Scotland) as part of a protest against the far-right and racism. Protesters expressed their support with refugees and denounced the Reform Party.

On 22 April 2026, 14 teachers and NEU members staged an hour-long walk out of Hessle Primary School and set up a picket outside the school in Hessle (England), as part of a protest against health and safety concerns. Teachers spoke of being subjected to verbal and physical assault from students at the school.

On 9 May 2026, in the morning, at the call of Stand Up To Racism, hundreds of protesters and anti-racism activists marched in Glasgow (Scotland) as part of a unity march and rally against the far-right Reform UK party, following their successful results in local elections two days prior. Two Reform party candidates had been elected to Scottish Parliament for the Glasgow region, and 17 across Scotland in total. Protesters expressed support for minority groups, such as migrants.

On 11 May 2026, in the morning, at the call of the Trades Union Congress, Unite the Union and the General, Municipal and Boilermakers Union (GMB), residents gathered outside of the Civic Offices in Sir Nigel Gresley Square in Doncaster (England) ahead of a meeting regarding plans to re-open Doncaster Sheffield Airport. Protesters spoke in support of the project, which they claimed would create employment opportunities and boost the region's economy.

On 16 May 2026, at the call of Tommy Robinson (a far-right activist affiliated with the Advance UK party), 60,000 people, including UKIP leader Nick Tenconi and Polish MEP Dominik Tarczynski (ECR), gathered in Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) as part of the Unite the Kingdom rally, a far-right and nationalist protest. Protesters insulted Prime Minister Keir Starmer, carried union flags and wooden crosses, wore red hats labeled 'Make England Great Again,' and chanted pro-Christian and anti-immigration messages. Simultaneously, at the call of Stand Up To Racism and other pro-Palestinian groups, between 20,000 and 200,000 protesters, including Labor MPs Apsana Begum and Diane Abbott, Your Party MP Zara Sultana, Former Leader of the Labor Party and MP Jeremy Corbyn and the General Secretary of the National Education Union, held a counter-protest in Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) against the Unite the Kingdom rally and to commemorate the Palestinian Nakba, expressing solidarity with Palestine and Palestinian hostages, and with anti-Trump and anti-Nigel Farage messages. Police arrested 43 people in both protests, at least 20 arrests were tied to the Unite the Kingdom rally and at least 12 arrests were tied to the counter-protest. Four police officers were assaulted and six were subjected to hate crime offences across both events.

On 14 October 2019, residents from nearby villages protested at Skala Sykamineas in Lesvos by symbolically throwing rocks at humanitarian vessel Open Arms and preventing it from docking. The vessel with 100 refugees and migrants on board from rescue missions in the Meditarrenean remained anchored at around 200 meters from the coast.

On 15 November 2019, members of the Pancyprian Unified Student Organisation protested outside the Turkish consulate in Thessaloniki over the 36th anniversary of the unilateral 'declaration of the pseudo-state in Cyprus' by lighting up the letters 'I don't forget'. They also shouted 'Cyprus is Greek' and slogans for Katsifas. This is part of the three-day anti-occupation events in Thessaloniki. Members of another three Cypriot student political parties marched in the city.

On 18 January 2020, just after midnight, members of Rouvikonas scattered fliers at the home of the German Ambassador in Athens and shouted slogans against the European policy of closed borders for refugees, which resulted in hundreds of deaths in the Aegean sea.

On 22 January 2020, around 7,000 local residents, business owners and officials have launched a day of protest on Lesvos, one of the Greek islands hardest hit by migration. The protesters staged a general strike, shutting down shops and public services and rallied in Mytilene at the island's main port, many waving Greek flags and demanding solutions both for migrants and local communities that have seen their islands turn into detention hubs. Members of KKE held a separate demonstration.

On 31 January 2020, on the day an updated defense agreement with the United States was approved in Parliament, tens of members of the Larissa Committee for Peace participated in a rally and march in Larissa to protest for the cancellation of the agreement and for the removal of NATO and U.S. bases from Greece.

On 4 April 2020, approximately 100 Christian Orthodox Romani rallied outside their closed church in the suburb of Agia Varvara in Athens - West Athens singing hymns and protesting against the government's restrictions due to the coronavirus. Police was called by nearby residents, arrested 1 individual and opened an investigation for identifying as many protesters as possible, who violated the ban on gatherings.

On 13 May 2020, tens of teachers and students protested in Heraklion against a law amendment allowing the video recording of class lectures to assist with remote attendance due to the coronavirus pandemic and generally against the government's education reforms.

On 14 May 2020, employees of a Mining and Metallurgical company in financial hardship supported by GSEE and representatives of members of parliament rallied at the company's offices in Athens to protest against dismissals.

On 17 May 2020, about 150 anarchists clashed with MAT riot police at the end of a demonstration march in Thessaloniki against police intervention the previous night in a city square breaking up a large gathering after complaints by the residents. The rioters damaged parked vehicles, set fire to garbage bins and hurled stones and about 20 petrol bombs at police, who responded with tear gas and stun grenades. Ten people were detained briefly.

On 6 September 2020, protesters against a regulation obliging children to wear face masks when they return to school as part of the government's coronavirus measures rallied in Kalampaka. The protesters, who were holding Greek national flags and comprised of a diverse crowd including parents, members of the anti-vaccine movement and Orthodox Christian religious groups organised in social media, stamped on face masks and burned them, while chanting slogans against the Prime Minister.

On 10 September 2020, hundreds of employees in the culture sector that has been hit hard due to the coronavirus pandemic marched to the Prime Minister's office in Athens-Central Athens participating in a musical protest to demand support.

On 29 September 2020, members of KKE and the Chania Committee for Peace, and members of Marxist group NAR-nKA protested in Chania with the main slogan 'Pompeo go home' during the visit of the US Secretary of State in Crete, where there is a US/NATO base in Souda. The protesters demanded that US and NATO bases leave Greece and that Greece does not participate in any NATO military operations.
On 7 October 2020, on the morning of the court ruling of the marathon trial of Golden Dawn members and leadership accused of running a criminal organisation, protesters in Florina demanded justice.

On Sept. 23, 2018: A group of around 20 or 30 people entered a church on Asklipiou Street in central Athens on Sunday morning and shouted slogans during mass. The act was claimed by anti establishment group Rouvikonas, declaring solidarity with members of a nearby homeless shelter.

On 3 October 2018, the Greek civil servants' union (ADEDY) demonstrated in Athens - Central Athens against government plans to abolish the benefits and status of unhealthy professions. A group of 30 demonstrators stormed the Finance Ministry demanding to meet with the Finance Minister to discuss the issue.

On 2 February 2021, about 20 anarchists threw flyers with slogans in support of Dimitris Koufodinas, a convicted member of November 17 who went on hunger strike to protest his transfer from a rural prison into a regular one, outside the house of the Supreme Court President in Athens - South Athens. The protesters also unfurled a banner and then fled.

On 30 January 2021, members of Golden Dawn organized a nationalist rally in Athens - Central Athens, defying Covid-19 restrictions on mass gatherings, on the anniversary of the Imia crisis. The protesters were holding a large banner reading 'against everyone' likely protesting against the jailing of their leadership following a lengthy trial, which concluded in October 2020 and found the leaders of far-right Golden Dawn guilty of running a criminal organization.

On Oct. 28, 2018: Greek citizens protested against the name change deal signed by Greece and Macedonia in July, shouting 'Macedonia is Greek' at the annual military parade commemorating Greece's entry into World War II in Thessaloniki.

On 7 March 2021, following a routine police inspection in Nea Smyrni square in Athens - South Athens during which a family was fined for defying coronavirus measures, a DIAS police officer used a collapsible steel baton on one of the demonstrators that rallied to support the family. Police claimed 30 people attacked them, 2 officers were injured, and they called for DIAS and OPKE reinforcements. Demonstrators claimed they were 12-13 people demonstrating peacefully. There were 11 detentions. The police officer was suspended and an administrative inquiry was launched. On 4 July 2023, an Athens court convicted the police officer for torturing a civilian and a second police officer as an accessory. A third police officer was cleared of accessory charges.

On 30 March 2021, health workers at 3 major Athens hospitals and members of POEDIN clashed with MAT riot police outside the Ministry of Health in Athens - Central Athens during a demonstration over the dismissal of a doctor. The demonstrators started pounding at the building's security shutters and police responded with tear gas.

Around 2 June 2021 (as reported), demonstrators rallied at Nafpaktos port to protest over the beating of a homosexual man outside his home with the slogan 'austerity, unemployment, sexism, capitalism can not become human'.

On 22 July 2021, in the morning, members of the Association of Greek Archaeologists (SEA) rallied in Thessaloniki for the preservation of the antiquities discovered at Venizelou metro station, which was under construction, at their original setting, rather than removing them off site during construction works. SYRIZA MPs and regional and local councilors of SYRIZA and Laiki Sispirosi participated in the protest. Later in the day, protesters organized by the Citizens' Movement for the Protection of Cultural Heritage, including members of the Music Association of Northern Greece, participated in a musical protest and formed a human chain around the metro station, also demanding the construction of the station without removing the antiquities.

On 28 July 2021, members of Ieros Loxos 2012 marched in Thessaloniki against mandatory coronavirus vaccination and against coronavirus vaccination certificates holding banners and shouting slogans. Many of the slogans were in support of Macedonia being Greek.

On 26 July 2021, hospital employees supported by OENGE rallied outside the Ministry of Health in Athens - Central Athens to protest against the government's decision to make coronavirus vaccination mandatory for all health and care workers.

On 2 September 2021, health care workers rallied outside the Ministry of Macedonia and Thrace in Thessaloniki to protest against mandatory coronavirus vaccination in their sector, following a third surge of coronavirus infections in the country and the suspension of about 6,000 unvaccinated frontline health workers as of 1 September. The demonstrators were organized by POEDIN, which called a Panhellenic strike-protest.

On 7 September 2021, people queueing to pay their respects to deceased Greek composer and political activist Mikis Theodorakis, whose remains were lying in state at the chapel of the Metropolitan Cathedral in Athens - Central Athens, protested spontaneously as police attempted to close the church as scheduled. Following the protest, police extended the closing time by 1 hour.
On 7 October 2021, on the first anniversary of the conviction of the leadership of Golden Dawn for running a criminal organization, an anti-fascist march took place in Patras.
On Dec.6 2018, a peaceful rally took place in the city of Larissa to commemorate the 10th anniversary of teenager Alexis Grigoropoulos's killing by a police officer in Exarchia.

On Dec.6 2018, a peaceful rally took place in the city of Rethymno to commemorate the 10th anniversary of teenager Alexis Grigoropoulos's killing by a police officer in Exarchia. The rally took place at the City Hall Square.

On 20 January 2022, unvaccinated health workers suspended from their jobs protested against mandatory coronavirus vaccination at a Patras hospital during a visit by the alternate health minister. The protesters unfurled a banner, were holding placards and shouted slogans. They also shouted for the minister to quit.

On 17 January 2022, members of the anti-establishment sector marched in Thessaloniki from the courthouse to the university campus, where they smashed the glass front of the security services in the ground floor of the administration building of the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki. The demonstrators left after they shouted slogans against the state and in solidarity with the anarchists arrested on 15 January.

On 16 January 2022, tens of anti-vaccine demonstrators marched in central Thessaloniki holding Christian symbols, singing the national anthem and shouting slogans against mandatory coronavirus vaccination and the government. They also verbally harassed customers who were displaying their coronavirus certificates before entering shops in the city. Police was observing the demonstration, but did not intervene.

On 10 February 2022, on the seventh day of farmers' protests over growing production costs sparked by price hikes in energy, fertilizers and pesticides among other issues, and following a call by the Panhellenic Roadblocks Committee that was not satisfied with the 7 support measures announced by the government, farmers arrived to protest at the Strofylia junction in Euboea.

On 8 March 2022, thousands of women and other demonstrators marched in Athens - Central Athens on International Women's Day. Protesters, including feminist organizations, labor unions organized by ADEDY and EKA, university students, political parties including SYRIZA, migrants' associations, the LGBTQ+ community and activist musicians The Open Orchestra, marched to Parliament in coordinated blocs throughout the day. Members of the Ukrainian women in Greece marched holding yellow carnations. Protesters chanted slogans in support of women's rights, against the war in Ukraine and called for the reinstitution of the General Secretariat for Equality. The city center was closed to traffic.

On Dec. 15 2018, at 11.30am a solidarity gathering to Gilets Jaunes and march took place in central Athens after a social media call. The political party Popular Unity participated, as well as other organisations of the left. This rally joined the pensioners' march that was also taking place in central Athens. The Syntagma metro station was closed as part of security measures imposed by police, traffic ground to a halt and public transportation schedules were thrown into chaos. These were two of the three demonstrations taking place this Saturday.

On 26 May 2022, in the evening, about 5,000 students, members of anarchist collectives and the wider anti-authoritarian space marched in central Thessaloniki against the introduction of university police outside universities starting patrols in the following weeks. Hooded rioters broke away from the demonstration and smashed shop windows, damaged the windows of a bank branch and ATM machines, and set garbage bins on fire. Traffic was disrupted. No injuries were reported. The clashes then moved to the university campus, where about 1,500 rioters hurled rocks, flares and petrol bombs at riot police, who responded with tear gas and stun grenades. 1 police officer was injured. There were 9 detentions, 3 of which turned into arrests.

On 22 June 2022, health workers marched to the Health Ministry in Athens - Central Athens to protest for staff hiring and to be included in the list of hazardous occupations receiving a bonus. The protesters left a banner and the amount of 2-month wages of a health worker outside parliament. Hospital cleaners also protested against the use of contractors rather than employees and placed their work equipment outside the prime minister's office.
On 14 July 2022, municipality cleaning staff rallied outside Thessaloniki city hall to protest over work related accidents and to demand health and safety equipment.

On 21 September 2022, some 800 people rallied in central Athens - Central Athens and then marched carrying banners on the anniversary of the killing of LGBT rights activist Zak Kostopoulos. Police stopped traffic. The demonstrators also protested over the reactions of the crowd during the killing and the initial media coverage of the event. At the end of the march, the last demonstrators poured red ink over the Syntagma square fountain and hurled paint at the Bank of Greece building. A group of people smashed 1 ATM.

On 17 September 2022, more than 500 students opposing the deployment of the newly established university police OPPI (University Institutions Protection Teams) marched in Athens - Central Athens and clashed with riot police, who did not allow them to block more than one lane on the road. The demonstrators reacted hurling various objects at police, who responded with tear gas.

On 24 February 2018, inmates in Korydallos prison - connected to urban guerrilla and anarchist groups - protested against the transfer of Konstantinos Giagtzoglou back to a penitentiary in Larissa. Giagtzoglou, who was on hunger strike demanding to remain in Korydallos after he had been brought to Athens for a court appearance, was suspected of sending the parcel bombs that seriously injured former prime minister Lucas Papademos in May 2016 and wounded an IMF employee in Paris in March 2016. The inmates allegedly stole keys from the guards, taking over several communal spaces in the facility, but no violence was reported.

On 30 November 2022, refugees protested over the closure of the Elaionas camp in Athens. The remaining 57 refugees, including families with minors attending schools, were removed from the camp in the middle of the school year. The demonstrators also protested that they were informed of the move just one hour before the camp's closure. Police detained some protesters.

On 6 December 2022, about 5,000 members of Thessaloniki's Roma community rallied outside the courthouse accusing police of racism during the arraignment of a police officer who shot and critically injured a Roma teenager. The demonstrators, including the boy's father, held up a banner reading 'It wasn't the gas, it wasn't the money, they shot him because he was Roma'. They set dumpsters on fire and hurled rocks and other objects at riot police, who responded with tear gas. Police circled the boy's father, pushed him on the ground, punched him and dragged him around before he entered the courthouse with his lawyer. There was 1 detention. The demonstrators re-assembled shouting slogans against the police. Traffic was disrupted. The court appearance coincided with the 14th anniversary of the fatal police shooting of teenager Alexis Grigoropoulos.

On 26 January 2019, local authorities and other institutions, as well as the people of Zakynthos, demonstrated because the island's hospital is understaffed. In the wake of deaths because the Emergency Room is not operating due to short staffing, the protesters asked of the government to hire more doctors and nurses and also to provide more ambulances as there is only one that is not enough to cover the island's needs.

On 26 March 2023, tens of citizens of Kastoria headed by officials including the mayor of Kastoria (independent politician with the local party 'ora gia douleia'), leaders of the Jewish community, local MPs of New Democracy and SYRIZA and the German consul in Thessaloniki, marched to commemorate the members of the local Jewish community, who were killed in Auschwitz, and to protest against Nazism.

On 8 April 2023, members of the civil society collective Menoume Energoi protested on the Acropolis Hill in Athens - Central Athens, unfurling a giant banner in solidarity with a 12-year-old girl, who had been sexually abused and procured to prostitution. Police detained 4 protesters.

On 23 April 2023, about 500 protesters marched on the Vryzes to Pyrgaki path on Mount Oeta to protest against the imminent installation of five wind farms on the mountain's highest peaks. The plan was opposed by the Regional Authority of Central Greece, the municipal councils of Lamia and Delphi, as well as local communities, civil society, hiking, nature and environmental organizations and associations.

On Jan. 29 2019, further to the previous day's blockades and escalating a series of countrywide farmers' mobilisations protesting for untaxed petrol, a higher ceiling for tax exemption, construction of irrigation and anti-flooding systems among other issues, farmers have blocked the road at the Antigonou junction in Florina.

On 3 August 2023, protesters of the 'Reclaim the beach' movement rallied on Mykonos island to protest the excessive commercial exploitation of beaches. Private beaches are illegal in Greece, where the constitution stipulates that all coastal strips are state property with guaranteed public access.

On Jan. 31 2019, on the fourth day of the farmers' countrywide mobilisations that are disrupting traffic, the head of the Panhellenic Roadblocks Committee rejected a call to talks from the government as 'insincere'. With regard to cheap diesel, they noted that the government had offered cheap fuel to shipowners, airline owners and the owners of major hotel groups, but not a single euro for farmers. The farmers accused the Minister of Agriculture that none of the issues discussed in their previous meeting was met and that this was the reason for their mobilisation.

On 9 September 2023, during the opening of the 87th Thessaloniki International Fair (TIF), and although the government presentation of the budget and policy program for the year ahead was postponed due to the storm Daniel, thousands of demonstrators participated in their annual protests for labour rights in central Thessaloniki, which was closed to traffic. They also expressed their solidarity with the people of Thessaly. There were 3 separate marches: GSEE, ADEDY, EDOTH and the Labour Center of Thessaloniki, unemployed and pensioners; PAME, students, farmers, health workers, delivery couriers; last, members of the extra-parliamentary left, students, members of anarchist collectives and the wider anti-establishment spectrum. Strong police forces were stationed outside TIF and other central locations.

On 9 October 2023, following Hamas' attack in Israel, Palestinians and members of anarchist collectives, political parties of the extra-parliamentary left and the anti-imperialist movement marched in Thessaloniki to express their solidarity with the Palestinian people.

On 14 October 2023, Palestinians living in Thessaloniki and members of the wider anti-establishment sector marched in central Thessaloniki carrying Palestinian flags and a large banner reading 'Freedom in Palestine' to express their solidarity with the people of Palestine. The march ended outside the Ministry of Macedonia and Thrace.

On 17 October 2023, prisoners of Korydallos protested peacefully over their incarceration conditions and unfurled a banner reading 'the lives of prisoners count'. They then reported that during the night riot police forcefully removed their 6 leaders from their beds without a chance to collect their belongings and transferred them to different prisons around the country.

On 15 November 2023, Roma youths rallied in Kamares and marched in Chalcis carrying banners and lighting flares while shouting slogans, following the fatal shooting of a Roma teenager by an OPKE police officer on 11 November.

On 31 December 2023, members of the Golden Dawn Youth Front rallied at their former offices in Thessaloniki encouraging Golden Dawn's action, following a call on social media. Residents in the area reported to the police the use of torches and far-right symbols. On 17 January 2024, a Thessaloniki prosecutor ordered an investigation that was assigned to the Department for Combating Racist Violence of Thessaloniki's Security Police.

On 28 January 2024, farmers and livestock breeders from 18 villages of the Thessalian plain, organized by the Panhellenic Roadblocks Committee, participated with more than 100 tractors in a rally at the central square of Larissa, where they scattered straw. They demonstrated over high production costs and demanded better compensation payments, among other issues, five months after the devastating storm Daniel. They also called for more farmers to reinforce the main blockade in Platykambos.

On 3 February 2024, students, who were members of Rouvikonas, protested in Pallini outside the home of the Athens Polytechnic (NTUA) rector because he requested police assistance to clear the student occupation of the university's rectorate. The occupying students were opposing the government's draft bill allowing private universities. The protesters scattered fliers, unfurled a banner and wrote slogans on the walls.

On Feb. 9 2019, in an escalation of the countrywide farmers' mobilisations since Jan. 28, farmers from Nikaia blocked traffic on one and later both lanes of the Athens-Thessaloniki highway at the entrance of the Tempi Tunnel, causing traffic to divert to the old national road from 1.30 to 3 p.m. They are mainly protesting against high energy and production costs and high taxation. Their representatives also protested against the government's attitude denying them a meeting and insinuating that they are trying to topple the government.

On 8 February 2024, farmers, livestock breeders and beekeepers of Central Macedonia, protesting over rising production costs, among other issues they said are pertinent to their survival, blocked the national road at Giannitsa for half an hour.

On 8 February 2024, farmers protesting over rising production costs, among other issues they said are pertinent to their survival, rallied at Kastro in Viotia. The general secretary of KKE visited the roadblock.

On 9 February 2024, farmers protesting over rising production costs, among other issues they said are pertinent to their survival, rallied at Kastro in Viotia, where the minister for agriculture arrived to listen to their grievances.

On 12 February 2024, during the night, farmers of Alexandroupoli, who were protesting over rising production costs, among other issues, and were unsuccessful earlier in the day in meeting the agriculture deputy minister, lined-up 50 tractors at the Kipi customs office before midnight.

On Feb. 12 2019, by the end of the second week of the countrywide farmers' mobilisations who have set up 23 roadblocks since Jan. 28, farmers in Naousa blocked in a symbolic protest the national highway of Thessaloniki - Veroia for one hour.

On Feb. 12 2019, by the end of the second week of the countrywide farmers' mobilisations who have set up 23 roadblocks since Jan. 28, farmers from the blockade at Nikaia escalated their protest by blocking for two hours one lane at the junction of Platykambos on the Athens - Thessaloniki highway.

On 28 February 2024, on the 1-year anniversary of the Tempe rail disaster, following a call by ADEDY and the labor center of Patras, and amid accusations of a systematic attempt to obscure the circumstances of the tragedy and cover up responsibilities, public and private sector workers, construction workers, freelancers, pensioners and students, marched in the city demanding justice. They also demanded sufficient wage increases to offset the impact of rising living costs and more hirings. They were joined by farmers of Achaia, who participated in their tractors and other vehicles, driving to the central square of Patras. At the end of the march, demonstrators clashed with police.

On 20 September 2024, hundreds of educators and their supporters marched in Athens - Central Athens to protest against government plans to merge school departments and they demanded the hiring of permanent teaching staff. They also protested against the strong police forces observing their demonstration.

On 27 September 2024, a large crowd carrying banners and placards and shouting slogans, picketed the Byzantine museum in Athens - Central Athens, following a call by the Association of Greek Archaeologists, to protest the government's decision to make the museum available for the wedding reception of the daughter of Constantine Glucksburg, the late former King of Greece.

On 5 November 2024, members of the Palestinian Community of Thessaloniki and other collectives marched in the city to protest in solidarity with the Palestinians. They demanded a stop to the genocide of the Palestinian people and protested for peace in the Middle East.

On 27 December 2024, efood delivery couriers staged a rally in central Athens and participated in a motorcade in central and north Athens to the company's headquarters, during a 24-hour strike for their rights.

On 23 January 2025, during farmers' mobilizations over rising production costs and inadequate infrastructure among other issues, farmers rolled out their tractors in various areas of the Pella region (coded to Edessa). The protesters did not obstruct traffic and police presence was discreet.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Aridaia at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Galaxidi at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Kalavryta at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 17 March 2019, members of PAME and other active labour organisations gathered at the entrance of the Kalamata hotel where the 37th GSEE conference was meant to take place demanding one more time that representatives of employers would not participate. The conference was cancelled.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Sikinos at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.
On 28 January 2025, farmers continued their mobilizations over rising production costs among other issues. Farmers rolled out 14 tractors at the Naousa junction.

On 29 January 2025, hundreds protested in Perama against the establishment of Onassis-funded public schools, linking schools to universities and research centers, that would operate under the Ministry of Education's oversight, and demanded quality education for all students.

On 7 February 2025, farmers, livestock breeders and beekeepers, protesting over rising production costs among other issues, escalated their roadblock mobilizations, demanding a meeting in Karditsa with government representatives. Farmers blocked traffic for 3-hours with 18 tractors at the Gypsochori junction.

On 7 February 2025, farmers, livestock breeders and beekeepers, protesting over rising production costs among other issues, escalated their roadblock mobilizations, demanding a meeting in Karditsa with government representatives. Farmers blocked traffic for 3-hours with 6 agricultural vehicles at Thermi.

On 14 February 2025, following a meeting with the minister of Rural Development and government representatives, farmers remained unsatisfied and decided to continue their mobilizations over rising production costs among other issues. Farmers lined-up their tractors on the side of the road at the Larissa blockade.

On 14 February 2025, following a meeting with the minister of Rural Development and government representatives, farmers remained unsatisfied and decided to continue their mobilizations over rising production costs among other issues. Farmers lined-up their tractors on the side of the road at the Giannitsa blockade.
Around 16 February 2025, the 26th anniversary of the arrest of PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan, PKK supporters marched in Athens in solidarity with their jailed leader.

On 26 March 2019, members of anarchist group Rouvikonas scattered fliers at an Aigaleo branch of the supermarket chain that made headlines because of the contentious letter of a manager to the employees. The group that had warned of actions to follow claimed responsibility on Facebook and said 'We have only just begun'.

On 28 February 2025, on the 2nd anniversary of the Tempe rail disaster and the day after an independent investigation report was released blaming human error, outdated infrastructure and major systemic failures, during a 24-hour general strike, a multitude of protesters rallied in Kymi with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', demanding justice and accountability.

On 25 March 2025, members of student associations in Athens participated in a brief march, carrying a giant banner, at the end of the Independence Day parade in Athens - Central Athens, demanding justice for the victims of the Tempe rail disaster. There was discreet police presence.

On 30 March 2025, on the occasion of the 115th anniversary of the Thessaly revolt, farmers of Thessaly and representatives of farmers from across the country rallied at the monument marking the Kileler Uprising to honor the Thessalian farmers, who lost their lives during the revolt. The rally was organized by the Panhellenic Roadblocks Committee and Federations of Farmers' Associations of Thessaly. The leader of Course of Freedom attended along with the party's representative for agricultural issues. The protesters held speeches demanding state support and called for stronger collective struggle.

On 2 April 2025, fishers, supported by fish merchants, opposing European regulations regarding the way they weigh their catch, which they say is unsanitary in their case and not applicable to small and medium scale fishing, protested in their boats at the port of Piraeus (coded to Coast of Piraeus).

On 9 April 2025, protesters rallied peacefully in Katerini over the high cost of living at the call of labor federations GSEE and ADEDY during a 24-hour nationwide general strike. Unions called for sector-wide collective labor agreements, wage increases and policy measures to ease the housing crisis and inflation pressures, among other demands.
