On 9 April 2026, at the call of The People of Ireland Against Fuel Prices, protesters gathered on the outskirts of Longford town (Longford), calling on the Government to take action against the rising costs of fuel and cap fuel prices. Protesters drove as a convoy along the N4. Sinn Fein activists participated in the protest. The event was part of an ongoing series of nationwide demonstrations across Ireland, which began on 6 April 2026, in response to sharply rising fuel prices and broader cost-of-living pressures.

On 29 July 2020, about 100 people of the 'Enough is Enough' campaign gathered outside the Convention Centre in Dublin to protest against the Government's failure to fully reopen day services for adults with disabilities and for equal treatment.

On 23 September 2020, a group of former Debenhams employees protesting outside of the Limerick store blocked a truck from making a delivery. The group, engaged in a long-running protest since the store's closure in April, demand a satisfactory redundancy package.
On 26 September 2020, at least 3 student protesters with Fridays for Future gathered outside the Dail government buildings in Dublin to protest over climate change.

On 31 March 2021, a group of local residents gathered in Grange to protest in opposition to the Sligo County Council's decision to close a major junction in the area that residents say has been made without consultation with local people.

On 21 August 2021, climate change activists belonging to Extinction Rebellion gathered in central Cork to demand governments take more swift action to try and avoid further environmental disasters, specifically citing projections that Cork itself would be below a rising sea-level by 2050.

On 8 October 2021, between 20,000 and 30,000 people marched through central Dublin to demand that the government-led redressal scheme for those affected by compromised homes built with materials containing Mica, a mineral that can cause cracking and crumbling, cover 100% of costs for repair and rebuilding. Agricultural Minister Charlie McConalogue and Sinn Fein leader Mary Lou McDonald addressed the crowd, pledging the party's commitment to delivering 100% redress to affected households.

On 6 December 2021, unemployment support staff gathered outside offices in Tullamore to protest against changes to the provision of such services made by the Department of Social Welfare that require organisations to turn over 1.9 million euros per annum to tender for contracts to provide the service, ruling out most 'job clubs' which have historically provides the services. This protest was organised by SIPTU. Sean O'Brien, a serving local councillor, was present.

On 20 January 2022, 38 school students walked out of their school to protest in Castleblakeney to call for students graduating in the current academic year to receive the option to either sit exams or receive an accredited grade due to disruption to schooling resulting to coronavirus.
On 5 February 2020, a group of childcare workers gathered in Cork city to protest labour conditions. It was organised by The Early Years Alliance, a campaign supported by SIPTU.

On 14 May 2022, hundreds of protesters, including abortion rights campaigners; gathered outside Leinster House in Dublin to demand the management of a new maternity hospital be entirely secular and prevented from religious influence as the land on which the hospital is planned to be built is owned by the Religious Sisters of Charity, a privately run Catholic organization. Protesters asked the government to buy the land using a Compulsory Purchase Order. A Labour TD was present, as were supporters of the Abortion Rights Campaign.

On 19 May 2022, more than 100 senior citizens, workers and students gathered outside the Dail in Dublin to protest, asking the government to do more to alleviate suffering amid the cost-of-living crisis. This event was organized by the Cost of Living Coalition. In attendance was People Before Profit TD Richard Boyd Barrett.
On 18 June 2022, cost of living activists gathered in Cork to demand government act urgently to address the situation. Solidarity TD Mick Barry addressed the crowd and workers were present.

On 28 June 2022, female asylum seekers staged a protest outside accommodation for asylum seekers in Killarney in opposition to a decision to move a proportion of the current residents to make way for the arrival of male asylum seekers.
On 23 November 2022, tenants facing eviction staged a protest outside Leinster House in Dublin, chanting, 'Homes for need, not for greed'.

On 17 December 2022, several Northern Ireland loyalists, including east Belfast activist Moore Holmes, staged a mock funeral for the Good Friday/Belfast Agreement in front of Leinster House in Dublin to protest against Leo Varadkar once again becoming taoiseach. They accused the Irish government of ignoring the interests of the Northern Ireland Unionists. The protest was organized by Let's Talk Loyalism, the anti-protocol group.
On 21 March 2023, campaigners from Raise the Roof and Forsa gathered outside the Dail in Dublin to protest against the Government's decision to lift the winter eviction ban.

On 22 March 2023, around 30 people from the 'Carlow Says No' group gathered at the Liberty Tree in Carlow to protest against proposed housing plans for Ukrainian refugees. Members of the far-right Irish National Party were also among the protestors. Around the same number of people from the 'Carlow For All' group gathered for a counter-demonstration. Sinn Fein TD Kathleen Funchion and People Before Profit councilor Adrienne Wallace also attended the counter-demonstration.
Around 18 March 2023 (as reported), residents gathered in Piltown to protest the plan for installing an 18-meter 5G mobile phone mast in the area, citing health concerns due to a lack of tests.
On 2 April 2023, residents held a demonstration in Union Hall against Cork County Council's plan to close off Keelbeg Pier due to health and safety concerns.

On 8 May 2026, in the afternoon, retired employees of An Post, the state-owned postal service, protested in Longford (Ireland) against a cap on pension increases. Protesters called for the cap to be removed to allow for fairer pension increases.

On 23 June 2023, some 200 residents gathered at the Library Plaza in Charleville (Cork) to highlight the need for immediate road safety measures in the town center after eight pedestrians died in the town in the last ten years.
On 24 October 2023, people demonstrated in Isafjordur to protest continued unequal pay and gender-based violence. The demonstration was held in support of a one-day national women's strike.

On 9 March 2020, around 50 members of the Efling trade union gathered in a protest rally in Reykjavik, as part of ongoing negotiations between the trade union and the city of Reykjavik for a collective bargaining agreement.
On 3 June 2020, about 100 people gathered in Isafjordur for a Black Lives Matter solidarity protest, sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.
On 20 April 2024, people demonstrated in Reykjavik to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine amid the Israeli offensive in Gaza.

On 18 September 2024, people gathered outside the Ministry of Health in Reykjavik to draw attention to the poor state of health care in Gaza and to the possible deportation of a disabled Palestinian child whose family previously sought protection in Iceland.

On 5 October 2024, people demonstrated in front of the US embassy in Reykjavik, calling on the US authorities to step up their efforts to achieve a permanent ceasefire in Gaza and stop escalation in the Middle East. During the demonstration, the embassy building was splashed with red paint. There was a minor scuffle between the demonstrators and the police, but no arrests were made. The demonstration was organized by the Iceland-Palestine Association.

On 18 January 2024, people gathered outside of the Icelandic Public broadcaster office in Reykjavik calling for the disqualification of Israel from Eurovision 2024 in relation with the Israel-Gaza conflict.

On 14 July 2025, people demonstrated outside of the Parliament of Iceland in Reykjavik to protest the visit of Ursula von der Leyen and condemn perceived complicity of European and Icelandic authorities in the perceived genocide in Gaza. The event was organized by the Iceland-Palestine Association.

On 30 March 2020, a group of inmates from the Rebibbia prison staged a peaceful protest at the facility in Rome - Ponte Mammolo (Roma, Lazio) over the delays in responding to their requests for home detention.

On 1 April 2020, prisoners held in Napoli's Poggioreale prison (Napoli, Campania) staged a protest flash-mob, hitting the bars of their cells with pieces of cutlery and pots. Protesters asked for amnesty and pardon, claiming that their condition makes them particularly vulnerable concerning the exposure to coronavirus.

On 3 July 2021, around 30,000 LGBT activists gathered in Bologna to protest in support of LGBT rights and against discrimination. They claimed that the approval of the Zan Law, which criminalizes violence and hate speech against LGBT people was not enough. Non Una Di Meno took part in the organization of the demonstration.

On 2 July 2021, a little less than 100 people, including members of the LGBT community and students, took part in a pride gathering organized by the local High School Students' Network section in Maggiore square in Feltre (Belluno, Veneto). They gathered to denounce all forms of discrimination based on sexual orientation.

On 6 July 2021, about a dozen mayors, the leader of Libera and two PD party figures, including the Torino mayoral candidate, gathered outside the Lascaris Palace, the seat of the Piemonte Regional Council, in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against a new regional gambling bill proposed by center-right majority councilors and denounce their alleged intention to fast-track its approval, canceling the amendments of the opposition. The new law would reportedly repeal a 2016 regional law imposing a 500-meter distance between gambling facilities and churches, schools, ATMs and hospitals.

On 4 July 2021, people gathered on their boats with red ribbons off the coast of Policoro (Matera, Basilicata) to protest against violence against women under the banner '10,000 sails of solidarity'. LNI (Italian Naval League) and Pangea onlus organized the demonstration.

On 5 July 2021, at the call of climate and social justice activists, people gathered outside a branch of the Intesa San Paolo group in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to protest against the bank's involvement in financing the fossil fuel industry and to denounce the upcoming G20 of Economics and Finance in Venice. Demonstrators criticized the financial system's role in environmental degradation and social inequality, calling for wealth redistribution, public welfare, and environmental justice. The action was part of a coordinated series of protests in several Italian cities ahead of the G20 summit.

On 14 July 2021, between 100 and 200 NGOs, among them AI, Article 21, Refugees Movement, MSF, Caritas, took part in a demonstration outside the Parliament in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio). They protested against the renewal of the agreement between the Italian and Libyan authorities over the management of the flows of migrants. They demanded not to support the Libyan authorities and the Italian mission in Libya.
On 13 July 2021, during the evening, around 60 people, among them a council member, gathered at the Ancona seaport to demand to reopen the seaport to bikes, skateboards, and scooters.

On 9 July 2021, residents took to the street in the Castelluccia fraction of Marino (coded as Marino, Roma, Lazio) to protest against the announced installation of a mobile phone mast in the area and denounce the alleged lack of consultations with the public.

On 27 July 2021, around 1,000 people, including I Open affiliates, an actor, restaurateurs, self-employed workers, New Force and other far-right activists, gathered in Del Popolo square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the government's decision to introduce restrictions on people not vaccinated against coronavirus and denounce compulsory vaccination. Protesters, some of whom likened journalists to 'terrorists' and pushed one covering the event, sought to launch a procession but were fended off by police cordons at various points.

On 15 April 2020, a group of activists belonging to a Neighborhood Committee staged a protest in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) at the headquarters of the Confraternity of Pilgrims. People residing in the houses that belong to that confraternity were asked to pay rent, which increased over the years, despite the economic difficulties caused by the coronavirus. Protesters aimed at raising people's awareness of this problem.

On 11 January 2020, dozens of protester took part in a demonstration in San Bonifacio (Verona, Veneto) to complain about long waiting lists at the local hospital and to underline the importance of adequately managing public healthcare. The demonstration was organized by the defense committee of the Fracastoro hospital.

On 28 August 2021, people gathered in Castelfranco Veneto (Treviso, Veneto), to express solidarity with the Afghan population hit by the takeover of Afghanistan by the Taliban. Demonstrators highlighted that Castelfranco is a welcoming town. Libera, ANPI, the Non Una di Meno movement, students, charity associations, the Male Female Horizon feminist movement (Orizzonte Maschile Femminile), Catholic and Muslim communities took part in the demonstration.

On 31 July 2021, over 400 people gathered in Martiri square in Reggio Emilia (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against the introduction of a mandatory 'green pass', a coronavirus measure to access public venues, facilities, or events.
On 31 July 2021, people gathered in Campobasso to protest against the introduction of a mandatory 'green pass', a coronavirus measure to access public venues, facilities, or events.

On 12 August 2021, people, including artists, activists and local administrators, gathered, at the call of the '9 August Let's Save the Chiese River' ('9 Agosto Salviamo il fiume Chiese') committee, outside the Prefecture, in Broletto square, in Brescia (Brescia, Lombardia) to protest against the decision to build a purification system on the Brescia side of Lake Garda. People were reportedly gathering for the fourth day.

On 29 April 2020, a group of storekeepers' representatives handed over the keys of their businesses to the local mayor in Florence (Florence, Toscana) in a symbolic gesture to protest against the government's measures implemented to contain the coronavirus.

On 9 September 2021, a group of Jotassassina activists unrolled a large rainbow flag from a balcony of a building in Ponterosso square in Trieste (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to protest against the FdI leader's, who was simultaneously taking part in a municipal campaign political meeting in the square, position on LGBT rights and specifically on the 'Zan Law', a bill set to criminalize violence and hate speech against LGBT people.

On 6 September 2021, Montessori elementary school students and their parents peacefully occupied the colonnade of the town hall (Ca' Farsetti) in Venezia (Venezia, Veneto) to protest against the alleged closure of their school's first grade.

On 7 September 2021, Riello S.p.A. metal construction workers gathered, with the support of the UILM (UIL) trade union branch, for the second consecutive day outside their workplace in the Villanova fraction of Cepagatti (Pescara, Abruzzo) to protest against the announced closure of their factory and the layoffs and workforce transfers entailed.

Around 19 September 2021 (as reported), Greenpeace activists staged a flash mob in Rome (Roma, Lazio) to mark European Mobility Week with the 'ParkingDay' initiative. They occupied a car park and redesigned it into a relaxing and sociable area. They asked mayoral candidates to reduce the presence of cars and create a more sustainable system.

On 24 September 2021, before dawn, Nexive shipping company workers staged, with the support of the S.I. COBAS trade union, a picket outside the Italian postal service company's Postal Mechanographic Center (CMP) in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against the potential closure of the Nexive center in Calderara di Reno and demand that all its workers be incorporated into the CMP following the Italian postal service company's purchase of Nexive in December 2020.

On 24 September 2021, people, including FFF activists, took to the streets in Modena (Modena, Emilia-Romagna) to call for more climate action. The event was part of an international Climate Strike day called by the FFF movement.

On 24 September 2021, over 200 striking Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) workers gathered, at the call of the FABI, FISAC CGIL, UILCA (UIL), FIRST CISL and UNISIN unions, outside MPS offices, in Fontana square, in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against uncertainties regarding their professional future. The event was part of a national day of strike and protest called by MPS unions.

On 24 September 2021, school students gathered outside the town hall of Ponsacco (Pisa, Toscana) to protest against climate change. The event was reportedly part of an international Climate Strike day called by the FFF movement.

On 29 September 2021, people gathered, with the support of CGIL and RSU, outside Santa Maria delle Stelle Hospital in Melzo (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the alleged closure of the facility's psychiatric department and denounce the impact on local healthcare services.

On 25 September 2021, between 3,000 (according to the police) and 100,000 (according to the organizers) people gathered in San Giovanni Square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to demonstrate against the 'green pass', a coronavirus measure to access schools and the workplace. They shouted 'Freedom'. A Vice Police Commissioner gave a speech during the protest. Ancora Italia, 3V Movement, No Paura Day, Primum Non Nocere, FISI, and Fronte del Dissenso organized the demonstration. Far-right and Neofascist groups took part in the protest. At the end of the event, a group of protesters started an unauthorized protest march. The police stopped the march and reported at least a dozen people for unauthorized demonstration and roadblock. Disciplinary action was taken against the Vice Police Commissioner.

On 28 September 2021, supporters of a referendum on the legalization of cannabis gathered outside the Valle d'Aosta Region headquarters in Aosta (Aosta, Valle d'Aosta) to call on municipal authorities across the region to send their electoral certificates of the signatures collected for the referendum by 30 September 2021.

On 7 October 2021, Pascali artistic high school students gathered outside their school in Bari (Bari, Puglia) to protest against coronavirus-induced double-entry shifts and denounce the inconveniences allegedly entailed.

On 2 October 2021, around 1,000 people took to the streets in Modena to protest against the green pass, a coronavirus measure to access public venues and the workplace. They criticized the government.

On 1 October 2021, many people, including associations' representatives and residents, gathered in Prampolini square in Reggio Emilia (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to protest in solidarity with the former, pro-refugee mayor of Riace, who was recently sentenced to 13 years of prison in the first instance for abetting illegal migration.

On 10 October 2021, people, among them CGIL members, gathered in Gravina in Puglia (Bari, Puglia) to guard the CGIL branch in protest against the far-right assault on the union's headquarters in Rome.
On 9 October 2021, people, among them CGIL members, gathered in Piacenza to guard the CGIL branch in protest against the far-right assault on the union's headquarters in Rome.

On 11 October 2021, several hundred workers, among them teachers, gathered in Palermo at the call of COBAS, CUB, USB, SGB, and USI-CIT to protest against the Government's job policies in response to the coronavirus pandemic. They demanded a stop to layoffs and job insecurity. They also demonstrated against the introduction of a mandatory green pass for working.

On 2 May 2020, members of the newly-born movement Tricolor Masks gathered in Vittorio Veneto square in Perugia (Perugia, Umbria) to protest against the 'healthcare dictatorship' allegedly imposed by the Italian government to contain the spread of coronavirus. The event was part of a national day of protest which occurred in 66 other localities across the country.

On 15 October 2021, hundreds of people, including local workers, took to the streets of Monfalcone (Gorizia, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to protest against the extension of coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions to public and private sector workers, set to come into force on that day.

On 11 October 2021, students gathered in Cagliari to demand a safe return to school and to oppose the new school reform. They also demonstrated against overcrowded classes and public transport. FGC took part in the event.

On 11 October 2021, in the evening, people gathered outside Prato city hall to demand the municipality to intervene over an attack that happened earlier that day [coded as another event] against some workers protesting for the exploitative conditions they were subjected to.

On 20 October 2021, Cerutti workers gathered, with the support of the FIOM CGIL union branch, for the last day of picketing outside their company's gates in Casale Monferrato (Alessandria, Piemonte) to protest against the liquidation of their production unit and its takeover by a third-party company, demanding the reintegration of most of its workers. They had reportedly been protesting for 250 days.

On 22 October 2021, FFF affiliates and students gathered in Giannella square and staged a 'bike strike' through the streets of Bari (Bari, Puglia) to call for more climate action. The event was part of an international Climate Strike day called by the FFF movement.

On 21 October 2021, in the evening, people, including councilors of Milano's 5th Municipality, gathered for a vigil at the Giardino Segreto park, near Dei Missaglia street, in Milano - Municipio 5 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the killing of a small dog recently killed by an Amstaff dog reportedly belonging to two squatters of the public park and demand that more security guarantees be given by public authorities.

On 15 October 2021, about 15 Technogym workers gathered outside their workplace in Cesena (Forli-Cesena, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against the adoption, by their company, of the extension of coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions to all workplaces, a governmental measure set to come into effect on that day.

On 18 October 2021, around 300 No Green Pass activists took to the streets in Milano for an unauthorized demonstration to support Trieste dockworkers protest against the mandatory green pass, a coronavirus measure to access the workplace.

On 16 October 2021, people took to the streets in Cagliari to protest against the mandatory green pass, a coronavirus measure to access the workplace. They also supported the Trieste dockworkers protest.

On 18 October 2021, over 100 people gathered in Garibaldi Square in Cagliari to support the Trieste dockworkers demonstration and protest against the mandatory green pass, a coronavirus measure to access the workplace.

On 29 October 2021, workers and CGIL, CISL and UIL delegates gathered outside the Prefecture in Modena (Modena, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against work-related deaths and demand more security guarantees for workers.

On 23 October 2021, a few hundred people gathered in Castello Square in Torino to support the Trieste dockworkers' demonstration and protest against the mandatory green pass, a coronavirus measure to access the workplace. The demonstrators criticized a TV crew and pushed it out. No physical contact was reported.
On 13 October 2021, SPI CGIL, FNP CISL and UR UILP (UIL) pensioners' union delegates protested in Nuoro (Nuoro, Sardegna). They asked for better local access to healthcare services.

On 4 May 2020, markets' vendors who sell non-food products staged a protest outside the offices of the regional administration in Torino (Torino, Piemonte). Protesters criticized institutions for having given little attention to their sector and asked for measures aimed at supporting them in handling the consequences of the coronavirus emergency.
On 30 October 2021, people, among them Arcigay, gathered in Lecce to protest against the Senate's rejection of the 'Zan Law', a bill to criminalize violence and hate speech against LGBT people.

On 2 November 2021, around 200 people, including PRC, M5S, SI, ANPI and ARCI members, gathered in Duomo square in Pistoia (Pistoia, Toscana) to protest against the simultaneous visit by the President of Brazil of a local monument commemorating Brazilian soldiers who died during the WWII Italian campaign.

On 4 May 2020, around 350 people took part in a demonstration organized in Grado (Gorizia, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) by tourist operators, who are concerned about the future of the sector due to the consequences of the coronavirus emergency.

On 6 November 2021, hundreds of people took to the streets in Riace (Reggio di Calabria, Calabria) to protest in support of the former, pro-refugee mayor of Riace, who was sentenced to 13 years of prison for abetting illegal migration. Mayors from the area, the former Mayor of Napoli, a journalist, and a priest took part in the demonstration.

On 11 November 2021, in the afternoon, metalworkers subcontracted by Stellantis gathered, with the support of CGIL, CISL and UIL delegates, outside their factory in Melfi (Potenza, Basilicata) to demand guarantees for their future in the wake of the coronavirus pandemic.

On 6 November 2021, people, among them FN activists, gathered in Roma Square in Catania to protest against the green pass, a mandatory coronavirus measure to access the workplace. They claimed they were under a 'healthcare dictatorship'
On 14 November 2021, dozens of people gathered in Rome (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the dismissal of a case concerning the disappearance of a kid 17 years ago.

On 24 November 2021, cab drivers gathered in various locations across Imperia (Imperia, Liguria) to protest against the government's competition bill, citing deregulation proposals that would favor multinationals against small independent drivers. The event was part of a national day of strike and protest called by several sector's unions, including UGL Taxi, Federtaxi CISAL, TAM, SATAM, CLAAI, Unimpresa, USB Taxi, Or.S.A Taxi, ATI TAXI, FAST CONFSAL and 'Taxi Legal Protection Association' ('Associazione Tutela Legale Taxi').

On 19 November 2021, students took to the streets of Lecco (Lecco, Lombardia) to demand more investments in their future from national authorities. The event was part of a national day of protest called by students' unions.

On 20 November 2021, between 1,000 and 2,000 students and GKN workers took to the streets in Florence (Firenze, Toscana). Students demanded to decide on their future and the school system. GKN workers denounced the uncertainty of their working conditions. Anarchist and communist activists and CGIL Fiom members took part in the demonstration.

On 20 November 2021, people, among them students, gathered in Vedelago (Treviso, Veneto) to protest against violence against women. The demonstration was organized by the anti-violence center and the municipality.
On 20 November 2021, around 1,000 people blocked the traffic in Trento to protest against coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions.

On 1 December 2021, Azzarina (part of IIS Tommaso Salvini) high school students staged an occupation on their school's premises in Rome - Parioli (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the education system and denounce the state of school infrastructure.

On 4 December 2021, between 700 (for the police) and 1,000 people took to the streets in Genova to demonstrate against the coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions. Students Against Green Pass and CUB took part in the demonstration.

On 4 December 2021, around 100 people, among them No Vax activists, gathered in Sempione Square in Milano - Municipio 1 to demonstrate against the coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions. Later dozens of protesters started an unauthorized demonstration in Duomo Square. The police intervened, stopped the demonstration, and identified the protesters.

On 6 December 2021, 5 people put chains along the railway near Meana di Susa (Torino, Piemonte). They showed a banner with 'No Green Pass, We block everything'. A train stopped before hitting the chains. No one was reported injured.

On 13 December 2021, Legambiente activists gathered in Bari to protest against air pollution, especially that produced by diesel trains. The event was organized to mark the Clean Cities Campaign. Some demonstrators wore gas masks.
On 13 December 2021, students of the Bovara high schools gathered outside their school in Lecco to denounce the low heating of the school building.

On 30 December 2021, in the morning, Trotta public transportation workers and union delegates gathered, at the call of FILT CGIL and FIT CISL, outside their company's offices in the Riofreddo area of Potenza (Potenza, Basilicata) to protest against alleged delays in the payment of their salaries and demand the renewal of their contracts.

On 15 December 2021, No TAV Movement activists gathered in Castello square in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against the latest declarations of the city's mayor in favor of the Turin-Lyon high-speed railway (TAV) project. A group of three Si TAV affiliates simultaneously gathered on another side of the square to stage a counter-protest in favor of the mayor's declarations.
On 14 December 2021, Socrate high school students occupied one of their school's buildings in Rome - Ostiense (Roma, Lazio) to denounce the state of the education system.

On 15 December 2021, a small group of Pertini Technical Institute teachers gathered outside their workplace in Carpaccio street in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to protest against the introduction of compulsory vaccination against coronavirus for school personnel and law enforcement workers on that day, citing the alleged anti-constitutional nature of the measure. They were joined by a group of students.

On 12 January 2022, Arco Spedizioni workers gathered for the third consecutive day, supported by ADL COBAS delegates, outside their company, in Inghilterra street, in the industria area of Padua (Padova, Veneto) to demand the stabilization of the ADL COBAS-affiliated workers' contracts.

Around 8 January 2022 (as reported), a wing of the ground floor of the building that housed the placement office in Parma (Parma, Emilia-Romagna) was occupied by homeless people. The property, owned by the Emilia-Romagna region, was for sale.

On 7 January 2022, in the morning, at the call of local civic groups, residents gathered along via Ardeatina outside the Roncigliano landfill in Albano Laziale (Lazio) to block incoming waste trucks and protest the site's continued use. Demonstrators denounced the renewal of an ordinance allowing waste from Rome to be dumped at the landfill, citing years of pollution, environmental harm, and unbearable odors affecting the local population. Protesters demanded the immediate halt of waste deliveries from the capital and the closure of the landfill.
On 21 January 2022, residents of Santa Marina di Salina (Messina, Sicilia) one of the Aeolian Islands, staged a demonstration against the closure of the general practitioner clinic on the island.

On 28 January 2022, in the morning, a few dozen health workers, notably nurses, from across the Friuli-Venezia Giulia region gathered, at the call of the NurSind union, in Liberta square in Trieste (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to protest against the alleged lack of resources of their category and demand a better acknowledgment of their role, notably in light of their activities during the coronavirus pandemic. The event was part of a national day of strike and protest called by health workers' unions.

On 28 January 2022, students took to the streets in Treviso (Treviso, Veneto) to demand more safety and less labor precarity for students and denounce the country's work-study program following the death, of a work accident, of an 18-year-old student from Udine while doing an internship in Lauzacco on 21 January 2022.

On 28 January 2022, Nial Mail workers contracted by the national post office company gathered, at the call of USB Lavoro Privato, outside Poste Italiane offices in Taranto (Taranto, Puglia) to protest against their 'authoritarian management' and demand compliance with their contracts.

On 27 January 2022, about 40 people gathered in front of the Teatro Comunale opera house in Belluno (Belluno, Veneto) to protest against coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions. Demonstrators bore signs likening restrictions and vaccine mandates to the persecution of Jews during World War II. The event received criticism from public institutions for being organized while a concert was being staged in the opera house to commemorate International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

On 23 January 2022, around 40 anarchists protested in Trento (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) against a drill installed a few days before. Two persons attempted to sabotage the said drill, but the police physically stopped them.

On 27 January 2022, in the evening, animal rights activists affiliated with 100% Animalisti and the 'Animalist Front' ('Fronte Animalista') gathered outside the Aptuit experimental center in Verona (Verona, Veneto), waving flares, throwing toilet paper rolls over the facility's gates and hanging a banner at the entrance, to protest against the alleged use of beagle puppies for pharmaceutical testing at the facility.

On 29 January 2022, people gathered, at the call of CPI, in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to protest against the government's coronavirus-related measures and denounce its alleged inability to curb rising costs. The event was part of a national day of protest called by CPI and dubbed 'Draghi Go Away' ('Draghi Vattene').

On 29 January 2022, people gathered, at the call of CPI, in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the government's coronavirus-related measures and denounce its alleged inability to curb rising costs. The event was part of a national day of protest called by CPI and dubbed 'Draghi Go Away' ('Draghi Vattene').

On 29 January 2022, in the afternoon, 'No Green Pass' advocates and a journalist and 'eco-pacifist' activist gathered near the Resistance Monument in Carducci street in Cesena (Forli-Cesena, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against coronavirus vaccines, deemed a profit-driven business, and their advocacy by the Italian government.

On 31 January 2022, Coopbox workers occupied their workplace in Ferrandina (Matera, Basilicata) to protest against the announced shutdown of their factory and denounce the 50 dismissals it would entail.

On 27 January 2022, 'No Vax' advocates staged a leafleting protest outside schools in Livenza street and Iberati street in Portogruaro (Venezia, Veneto) to denounce coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions. On 15 March 2024, about 40 students demonstrated outside the Fuorigrotta seat of the Federico II University in Napoli (Campania) against an event featuring Repubblica's Director Maurizio Molinari and against relations between the University and the Israeli government. The demonstration started as a peaceful event but turned violent as students clashed with police officers and made their way inside the University, causing the suspension of the event.

On 20 March 2024, between 100 and 300 students, including some affiliated with CUA and CR, gathered in Verdi Square in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) during the inaugural ceremony of the academic year, expressing solidarity with Palestine, calling for the interruption of all academic agreements with Israel, and demanding that the University of Bologna take a stand against what they defined as a 'genocide' in the Gaza Strip. Students reached Indipendenza Street, where some threw objects at the police, who charged them to disperse the gathering, clubbing some of its participants. Some participants later reached Zamboni Street, where they entered the University of Bologna Rector's office and wrote 'UniBo accomplice' on a wall.

On 23 March 2024, members of the movement 'Free All Antifas' threw smoke bombs inside the Carrefour supermarket in Dei Sabelli Street in Roma - Tiburtino (Lazio) to express solidarity with Ilaria Salis and Gabriele Marchesi, two anti-fascist activists arrested in Budapest on suspicion of a serious assault on two far-right supporters at Hungary's Day of Honour commemorations. Protesters threw red paint on the entrance and held a banner with the words 'neither prison nor extradition'. Zaum collective was present.

On 23 March 2024, 3,000 people took to the streets in Savona (Liguria) to protest against the construction of a gasifier. The mayors of Savona (civic list), Bergeggi (civic list), Albissola Marina (no political affiliation reported), Quiliano (civic list), and Altare (civic list) were present.

On 30 March 2024, at the call of CGIL, CISL and UIL, large-scale retail workers of Federdistribuzione staged a protest in front of a shopping center in Lionello Street in Castel Giubileo (Lazio) against the non-renewal of their company's collective labor agreement, which, according to protesters, would worsen workers' conditions.

On 5 April 2024, at the call of CGIL, CISL and UIL, around 200 dock workers gathered in Monfalcone (Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to protest against the blocking of negotiations for the renewal of the collective agreement, asking for better working conditions, including an 18% salary increase. Various local and regional politicians, including members of PD, were present.

On 15 April 2024, at the call of the New Autonomous Federation of Trentino Workers (Fe.N.A.L.T. - Nuova Federazione Autonoma dei Lavoratori del Trentino), senior care workers staged a protest under the headquarters of the health department in Trento (Trentino-Alto Adige) against their working conditions, including excessive workloads and exhausting shifts due to staff shortages.

On 20 April 2024, at the call of 'Let's Save the Land' (Salviamo il Suolo), members of several local associations and committees gathered in Caravaggio (Lombardia) for a flash mob against land consumption and the planned construction of a large industrial area in the municipality of Misano Gera d'Adda. Protesters also demanded more climate action. Members of the Lombardy Episcopal Conference were also present.

On 25 April 2024, on the occasion of Liberation Day, hundreds of people, including anti-fascist activists, members of ANPI, CGIL, ARCI, the president of the Region (FI), the mayor (UdC) and other local elected officials, took to the streets of Palermo (Sicilia) to denounce fascism.

On 29 April 2024, at the call of M5S, people staged a protest in front of Chigi Palace in Roma - City Center (Lazio) during the discussion of the differentiated autonomy for regions which, according to protesters, would create major inequalities, especially between the north and the south of Italy. CGIL participated.

On 16 May 2024, at the call of CGIL, CISL, UIL, and UGL, 'Sicilian Transport Agency' (AST: Agenzia Siciliana Trasporti) workers demonstrated outside the seat of the Sicilian Regional Assembly (ARS) in Palermo (Sicilia) to demand competent authorities finalize a law amendment which would allow the recapitalization of AST.

On 22 May 2024, people including farmers and shop owners, staged a protest on the Due Ponti provincial road 588 in Villanova sull'Arda (Emilia-Romagna) against the traffic lights installed to establish the alternate one-way system on the Arda bridge. According to protesters, the measure paralyzed the area and created additional traffic.

On 29 May 2024, as part of an ongoing demonstration, students and pro-Palestinian activists took to the streets of Palermo (Sicilia) to protest against the killing of Palestinian civilians. They marched toward the Rectorate and requested that the Academic Senate cut ties with all Israeli-based Universities, companies, and institutions. Protesters also criticized the Israeli government and The Palermo University authorities.

On 1 June 2024, approximately 100 people, including residents and members of local civil societies such as the No Bridge Network, demonstrated in Messina (Sicilia) against the construction of a bridge across the Strait of Messina. They also criticized Italian Minister of Transports Matteo Salvini, who is in favor of the project and was visiting the city. Demonstrators voiced concerns about the environmental impact of the bridge.

On 1 June 2024, on the sidelines of the rally for the closing of the Lega electoral campaign for the European Parliament, about 50 people, including Antifa activists and pro-Palestinian activists, demonstrated against Lega, fascism, and the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the government of Israel at the corner between the Duomo and Vittorio Emanuele II Boulevard in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia). The police in riot gear prevented them from reaching the Lega event site. Demonstrators then took to the streets of the center to continue their march. About 20 people also gathered near the Lega's info point in Duomo Square to demonstrate against the party and Lega's candidate for the EU Parliament, namely General Roberto Vannacci. Demonstrators also tried to tear down an election poster but were asked to stop by the police. There were no clashes, and the demonstrators left the site immediately.

On 15 June 2024, around 5,000 people, including LGBTQ+ activists, participated in a pride parade in Bergamo (Lombardia). Demonstrators emphasized intersectionality, condemned the practice of gay-washing, and offered attendees services like free HIV testing. Outgoing councilor Marzia Marchesi (PD), PD provincial and city secretaries Gabriele Giudici and Alessandro De Bernardis, provincial councilor Romina Russo (PD), M5S member Vittorio Apicella, members of PD's youth section Young Democrats, and representatives of CGIL were present.

On 18 June 2020, around 100 nurses belonging to trade union NurSind gathered in UnitA square in Trieste (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to claim the bonus promised by the national government and local authorities for having faced the coronavirus emergency on the front line. Protesters put white roses on the ground to remember colleagues deceased due to the coronavirus.
On 24 June 2024, around 200 workers of Abramo Customer Care staged a protest inside the town hall in Crotone (Calabria) against uncertainty and lack of a future for their employment.

On 18 June 2020, relatives of 7 workers of a German multinational company who died during a fire at work in Italy in 2007 staged a protest in front of the Palace of Justice in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) against a ruling regarding the company's two managers. Protesters claimed that the ruling issued in Germany regarding the fire and the deaths is unfair towards the victims.

On 30 June 2024, at the call of the association 'Rights of the Patients' (Diritti del Malato), people, including residents, health workers and administrative workers, staged a flashmob in Udine (Friuli-Venezia Giulia) in support of the public health system. Protesters demanded decent working conditions and salaries for healthcare workers and the protection of patients' rights. Regional councilor Simona Liguori (Civic List) was present.

On 18 June 2020, employees of a fashion company, together with trade unions Femca Cisl and Filctem Cgil, staged a protest outside their firm in Sesto Fiorentino (Florence, Toscana). Protesters demonstrated against the company's decision to shut down the branch in Sesto Fiorentino and to move staff to Milan, and against the lack of clarity about the future of those workers who will accept to be relocated.

On 11 July 2024, at the call of the Union of Italian Criminal Chambers (Unione Camere Penali Italiane), people gathered in Santi Apostoli Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against the phenomenon of suicides and overcrowding in prison. The president of the criminal chambers and various lawyers participated.

On 19 July 2024, at the call of FP CGIL and CISL FP, striking administrative and health workers employed by the 'Citadel of Charity Foundation' (Fondazione Cittadella della Carita) demonstrated in front of the foundation's seat in Taranto (Puglia) to protest against unpaid wages and ongoing financial instability. Representatives of UGL also took part in the demonstration.

On 22 July 2024, over 200 people gathered in Torino (Piemonte) in solidarity with 'La Stampa' journalist Andrea Joly, who was attacked by members of Casa Pound. Demonstrators also protested against violence and demanded the government take a firm stance against far-right groups' violent acts. The demonstration was organized by the Order of Journalists of Piedmont along with the Subalpina, the local journalists' union. Representatives of ANPI, CGIL, UIL, local councilors and members of the M5S, journalists, former mayor of Turin and ex-president of the Piemonte region Sergio Chiamparino, and Andrea Joly himself partook in the demonstration.

On 24 July 2024, at the call of opposition council groups, hundreds of people gathered in Campo Santa Margherita in Venezia (Veneto) to ask for the resignation of the mayor after the arrest of a councilor on 16 July. Trade unions participated.

On 2 August 2024, on the occasion of the 44th anniversary of the bombing of the Bologna Centrale railway station by neo-fascists, thousands of people took to the streets in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to commemorate the event and to ask for truth and justice. Associations, representatives of institutions including the mayor of Bologna (PD), the PD secretary, the Minister of the Interior (Independent), the president in office of Emilia Romagna (PD), the president of the Association of Family Victims of the Massacre, and two candidates for the regional elections (civic list and PD) took part in the event.

On 31 July 2024, at the call of FP CGIL and SILP CGIL, people gathered in Capranica Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against the working conditions of workers in the security sector, asking for a better contract. This event is part of a national demonstration in support of the renewal of the contract for military and law enforcement officers, including police, prison police, Carabinieri and Guardia di Finanza.

On 12 August 2024, dozens of people staged a picket outside the Court in Cagliari (Sardegna), exposing banners and protesting against the management of the renewable energy plants on the island. Protesters stressed their concerns about possible speculation and negative impact on the environment as well.

On 12 September 2024, at the call of the High School Students' Network, students gathered in front of various schools across Basilicata [coded to Potenza (Basilicata)] to protest against planned cuts to education and the implementation of differentiated levels of regional autonomy across Italy.

On 18 September 2024, at the call of the SUDD COBAS trade union, striking Ellebi workers staged a picket outside their factory in Calenzano (Toscana) to protest against the management's decision to fire two workers in July 2024.

On 12 April 2023, NO TAV activists took to the streets in San Didero (Piemonte) to demonstrate against the TAV Turin-Lyon high-speed railway connection project. During the march, activists tore down several meters of barbed wire. The police intervened but no additional information was given in the report.

On 25 September 2024, at the call of CGIL and UIL, people gathered in Reggio Emilia (Emilia-Romagna) to protest against a bill that sanctions protests, occupations and roadblocks (DDL Sicurezza). The event was part of a national mobilization throughout Italy.

On 25 September 2024, at the call of the Union of clinics, polyclinics, institutions and private hospitals (UAP- Unione Ambulatori, Poliambulatori, Enti e Ospedalita privata), people gathered at the Brancaccio theater in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to ask for a permanent discussion table with the government to request more rules and the adaptation of tariff nomenclatures and essential levels of assistance.

On 3 February 2024, about 20 No TAV activists demonstrated in San Didero (Piemonte) by tying expulsion orders issued against some No TAV activists by the police headquarters to balloons and let them fly away to contest the political use of such measures and protest against repression of dissent.
On 22 January 2020, Amtab workers gathered outside the Bari municipality offices to protest against the cut in their salaries if they are on sick leave.

On 9 October 2024, on the occasion of the World and European Day against the Death Penalty, the Iranian community staged a protest in Magenta Street, in front of the headquarters of the Representation in Italy of the Commission and the European Parliament, in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to denounce the repression in the country, with indiscriminate arrests, unfair trials, arbitrary sentences and torture in prison, as well as violations of human rights and discrimination based on ethnicity, language, and religion, as well as against women and the LGBTQ+ community.

On 11 October 2024, FFF activists staged a protest in Santissima Annunziata Square in Firenze (Toscana), calling on regional institutions to take further steps against climate change. Communities involved in renewable energy and local associations took part in the event. Protesters showed photographs of recent environmental disaster and marked the anniversary of the flood of November 2023 in the region.

On 16 October 2024, students from the Art High School walked out of school and staged a picket in Pavia (Lombardia) to protest against new directions requiring them to take recess in class. The students also protested against the current state of the building and the presence of rats, arguing it made eating inside the buildings unsanitary.

Around 1 January 2020 (as reported), protesters, including No TAV activists, gathered in Susa (Torino, Piemonte) in solidarity with a 73-year-old No TAV activist arrested on 30 December 2019 and three other previously arrested No TAV activists.

On 21 June 2020, around 250 Bangladeshi people working in Italy gathered with banners outside the Police Headquarters in Marghera (Venice) to protest against the 'Rilancio Decree', which regulates only specific categories of work. The protesters asked for a generalized regulation.
On 26 June 2022, tenants' unions organized a 'march for housing' in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the housing emergency in the city.

On 15 April 2023, at the call of CGIL, CISL, and UIL, people, including national deputy and PD vice-president Chiara Gribaudo, gathered in Alessandria (Piemonte) to call for the protection of public healthcare.

On 2 April 2023, a few hundred or 500 people, including Rainbow Families members and members of the LGBTQ+ community, as well as the mayors of Bologna (Matteo Lepore, PD) and of San Lazzaro di Savena (Isabella Conti, PD), gathered in Maggiore Square in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to demand LGBTQ+ people's rights be guaranteed, especially in the school and health systems, and the implementation in all schools of the 'Alias career', namely the opportunity to use chosen names in official school documents.

On 16 December 2022, people gathered in Unita d'Italia square in Livorno (Toscana) to protest against the 2023 government's budget bill proposal. Protesters called for a minimum salary, the elimination of all forms of precarious work, the revaluation of pensions and a tax reform that respects the principle of progressivity. The event was part of a national day of strike organized by CGIL and UIL.

Around 20 July 2024 (as reported), prisoners held at the 'Regina Coeli' prison in Roma - City Center (Lazio) protested against the extreme heat in their cells, where temperatures reached up to 40 degrees Celsius, by refusing to go back to their cells.

Around 24 July 2024 (week of), street artists and performers, including professional ones, gathered outside the town hall in Genova (Liguria) to protest against plans by the municipality to introduce an online app to book specific places and times to perform in the street, arguing the move would restrict street performers' activities and create additional problems.
On 22 January 2020, around 100 business owners gathered in Valguarnera Caropepe to protest against the high level of taxation they face.

On 24 October 2024, at the call of Rainbow Families, around 300 people gathered in front of Marino Palace in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to protest against the law that made surrogacy a universal crime. Local associations, the PD group leader in the regional council, various municipal councilors (PD) and the president of municipality (PD) took part in the event.

On 31 October 2024, at the call of UILTUCS, people, including workers and lifeguards, took to the streets of Terracina (Lazio) to protest their working conditions, low wages, the phenomenon of illegal work, and delays in payment of back wages.

On 29 October 2024, around 80 teachers and parents, as well as a local school principal, staged a protest outside the town hall in Ciampino (Lazio) against the municipality's school sizing plan. Protesters expressed concerns about inadequate laboratories and a gymnasium in the new building, as well as difficulties in managing teachers due to the proposed changes, which they believe could jeopardize the future of their educational institutions.

On 21 May 2022, people gathered in Palazzolo sull'Oglio (Lombardia) to protest against the municipality's decision to approve the new General Urban Traffic Plan and make some streets one-way only. Councilors and representatives of FdI and civic lists participated in the protest.

On 4 November 2024, as part of the national demonstration 'Stop Genocide Day', students and members of the university association CUA staged a demonstration outside the university in Padova (Veneto) and exposed banners to protest against the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Protesters also criticized the Italian government and other Western governments for their support of the Israeli government.

On 9 November 2024, people took to the streets in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) in favor of the Palestinian cause and against Israel. Protesters held a banner reading 'Against colonization and apartheid' and waved Palestinian flags. A group of protesters gathered in front of a McDonald's restaurant in Cairoli Street, calling for a boycott of the fast food chain, which they accused of distributing free meals to Israeli soldiers. Two city councilors (PD) participated in the event.

On 15 November 2024, as part of the national demonstration 'No Meloni Day', people, including students, representatives of UDU, the High School Students' Network, the association 'Red Pig' (Porco Rosso), Palestinian and Libyan students, and representatives of several local associations, took to the streets of Perugia (Umbria) to protest against the Italian government, regional authorities, the cutting of funding for public schools, the so-called Security Decree (DDL Sicurezza), which, according to them, would hinder their right to freely protest, the increase in the cost of rentals and public transport, and the killing of Palestinian people by the Israeli military.

On 20 November 2024, people, including affiliates of the far-right group 'Brescia ai Bresciani' (Brescia to Brescians), staged a protest in Cremezzano (Lombardia) to protest plans for opening a reception center for migrants in the area, citing sentiments of neglect and abandonment toward the village.

On 22 November 2024, high school students protested in Matteotti Square in Novara (Piemonte) against the poor conditions of their school infrastructure, including freezing classrooms, crumbling walls, malfunctioning laboratories, and a lack of teaching materials, which they argued compromised education quality.

On 19 November 2024, at the call of CUA, students demonstrated in Padova (Veneto) against the government's policies regarding schools and universities. Demonstrators also criticized the Israeli government and protested against the killing of Palestinian civilians. Representatives of the students association 'DiSll Collective' and CORDA - Researchers, Undergraduates, and Research Fellows Coordination (Coordinamento Ricercatori, Dottorandi e Assegnasti) participated in the protest.

On 29 November 2024, a large group of Boccardi-Tiberio High School students demonstrated outside their school in Termoli (Molise) to protest against the merger between the Boccardi-Tiberio High School and another High School in the city.

On 29 November 2024, on the occasion of the general strike organized by CGIL and UIL, between 900 and 1,000 people, including workers, took to the streets of Rovigo (Veneto) to protest against the Meloni government and the 2025 Budget Law. Local representatives of AVS and PD participated in the protest.

On 27 November 2024, at the call of the Italian National Association of Deaf People (ENS: Ente Nazionale Sordi), thousands of deaf people from all over Italy gathered in Santi Apostoli Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to ask the Government for concrete interventions against discrimination and more efforts towards inclusion and accessibility.

On 25 November 2024, on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, at the call of the municipality, people, including students, took to the streets in Parma (Emilia-Romagna) to protest against gender violence. Students read the names of the victims of 2024 femicides and the names of the murderers. The mayor of Parma (Independent), the councilor for Rights and Equal Opportunities (PD) and the President of the City Council (PD) took part in the event.

On 30 November 2024, the Corsican Nationalist Movement Core In Fronte demonstrated outside the offices of Moby Lines in the port of Santa Teresa Gallura (Sardegna) and held a protest press conference against the deterioration of maritime connections between Corsica and Sardinia. Representatives of the Sardinian independence party Entula were present too.

On 12 December 2024, about 30 workers employed as drivers for companies operating in the chauffeur-driven rental service (NCC) staged a slow-driving protest in Aosta (Valle d'Aosta) against new regulations affecting the sector. The protest was part of a national mobilization against the provisions introduced by interministerial decree 226, which include mandatory 20-minute breaks, the obligation to communicate customers' data to the Ministry of Transport, and requirements such as returning to the company's base between services.

On 13 December 2024, lawyers and representatives of Bar Associations from multiple municipalities across Campania protested in Napoli (Campania) against the state of the National Judicial System. They cited insufficient administrative staff, a shortage of Justices of the Peace, and inadequate court facilities as key issues, warning of worsening delays and inefficiencies.

On 14 December 2024, pro-Palestine activists took to the streets of Milano (Lombardia) to protest against the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Representatives of the Palestinian community in Italy, Communist Refundation, the International Women's House, women, and students participated in the protest. Demonstrators also protested against the killing of civilians in Syria and the Security Decree, namely a bill set to sanction protests, occupations, and roadblocks (DDL Sicurezza). Finally, protesters also commemorated Ramy Elgaml, a nineteen-year-old who recently died in a scooter accident during a police chase.

On 11 January 2025, around 500 people, including residents, ARCI representatives, and workers, gathered outside an ARCI seat on Cervino Street in Torino (Piemonte) to express solidarity with the circle's staff after unknown perpetrators placed a cherry bomb outside the entrance of the building some days prior (coded separately). Demonstrators asked for more safety and a swift investigation into the event, which they deemed an act of intimidation. MP Andrea Giorgis (PD), the deputy mayor of Torino (PD), several municipal councilors and members of PD and AVS, and regional councilor Nadia Conticelli (PD) participated in the demonstration.

On 18 January 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of Florence for Palestine (Firenze per la Palestina), around 100 people staged a protest in San Marco Square in Firenze (Toscana) to ask for the boycott of collaborations with Israeli universities and with companies in the defense and security sector, such as Leonardo, which, according to the protesters, sell weapons to Israel. Protesters held a banner with thousands of names of Palestinian minors killed by Israeli bombings.

On 22 January 2025, at the call of the local committee '#IAmWithSaverio' (#IoStoConSaverio), people gathered outside a private home in Taranto (Puglia) to protest against the forceful eviction of an older mother and her autistic adult son from their home. Some protesters climbed onto the roof as a symbolic gesture to oppose the eviction.

On 27 January 2025, following the discovery of larvae in school canteen meals, parents of children enrolled at public elementary schools demonstrated in Massa Lubrense (Campania) to demand checks on the production and distribution of meals. Protesters also demanded alternative meals be provided to the kids.

On 23 December 2024, about 20 Beko workers gathered outside factory gates in Siena (Toscana) and staged a picket to protest against the planned closure of the production site. Representatives of RSU participated in the protest.

On 9 February 2025, farmers with about 50 tractors drove at a slow pace along the Florence-Pisa-Livorno highway and then across the city of Firenze (Toscana), where they staged a picket as part of a national demonstration to protest against the growing crisis in the sector. Protesters asked for more support and criticized the government for its lack of concrete actions following last year's demonstrations. Representatives of Representatives of Coapi participated in the protest.

On 26 June 2020, a protest organized by the feminist movement Non Una di Meno took place in Dell'Esquilino square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio). Protesters gathered to protest against injustices against women, which worsened during the coronavirus emergency. Media reported that protesters gathered in dozens of Italian cities.

On 22 February 2025, as part of a national demonstration, about 5,000 people, including representatives of the association 'At Full Capacity' (A Pieno Regime), members of self-managed social centers, students, antifascist activists, workers, and residents, took to the streets in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to protest against a bill set to sanction protests, occupations, and roadblocks (DDL Sicurezza). The deputy mayor of Bologna (AVS) participated in the demonstration.

On 25 February 2025, family members of people suffering from disabilities staged a demonstration outside the Campania Regional Council seat in Napoli (Campania) to protest a delay in the allotting of state funds aimed at supporting caretakers. Demonstrators also demanded a transparent and streamlined management of the funds. A regional councilor (M5S) participated in the demonstration.
On 22 February 2025, as part of a national demonstration, people demonstrated in Isernia (Molise) against a bill set to sanction protests, occupations, and roadblocks (DDL Sicurezza).

On 22 February 2025, at the call of the 'Trieste Committee for Palestine' (Comitato Trieste per la Palestina) and 'Picket OdV Salaam Olive Tree Kids' (Presidio Odv Salaam Ragazzi Dell'Olivo), about 30 people gathered in Trieste (Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to protest against the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian people.

On 2 March 2025, in the morning, at the call of IV, people gathered in Corso Magenta in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to express solidarity with Ukraine, emphasize the importance of European unity and democratic values and demand the immediate accession of Ukraine to the European Union. In the afternoon, several hundred people, including elected representatives, PD and More Europe affiliates, and members of the Ukrainian community, gathered in Mercanti Square in Milano - Municipio 1 at the call of Action for the same reasons.

On 19 March 2025, 5 Last Generation activists staged a protest at a Michelin restaurant owned by renowned chef Carlo Cracco in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) as part of the initiative 'The Right Price', a campaign against luxury, excess, and extreme inequality. Protesters demanded concrete actions in support of the less fortunate and highlighted the necessity of sharing equitably and promoting social justice. The police dragged the protesters outside and reported them.
On 23 January 2020, a group of shop owners blocked the work for the new cycle path in Terni. They claim that there will be less car parks due to the bike path construction.

On 15 March 2025, at the call of the committee Families Suspended, Lives on Hold (Famiglie sospese, vite in attesa), people, including FI, FdI, Lega, PD and EV local elected representatives, gathered in Della Scala Square in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to demand urgent legislative and administrative action to unblock seized construction sites and protect the housing rights of approximately 1,600 families left without homes due to ongoing legal investigations.

On 17 March 2025, at the call of CGIL and CISL, striking Feltrinelli employees gathered in front of their bookstore on Melo Street in Bari (Puglia) to denounce the lack of renewal of the national employment contract for bookstore workers.
On 17 March 2025, people gathered in Siracusa (Sicilia) to protest against the construction of a Waste Collection Center (CCR).

On 28 March 2025, at 9.30 am, around 500 striking metalworkers and Beko workers marched from Albertini Street to the Confindustria headquarters in Ancona (Marche), blocking traffic. Protesters lit smoke bombs and waved flags.

On 28 March 2025, 7,000 striking metalworkers took to the streets, blocking traffic, in Reggio Emilia (Emilia-Romagna). This was part of a nationwide mobilization, called by FIOM CGIL, FIM CISL and UILM (UIL), to demand the reopening of negotiations for a new national collective labor contract.

On 24 March 2025, people, including farmers, members of farmers groups 'Conca' and 'Italian Farmers' (Agricoltori Italiani), and a former MP (M5S), interrupted a panel discussion featuring the Italian Minister of Agriculture (FdI) during the event 'Farming Is' (Agricoluta E) in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against the sector crisis and the government's lack of action.
On 11 April 2025, at the call of FFF, hundreds of people marched in Torino (Piemonte) to demand urgent action on climate change.

On 5 April 2025, at around 1 pm, about 50 people, including pro-Palestine activists and representatives of self-managed social centers, demonstrated in the Torrette neighborhood in Ancona (Marche) against the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Protesters gathered outside a McDonald's joint, exposing banners and Palestinian flags, and then entered the restaurant to hand out flyers and condemn the multinational for having offered free meals to Israeli soldiers.

On 17 April 2025, people, including residents and members of the local Committee Oriani (Comitato Oriani), gathered on Oriani Boulevard in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to protest the administration's decision to cut six pine trees.

On 12 April 2025, around 30 people gathered on the steps of the municipality of Marino (Lazio) to demand the resignation of the mayor due to his perceived failure to address the town's declining conditions and neglect of essential public services.

On 19 April 2025, at around 3 pm, people, including pro-Palestine activists, marched from Loreto Square to the Trotter Park in Milano - Municipio 2 (Lombardia) to protest the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Protesters criticized the Italian government and protested repression and national and European rearmament plans.

On 29 April 2025, at the call of CGIL, people gathered at the Esselunga construction site in Mariti Street in Firenze (Toscana), on the occasion of the World Day for Health and Safety at Work, to demonstrate against unsafe labor conditions.

On 4 May 2025, a small group of people, including antifascist activists, staged a demonstration in Genova (Liguria) to protest against fascism and condemn the annual commemoration of a 32-year-old MSI activist who was killed by far-left activists during a speech by Giorgio Almirate on 1 May 1970. The commemoration included representatives of CasaPound Italia, and members of other far-right associations, including Loyalty Action and Skinheads Veneto Front.

On 27 May 2025, at around 11:30 am, at the call of OSA and Changing Course, about 80 people, including students, took to the streets in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna)to protest the Italian government, pending a speech of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Demonstrators protested a bill set to sanction protests, occupations, and roadblocks more harshly (DDL Sicurezza), the rearmament plans at the national and European levels, and police repression. As part of the event, called No Meloni Day, a student chained themselves outside the Minghetti High School while others set a banner with the words 'Rearm Plan' on fire on Aldo Moro Boulevard.

On 26 May 2025, at the local call of the Turin Antifascist Committee (Comitato Antifascista Torinese), people, including antifascist activists, gathered in Castello Square in Torino (Piemonte) to protest a bill set to sanction protests, occupations, and roadblocks more harshly (DDL Sicurezza). The event was held as part of a national demonstration against the Italian government and the passing of the bill.

On 31 May 2025, people, including Last Generation activists, gathered inside a supermarket in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to demand more climate action and VAT reductions on basic items and foods. The event was part of the national demonstration 'Let's Cut the VAT' called by Last Generation to promote social justice and fight against price increases and poverty.
On 23 June 2025, about 100 residents staged a flash mob in Boscoreale (Campania) to protest the planned closure of the Minerva Theatre and demand that competent authorities preserve the theatre.

On 20 June 2025, at the call of USB, workers employed by delivery company Glovo demonstrated outside the municipality of Torino (Piemonte) to protest their working conditions and low wages. Protesters also demanded that their sector's labor contract be updated. The mayor of Torino (PD), the deputy mayor (PD), and a councilor (PD) met with the protesters to ensure the administration would focus on their instances.

On 4 July 2025, during a municipal council session in Manfredonia (Puglia), dozens of residents staged a protest action against a recent increase in the waste-collection tax (TARI), displaying signs reading 'Lower the taxes, we are not cows!' and 'Resignations!'. Protesters denounced the 24-percent tax hike, citing errors in the calculation, inadequate public services, and unmanageable financial burdens. The demonstration caused verbal tensions outside the council chamber, prompting intervention by the State Police, though the nature of the intervention was not specified.

On 2 July 2025, court employees on temporary contracts staged a demonstration in front of the Tribunal in Torre Annunziata (Campania) to protest against job insecurity and the impending expiration of their contracts. The demonstrators demanded that the upcoming national budget law include provisions to stabilize their positions and ensure long-term employment, warning that the failure to do so could result in mass dismissals. The protest was part of a broader mobilization within the justice sector.

On 19 July 2025, at the call of Stop Rearm Europe, around 1,500 people, including CGIL and PRC affiliates, and M5S elected officials, gathered in front of the US military base Camp Darby in Tirrenia (Toscana) to demonstrate against the rearmament policies of the European Union and NATO countries. They also expressed solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemned Western military and economic complicity in conflicts, and commemorated the 30th anniversary of the Srebrenica genocide.

On 20 August 2025, at 6:30 am, about 30 residents gathered on Don Minzoni Street in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to protest the planned cutting of a maritime pine. Demonstrators displayed banners with slogans such as 'More trees and less concrete' and 'Do not cut healthy trees', criticizing the municipality's policy of tree removal and demanding greater transparency.

On 4 September 2025, in the late afternoon, at the call of the Global Movement to Gaza, thousands of people marched from Duca d'Aosta Square through Repubblica Square to Porta Venezia Gate in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to support the Global Sumud Flotilla, a fleet aiming to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza. The demonstration was backed by around 80 organizations, with participants highlighting international solidarity and calling for continued mobilization in support of Gaza.

On 6 September 2025, residents, workers, and pro-Palestine activists gathered in Avezzano (Abruzzo) to protest the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. The event was held as part of a national demonstration called by the CGIL in support of the Global Sumud Flotilla, an international maritime initiative launched in mid-2025 to break the Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip.
On 7 July 2020, nearly a dozen psychiatrists gathered outside the Provincial Health Authority in Reggio Calabria to protest against the lack of funding in their sector and the delay in payments.

On 26 September 2025, at the call of the Committee for Remigration and Reconquest (Comitato Remigrazione e Riconquista), numerous people staged a protest in Del Popolo Square in Latina (Lazio), demanding an end to degradation, crime, and insecurity in the city, calling for immediate action and a 'remigration program'.

On 20 September 2025, at around 6 pm, Last Generation activists gathered outside the entrance of the Gran Reno shopping center in Casalecchio (Emilia-Romagna) to protest economic ties between several multinationals, including Zara and Carrefour, and the Israeli government. Demonstrators also protested the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians.

On 2 October 2025, at the call of FIM-CISL, 30 employees at Bluesteel staged a picket line in Colle Umberto (Veneto) to demonstrate against the planned shutdown of Bluesteel's production and the broader lack of job security, demanding clear commitments and solutions from the company (Somec Group) to safeguard jobs and clarify the firm's future.

On 2 October 2025, in the evening, people gathered in front of the hospital in Colleferro (Lazio) in support of Palestine and to commemorate medical personnel killed in Gaza. The event was part of a nationwide flash mob, 'Lights on Palestine: 100 Hospitals for Gaza', organized by the healthcare networks FastingGaza (DigiunoGaza) and Health Workers for Gaza (Sanitari per Gaza).

On 3 October 2025, hundreds of people staged a protest in Lecco (Lombardia). The event was part of an nationwide demonstration movement called by USB, CGIL, CUB and SGB, following the interception (1-3 October 2025) by Israeli forces of the Global Sumud Flotilla, a humanitarian convoy of more than 40 vessels and some 500 participants bound for Gaza, denounced by activists as a violation of international law and of the right to deliver humanitarian aid.

On 3 October 2025, people staged a protest in Macerata (Marche). The event was part of an nationwide demonstration movement called by USB, CGIL, CUB and SGB, following the interception (1-3 October 2025) by Israeli forces of the Global Sumud Flotilla, a humanitarian convoy of more than 40 vessels and some 500 participants bound for Gaza, denounced by activists as a violation of international law and of the right to deliver humanitarian aid.

On 3 October 2025, people, including students, staged a protest in Matera (Basilicata). The event was part of an nationwide demonstration movement called by USB, CGIL, CUB and SGB, following the interception (1-3 October 2025) by Israeli forces of the Global Sumud Flotilla, a humanitarian convoy of more than 40 vessels and some 500 participants bound for Gaza, denounced by activists as a violation of international law and of the right to deliver humanitarian aid.

On 2 October 2025, in the evening, 3,000 people, including health workers, staged a torchlight march in Ravenna (Emilia-Romagna) to show solidarity with Palestinians, call for an end to the conflict, and commemorate medical personnel killed in Gaza. The event was part of a nationwide flash mob, 'Lights on Palestine: 100 Hospitals for Gaza', organized by the healthcare networks FastingGaza (DigiunoGaza) and Health Workers for Gaza (Sanitari per Gaza).

On 9 July 2020, around 50 residents, together with the Gramsci Avenue Committee and some right-wing politicians, demonstrated against the local administration in Modena (Modena, Emilia-Romagna) regarding its inaction tackling the problems of the avenue, including the presence of drug dealers.

On 8 October 2025, at around 7 pm, more than 300 pro-Palestine activists took to the streets in Bergamo (Lombardia) to demonstrate against the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. The event was held at the local call of Bergamo Network for Palestine (Rete Bergamo per la Palestina) as part of a wave of demonstrations in solidarity with a group of sailboats bound to Gaza to deliver humanitarian aid under the Global Sumud Flotilla banners. During the demonstration, a group of activists bypassed the police cordon placed to protect the municipality and entered the building's courtyard, occupying it for about 30 minutes before resuming the protest march. Representatives of the PRC participated in the demonstration.

On 10 July 2020, street vendors staged a protest outside the Regional Council's offices in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to urge the approval of a provision that would allocate EUR 160 million to support workers and companies suffering from the economic consequences of the coronavirus crisis.

On 17 October 2025, at the call of FP CGIL, FIT CISL, Uiltrasporti, FIADEL, and UGL, hundreds of striking waste collectors gathered in Treviso (Veneto) to demonstrate. The protest was part of a nationwide strike in the environmental hygiene sector to demand the renewal of the national collective labor agreement (CCNL), which expired on 31 December 2024.
