Workers demanded fair wage increases, better safety conditions, and recognition of new professional roles.

On 12 October 2025, more than 200,000 people from all over Italy, including workers, participated in the March for Peace and walked from Perugia (Umbria) to Assisi (Umbria) to denounce all wars and call for global peace. Demonstrators carried rainbow peace flags alongside those of Ukraine, Palestine, Russia, and Israel. Representatives of CGIL and other unions participated, reaffirming opposition to war and militarization under the slogan 'Imagine all the people.'

On 31 October 2025, striking health workers marched from the San Raffaele Hospital to the Lombardy regional offices in Milano - Municipio 3 (Lombardia) to demonstrate against the lack of renewal of the Aiop private-healthcare contract, frozen bonuses, worsening working conditions and pay, excessively long waiting lists, and what they describe as unacceptable levels of cleanliness and hygiene leading to staff leaving the hospital.

On 6 November 2025, more than 200 striking private pharmacy employees demonstrated in Venezia (Veneto) to protest their current working conditions. The event was held as part of a national demonstration called by FILCAMS CGIL, FISASCAT CISL, and UILTUCS UIL to demand the update and renewal of the sector's national labor contract and wage increase.

On 7 November 2025, in the evening, residents and members of the local committee People's City (Citta delle Persone) demonstrated on Bronzetti Street in Milano - Municipio 4 (Lombardia) to demand more road safety and stricter norms following a car accident that cost the life of an 87-year-old resident.

On 21 November 2025, at the call of CGIL, FILCTEM CGIL, FIOM CGIL, UILTEC UIL, UILM, and UIL, striking workers staged a flash mob and a picket on Tornabuoni Street in Firenze (Toscana) to protest worker exploitation and a law proposal that would shield fashion brands from criminal charges in cases where subcontracting companies were found guilty of exploitation and illegal practices.

On 22 November 2025, in the evening, at the call of Non Una di Meno, about 7,000 women, residents, activists, and members of the LGBTQ+ community took to the streets of Roma - City Center (Lazio), from Repubblica Square to San Giovanni Square to protest gender violence, femicides, repression, and the patriarchy pending the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on 25 November. Demonstrators also protested the Italian government, PM Giorgia Meloni, all wars, and the rearmament and defense plans being discussed at both the national and European levels.

On 29 November 2025, people took to the streets in Trento (Trentino-Alto Adige) to commemorate those killed or harmed by transphobic violence and to denounce discrimination, calling for greater respect, legal protection and social recognition of trans people.

On 9 January 2026, people, including PRC and AVS affiliates, gathered outside the Prefecture in Cremona (Lombardia) to protest against the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. Demonstrators also condemned what they described as the silence and complicity of the Italian government and European institutions, arguing that they failed to respond to the US move, which they portrayed as driven by oil interests.

On 19 December 2025, at around 12 pm, 3 striking Egyptian nationals employed by a subcontracting construction company working on the project of a hotel of the B&B Hotels al Tronchetto chain climbed on top of a crane in the hotel's worksite in Venezia (Veneto) to protect their working conditions and demand the immediate payment of pending salaries.

On 24 January 2026, a large number of striking administrative workers and teachers gathered in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to protest the management of the Public School System and the merging of school complexes. The President of the Region (PD), a regional councilor (PD), the Mayor of Bologna (PD), local administrators, regional councilors, members of several associations, parents, students, residents, and representatives of FLC CGIL, CISL SCUOLA, UIL Scuola, Gilda UNAMS, SNALS CONFSAL, and ANIEF participated in the demonstration.
On 23 February 2026, residents gathered in Piadena Drizzona (Lombardia) to demonstrate against trains being left idling overnight at the local train station.

On 3 March 2026, at 3 am, striking Bartolini workers and representatives of USB staged a picket outside the Bartolini seat in Origgio (Lombardia) to protest their working conditions and demand an update in their national labor contract.
On 9 March 2026, at the call of CGIL, around 50 metalworkers gathered in Reggio Emilia (Emilia-Romagna) to demand equal pay and better rights for women in the workplace.

On 9 March 2026, in the morning, people, including CGIL affiliates, gathered in Mestre (Veneto), protesting low wages, job insecurity, involuntary part-time work, and the gender pay gap that disproportionately affects women. The event was held as part of a nationwide demonstration on International Women's Day.

On 12 March 2026, students, activists, and members of CUA demonstrated in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) against police violence, repression, and authoritarianism, while commemorating a student and member of Continuous Struggle (Lotta Continua) killed by the police in 1977. Demonstrators also criticized the administration (including deputy mayor Emily Clancy) and the forcible eviction, a week prior (coded separately), of a protest picket against the project for the construction of the Children's Museum (MuBa).

On 14 March 2026, in the afternoon, at the nation-wide call of NIDIL CGIL, about 30 striking delivery workers (including foreign nationals) employed by companies such as Deliveroo and Glovo gathered in Bergamo (Lombardia) to demonstrate against their working conditions and low wages. Protesters also demanded a new national labor contract.

On 30 March 2026, on the second day of the European Outdoor Show, Extinction Rebellion activists, including some dressed as Pikachu, members of the association Road Workers' House (Casa Cantoniera), and representatives of Critical Mass, demonstrated in Parma (Emilia-Romagna) against the expo, the weapon-making industry, war, and hunting as a sport.

On 30 March 2026, 54 striking Peg Perego workers took to the streets in San Dona di Piave (Veneto) to protest the company's decision to move the production site to Lombardy and the planned cutting of 45 jobs. Representatives from FIM CISL and FIOM CGIL participated in the demonstration.

On 10 April 2026, about 8,000 farmers, residents, and members of Coldiretti took to the streets in Bari (Puglia) to protest the crisis of the agricultural sector and demand concrete action in support of Italian farmers.

On 13 April 2026, at 1 pm, striking Menarini workers staged a picket outside the company's seat in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to protest the company-mandated transfer of a worker to the Caserta offices. Demonstrators opposed the forced transfer of any employees. Representatives of FIOM CGIL, FIM CISL, and UILM UIL participated in the demonstration.

On 14 April 2026, around 40 astrophysics researchers protested outside the observatory in Padova (Veneto) as part of a national mobilization against precarity and in support of stable contracts at the INAF - Italy's National Institute for Astrophysics (Istituto Nazionale di Astrofisica).

On 26 April 2026, at the call of ANPI and CGIL, hundreds of Antifa activists, including MEP Ilaria Salis (AVS), gathered in Dongo (Lombardia) to demonstrate against the commemoration of the fifteen fascist leaders who were executed by partisans on 28 April 1945 during their attempted flight toward Switzerland alongside Benito Mussolini. Some people threw balloons filled with manure toward the neo-fascist group.

On 17 July 2020, around 100 people gathered outside a shantytown in Cassibile (Syracuse, Sicily), where migrant farmworkers live, to demand its dismantlement. The protest was triggered by recent criminal episodes in the city involving migrants.

On 1 May 2026, a large group of workers, students, activists, residents, and trade unionists took to the streets in Firenze (Toscana) to demand safe and dignified working environments, protest deaths on the job, and call for concrete actions in support of all workers. Demonstrators also protested wars, repression, and military spending. Moreover, they expressed their solidarity with the civilians in Gaza and the crew of the Global Sumud Flotilla after the interception by the Israeli navy of some ships of the Flotilla in international waters off the coast of Greece. The event, at the local call of COBAS, USB, and CUB, was held as part of the national demonstrations on International Workers' Day.

On 3 May 2026, in the afternoon, people, including street artists, musicians, and a former mayor of Napoli (DemA, took to the streets of Napoli (Campania) to protest a new municipal ordinance regulating street art and introducing fines for those who use musical instruments and small amplifiers on public streets.
Around 18 July 2020 (week of), residents of Costa street in Milano - Municipio 2 (Milano, Lombardia) staged a protest to denounce the neglect and crime affecting their road.

On 18 May 2026, at the call of USB, between 500 and 2,000 people, including PaP and CR affiliates, gathered in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to demonstrate against the war in Gaza and to show solidarity with the Global Sumud Flotilla after Israeli forces intercepted the humanitarian boats in international waters, calling for higher wages and more investment in healthcare, education, and housing instead of increased military spending and rearmament.

On 19 May 2026, about 30 striking school welfare officers, education assistants and representatives of USB took to the streets in Brescia (Lombardia) to protest their working conditions and demand a wage increase.

On 20 May 2026, in the morning, students from the Carlo Rinaldini classical high school gathered in Ancona (Marche) to demand the immediate release of their philosophy and human sciences professor, arrested by the Israeli navy while aboard one of the vessels of the Global Sumud Flotilla, intercepted by the Israeli navy in international waters on 18 May. Demonstrators protested the Israeli government, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the illegal arrest of the flotilla's crew.
On 20 May 2026, residents and shop owners demonstrated on Generale Di Maria Street in Palermo (Sicilia) to protest the implementation of a new cycle path.

On 19 July 2020, over fifty people working in a Cagliari local market gathered to protest against the transfer of the market to another location. The demonstration was supported by the USB Labour Union.

On 25 January 2020, over one hundred people gathered by the Meschio river in Vittorio Veneto to protest against the excessive use of hydroelectric, which they said is damaging the rivers, and to demand better maintenance of Italian rivers in general. They claimed that the river's biodiversity is in danger. The demonstration was organized by Legambiente and supported by LIPU.

On 1 August 2020, around 100 people participated in a protest in Imperia (Imperia, Liguria) against the closure of a local hospital and one situated in Sanremo to create a unified facility in Taggia. Protesters gathered at the call of CittadinanzAttiva and by the Tribunal of the Rights of Patients.
On 3 August 2020, over twenty No TAV Movement activists gathered with banners in Chiomonte to protest against the land expropriation in order to build the high-speed railway Turin-Lyon.

On 4 August 2020, a dozen Aqp meter readers gathered with banners in Lecce to protest against the non-payment of June, July and 14th month salary. The demonstration was organized by the CGIL labour union.

On 26 August 2020, eleven 'Industrie Meccaniche Siciliane' workers gathered outside the Town Hall in Priolo Gargallo (Siracusa, Sicilia) to protest against a court's verdict that doesn't recognize them the rights and benefits after being exposed to asbestos. They started the protest on 6 July 2020, and they have been gathering outside the Town Hall every day since then.

On 3 September 2020, a few employees of a company working in the aviation and aerospace industry climbed on the roof of their company in Somma Vesuviana (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the company that did not honor an agreement regarding temporary layoff schemes. Trade union Cgil was involved.

On 4 September 2020, trade unions representing local healthcare workers demonstrated in Dante square in Trento (Trento, Trentino Alto Adige) to demand a meeting with provincial authorities and request a reform of the current healthcare system. Shortcomings of such a system became evident during the coronavirus emergency.

On 4 September 2020, a group of Venice Climate Camp activists occupied the Regional Council offices in Venezia (Venezia, Veneto) to demonstrate against how Veneto's president and his party, i.e. Lega, managed the coronavirus epidemic.

On 8 September 2020, under twenty students and parents gathered with banners in front of the Massa Carrara province headquarters in Massa to protest against the cut in the number of beds in the Marina di Massa boarding school due to the coronavirus measures.

On 17 September 2020, workers that provide services to hospitals staged a protest sit-in in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna). Their positions have been assigned through a tender, and some companies intend to apply a national labor contract that is different from the usual one, and that provides lower wages. Trade unions Filcams Cgil, Fisascat Cisl, and Uiltrasporti were involved.

On 18 September 2020, people gathered in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) on the occasion of a national demonstration named 'Starting again from work' organized all over Italy by trade unions Cgil, Cisl, and Uil. Protesters demanded institutions to take action and tackle problems caused by the coronavirus emergency in several fields, as well as long-standing ones.

On 18 September 2020, people gathered on Duomo Square in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia) on the occasion of a national demonstration named 'Starting again from work' organized all over Italy by trade unions Cgil, Cisl, and Uil. Protesters demanded institutions to take action and tackle problems caused by the coronavirus emergency in several fields, as well as long-standing ones.

On 22 September 2020, dozens of ArcelorMittal workers gathered at an entrance of the company's factory in Taranto to protest against the uncertainty of their working conditions, problems related to work safety and the large-scale use of unemployment benefits. The protesters blocked the goods from going in or out of the factory. The labor unions CGIL, CISL, UIL and USB organized the demonstration.
On 26 September 2020, No TAV activists gathered outside a prison in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) in support of a No TAV activist who was recently arrested. Protesters opposed the verdict against her.
On 29 September 2020, Rho residents gathered to demand the re-opening of the local post office. The post office has been closed since last March due to coronavirus measures.
On 30 September 2020, farmers gathered outside the chamber of commerce in Foggia to protest against the reduction of the set price for wheat.
On 6 October 2020, Somali migrants gathered in front of the police headquarters in Torino and blocked the traffic to demand the documents necessary for traveling all over Europe.

On 8 October 2020, in the morning, food delivery riders, together with trade union NIDIL CGIL, staged a protest in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) against a national labor contract signed by trade union UGL and the Italian association of food delivery Assodelivery. Protesters considered the contract as unlawful as it was signed just by one labor union, and they claimed that it would worsen their working conditions.

On 9 October 2020, the High School Students' Network staged a protest in the Basilicata region (coded to Potenza, Potenza, Basilicata) to demonstrate against severe problems concerning the region's urban and extra-urban public transport. Protesters claimed that this situation was further exacerbated by the coronavirus emergency as containment measures are not guaranteed by the public transport system.

On 9 October 2020, protesters gathered in Piacenza (Piacenza, Emilia-Romagna) on the occasion of the Sixth Global Climate Strike organized by the Fridays for Future movement. In the morning, protesters carried out a flash-mob in Cavalli square. In the afternoon, around 20 activists staged a 'die-in' protest.

On 10 October 2020, less than 2000 protesters gathered in San Giovanni square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) for the 'Liberation March' organized by the Let's Free Italy Committee. Protesters demonstrated against the use of face masks as a measure to limit the spread of the coronavirus. Protesters insulted police forces after the latter arrested one of the demonstrators as he refused to wear a face mask, but no clashes occurred. Flags of the Italian Sovereign Front could be seen.

On 10 October 2020, Extinction Rebellion activists continued a protest at the headquarters of an Italian oil and gas company Eni in Rome - Europa (Roma, Lazio), where they chained themselves on 8 October 2020. They also staged a protest standing naked to urge the media to report the current climate emergency properly.

On 10 October 2020, people gathered on Duomo Square in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia) at the call of Non Una di Meno to protest against violence targeting women and in favor of a law decree against homotransophobia and misogyny that is about the be debated in Parliament.
On 14 October 2020, parents of students living in small towns gathered to demand better school transport outside the Molise regional council headquarters in Campobasso.

On 14 October 2020, teachers with a temporary contract gathered in front of Torino prefecture to protest against the decision to set the national exam for a permanent position at the end of the month. They claim that taking the exam during the coronavirus emergency is risky for the exam candidates and unfair for the candidates who can't make it because they have to quarantine at home. They also asked for a permanent job contract after years of temporary employment. The demonstration was supported by the labor union CGIL.

Around 16 October 2020 (week of), hospital cleaning staff gathered in Rovereto (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) at the call of trade unions FILCAMS CGIL, FISASCAT CISL, and UIL TUCS to demand better contract conditions and the renewal of their national labor contract.

Around 19 October 2020, people staged a sit-in in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) in solidarity with the town's former police commissioner, who was removed from his seat by the Tribunal of Perugia in relation to the extradition of a Kazakh citizen.

On 19 October 2020, San Carlo ballet school students staged a dancing protest flash-mob in Napoli (Napoli, Campania). The school should have reopened after seven months but remained further closed due to the new coronavirus-related restrictions implemented.

On 22 October 2020, a group of high school students from the Luigi di Savoia Institute took part in a sit-in in Mazzini square in Rieti to protest against the lack of transport routes to the city and the consequent crowds in public transports in times of coronavirus as well as against the traffic jams created by the institution of a drive-in COVID-19 testing booth in the area.

On 23 October 2020, about 100 people, among them local shopkeepers and restaurant owners and operators, gathered in Municipio square in Aversa to protest against the recent introduction of a curfew by the Campania Region president amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections.
On 24 October 2020, in the evening, around 50 young people gathered in Gallarate (Varese, Lombardia) to protest against the latest coronavirus containment measures and verbally insulted the police.

On 24 October 2020, an unspecified number of people, among them students, S.I. COBAS affiliates as well as youth representatives of the PCI, took to the streets in Largo Giulio Cesare in Milano - Municipio 8 to protest against the exploitation of workers by large companies amidst the coronavirus pandemic.
On 26 October 2020, trade unions Filcams CGIL and UILTucs staged a protest sit-in in Siracusa (Siracusa, Sicilia) in support of 12 Ideal Service workers, whose working future is unclear.

On 26 October 2020, in the morning, five employees of a company participated by Brindisi's province and who are waiting to be repositioned staged a protest outside the provincial administration offices in Brindisi (Brindisi, Puglia), demanding answers. Trade unions CGIL and CONFIAL were present too.

On 26 October 2020, a few dozens of people, including business owners, as well as employers and employees of the catering sector, staged a protest outside the regional administration offices in Ancona (Ancona, Marche) against the lastest coronavirus containment measures implemented by the Italian government.

On 28 October 2020, employers and employees of the catering sector staged a protest in Verona (Verona, Veneto) against the latest coronavirus containment measures implemented by the Italian government. The initiative was launched by Confcommercio's Italian food and entertainment federation (FIPE). The mayor was among the participants.

On 31 January 2020, around 300 people, most of them residents and members of the local Catholic community, took part in a march through the streets of Albignasego (Padova, Veneto) to demand the return of the town's priest, recalled by the Catholic Church on suspicion of having broken his vow of chastity.

On 1 February 2020, at least 11 protesters affiliated with local environmental associations staged a flash mob on Venezia boulevard in Udine to protest against the impending felling of local trees for building a roundabout. Protesters chained themselves to the 11 different trees for an hour, carrying banners to attract motorists' attention.

On 31 October 2020, a large group of people, among them shopkeepers, restaurateurs, managers of gyms, dance centres, DJs, artists, professionals, took part in a flash mob in Municipio square in Messina to protest against the restrictions to their activity introduced by a President of the Council of Ministers decree amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections and demand help from public authorities.

On 31 October 2020, around 50 students close to the self-managed social center Gramigna gathered in Delle Erbe square in Padua (Padova, Veneto) to denounce the difficulties of the school sector caused by the coronavirus pandemic.

On 1 November 2020, around 80 protesters, including business owners and their employees, gathered in Sciacca (Agrigento, Sicilia) to demonstrate against the latest coronavirus containment measures implemented by the Italian government.

On 3 November 2020, hundreds of Whirlpool workers marched through Napoli (Napoli, Campania) and occupied the rails of the city's central station to demonstrate against the closure of their plant, which occurred on 31 October 2020. Trade union UILM was involved.

On 3 February 2020, a group of New Force activists took part in a flash mob in the centre of Busto Arsizio to protest against Chinese products in the wake of the COVID-19 outbreak and promote 'Made in Italy' instead. Protesters unrolled an extra-large banner for conveying their message.

On 7 November 2020, not more than 50 people, among them Orange Vests Movement affiliates and New Force activists, took part in a sit-in in Bocca della Verita square in Rome - City Center to protest against the restrictions introduced by a government's decree amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections.

On 7 November 2020, a group of residents, health workers and trade union representatives gathered in front of the main hospital of Amelia to protest against the lack of efficiency of the local healthcare network and to demand continuous care for extra-COVID 19 patients amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections.

On 10 November 2020, La Nostra Famiglia rehabilitation center employees, together with trade union FP CGIL, staged a protest sit-in in Treviso (Treviso, Veneto) to demand the application of the national labor contract for private health workers to all the center's employees.

On 11 November 2020, workers of a fabricated metal product manufacturing industry staged an 8-hour strike and stayed outside their plant in Chiuppano (Vicenza, Veneto) as their employment future is unclear. Trade unions CGIL's FIOM and CISL's FIM were involved.

On 12 November 2020, about 30 Tricolor Masks activists took part in a sit-in in front of the Amazon logistics centre in Calenzano to denounce the discrepancy between Big Tech companies' earnings and the Italian people's increasing precariousness amidst the coronavirus pandemic. Amazon's CEO was at the centre of their protest, which occurred in a dozen cities across Italy on that day. The demonstration reportedly violated COVID-19 gathering restrictions and was unauthorised, leading to the deployment of a police force contingent and the fleeing of most protesters. Some of them were fined and 11 others were under police investigation.

On 19 November 2020, a group of ENEL energy distribution workers took part in a sit-in outside of the company's headquarters in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) to protest against strenuous shifts and the outsourcing of some of the company's activities to temporary workers and to demand the recruitment of permanent staff instead. The demonstration was part of a day of protest of energy distribution workers called and coordinated by CGIL, CISL and UIL across Italy.

On 27 November 2020, a group of Tricolor Masks activists staged a flash mob in the center of Siracusa (Siracusa, Sicilia) to protest against buying goods on Amazon on Black Friday and promote buying 'Made in Italy' products for Christmas instead. Other similar protests were organized by the Tricolor Masks across the country on that day.

On 1 December 2020, 4 Ecotecnica srl workers gathered at the Vernole city hall for the second day in a row to demand their job contract to change from part-time to full time. Their contract has been part time for years. The demonstration was supported by the CGIL labor union.

On 1 December 2020, dozens of people gathered at the Arbatax port and started a protest by honking their cars' horns. They demonstrated against the removal of the Arbatax-Civitavecchia route by the Italian shipping company Tirrenia.

On 7 December 2020, nurses gathered outside the Veneto Region headquarters in Venezia to demand an increase in salary and to have an autonomous job contract, especially after the help they provided during the coronavirus emergency. The demonstration was organized by Nursing Up.

On 9 December 2020, labor unions CGIL, CISL and UIL organized a demonstration in Salerno to protest against the conditions of the public administration. They demanded the hiring of more people, temporary job contracts to be changed to permanent job contracts, and more safety and security in the workplace, especially linked to the coronavirus emergency. They also asked for the renewal of national job contracts. The protest took place in several cities all over Italy.

On 9 December 2020, labor unions CGIL, CISL and UIL organized a demonstration in Palermo to protest against the conditions of the public administration. They demanded the hiring of more people, the temporary job contracts to be changed to permanent job contracts, and more safety and security in the workplace, especially linked to the coronavirus emergency. They also asked for the renewal of the national job contracts. Around 200 people, among them health workers, took part in the demonstration. The protest took place in several cities all over Italy.

On 8 February 2020, around 50 people, most of them anarchist and autonomous social centres' activists from Milan, staged a sit-in in front of the Versoprobo cooperative in Vercelli to protest against the structure's management of the CPR (Detention Centre for Repatriation) of Milan. Police forces were dispatched on the spot to maintain order, although no violence occurred.

On 10 December 2020, a group of high school students, at the joint call of the Treviso branch of the High School Students' Network and Priority to School, staged a flash mob outside the Berto high school in Mogliano Veneto (Treviso, Veneto) to protest against the distance learning introduced amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections and demand security guarantees regarding the reopening of schools announced by public authorities for January 2021.

On 11 December 2020, a group of local street and market vendors took part in a sit-in in front of the Puglia Region headquarters in Bari (Bari, Puglia) to protest against the lack of relief measures and acknowledgment they received from regional authorities and the government in the wake of the coronavirus pandemic and of the resultant restrictions on their activities.

On 13 December 2020, around 100 people gathered in Modena claiming that the coronavirus pandemic does not exist and demonstrating against the government's 'oppression'. They also protested against coronavirus restrictions. Some people were sanctioned for not wearing a face mask.

On 13 December 2020, around 30 people gathered with banners in Torre del Greco to protest against distant learning, implemented in order to stop the spread of coronavirus. They demanded schools to be reopened.

On 18 December 2020, a group of workers and S.I. COBAS representatives took part in a sit-in outside of the Prefecture building in Modena (Modena, Emilia-Romagna) to demand greater prevention and protection for workers against coronavirus and guarantees for those who test positive.

On 5 January 2021, people working at the Sant' Anna hospital continued the protest in Catanzaro against its possible closure. It was the the third day in a row of protest. The demonstration was organized by the USB labor union.

On 9 January 2021, a group of female activists affiliated with a regional women's rights association took part in a flash mob outside of a clinic in Jesi (Ancona, Marche) to protest against the regional government's declarations on the right to abortion and announced restraints on the administration of the abortion pill.

On 19 January 2021, a group of local farmers, some of them on their tractors, briefly blocked the SS 106 state highway in Isola di Capo Rizzuto (Crotone, Calabria) to protest against the losses incurred by their category in 2020 as a result of the coronavirus pandemic and recent heavy rains and demand relief measures from the Calabria Region.

On 20 January 2021, a group of people, among them municipal councilors and officials, gathered outside of the city council of Pisa (Pisa, Toscana) holding a banner reading 'Verita per Giulio Regeni' to demand answers regarding the death of a University of Cambridge Italian PhD student who was killed while doing research in Cairo in February 2016. The banner was reportedly meant to be affixed to the building's facade.

On 14 January 2021, around 20 high school students gathered in Cividale del Friuli to protest against the extension of distant learning, implemented in order to stop the spread of coronavirus. They demanded to safely reopen schools.

On 22 January 2021, about 40 high school students from a local student coordination committee peacefully occupied the garden of the G. B. Quadri high school in Vicenza (Vicenza, Veneto) to protest against the regional government's decision to prolong distance learning for high schools amidst the coronavirus emergency and demand their return to school.

On 25 January 2021, people gathered outside the Regional School Office in Ancona to protest against the management of schools reopening, after they've been shut due to the coronavirus pandemic. They demonstrated against overcrowded classes. The protest was organized by Priority to School and supported by the labor unions COBAS, CGIL and UIL, by the parties PaP and PRC and by the National Network of Schools' Temporary Employees.

On 20 January 2021, a group of local farmers, some of them on their tractors, continued to block a portion of the SS 106 state highway in Isola di Capo Rizzuto (Crotone, Calabria) to protest against the losses incurred by their category in 2020 as a result of the coronavirus pandemic and recent heavy rains and demand relief measures from the Calabria Region. Their permanent protest reportedly ended on that day.

On 1 February 2021, a group of Aspag Service storage and supermarket supplying workers affiliated with ADL COBAS staged a sit-in outside the Interspar supermarket at the Le Brentelle mall in Rubano (Padova, Veneto) to protest against the announced reorganization of their supply network and denounce its social shortcomings for workers.

On 31 January 2021, a group of local FFF and Extinction Rebellion activists staged a flash mob in Mogliano Veneto (Treviso, Veneto) to protest against the announcement by the Municipality of the construction of a new building in the area and demand the safeguard of trees and related wildlife.

On 30 January 2021, a few dozen people working in the fitness industry (mainly gym owners) gathered outside the Sardinia Regional Council in Cagliari to demand the reopening of their businesses, which have to be closed due to the coronavirus restrictions.

On 5 February 2021, a group of local workers dependent on the skiing industry gathered at the ski resort of Lizzola, a fraction of Valbondione (Bergamo, Lombardia), to protest against the ongoing closure of ski resorts decided by the government due to the coronavirus pandemic. The demonstration was part of the #perchisuonalamontagna flash mob, which took place across Italian mountain localities on that day.

On 25 January 2021, a group of Labriola high school students, some of them Osservatorio Popolare Studentesco activists, peacefully occupied their school in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the way their return to school was organized by public authorities after months of distance learning due to the coronavirus pandemic.

On 14 February 2021, people gathered in Repubblica square in Rome - City Center to protest in support of the Tigray women. The demonstration was supported by Non Una di Meno. On the same day wonmen organized by Non Una di Meno also gathered at the Giorgiana Masi Bridge in the Trastevere area of Rome to protest against violence against women.

On 18 February 2021, a group of various workers dependent on the legal gambling industry took part in a sit-in in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the coronavirus restrictions to their activities and call for their right to work.

On 18 February 2021, about 100 people, among them Power To The People and S.I. COBAS affiliates as well as self-managed social center activists, took part in a sit-in outside the Confindustria offices of Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the new government, simultaneously sworn in, and denounce the pro-business stance of the new prime minister.

On 23 February 2021, hundreds of culture and entertainment workers from various categories, as well as Non Una di Meno female activists and Power To The People party affiliates, marched through the streets of Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to denounce their precariousness following year-long coronavirus restrictions and demand the resumption of their activities and sector reforms as well as relief measures from the new government. The protest was organized nationally by the CGIL, CISL and UIL unions, whose leaders took part in the protest in person, and their respective culture and entertainment branches, SLC CGIL, FISTEL CISL and UILCOM UIL.

On 20 February 2021, people gathered in Melegnano (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the management of the healthcare system, especially during the coronavirus pandemic. They demanded to strengthen public healthcare. The demonstration was organized by the Right to Health Organization (Coordinamento per il Diritto alla Salute).

On 14 February 2020, people, most of them female school students under the supervision of teachers, took part in a dancing flash mob in Turingen square in Canale Monterano to protest against violence against women. The protest was part of the 'One Billion Rising' initiative and was supported by the Municipality.

On 21 February 2021, around 20 people gathered in Modena to protest against the lockdown imposed by the government in order to stop the spread of coronavirus. The demonstration was organized by the 'No lockdown' group.

On 25 February 2021, a group of striking Amazon logistics workers gathered, at the call of the UILTrasporti Piemonte trade union branch, in front of their workplace in Brandizzo (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against their working pace and their being at the mercy of the company's algorithm, and to demand more social guarantees in their day-to-day work.

On 2 March 2021, a group of pensioners backed by the USB trade union gathered in front of the Sardegna Region healthcare department main offices in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to protest against the new mode of delivery of home care services and contest the reduction, linked to the coronavirus emergency, of the hours for the delivery of medicines to Quartu Sant'Elena, in the Metropolitan City of Cagliari.

On 4 March 2021, about 30 people, most of them mothers of the defendants, took part in a sit-in outside the Palace of Justice of Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to protest the State's decision to press charges against their children, some of them standing accused of 'subversive' behavior and others of damage and resistance while taking part in anti-militarist protests across Sardegna.

On 9 March 2021, a group of ACC (ex Embraco) metalworkers affiliated with FIM CISL and trade union representatives continued to peacefully occupy the town hall of the Mel fraction of Borgo Valbelluna (Belluno, Veneto) to demand guarantees for workers following the announced company restructuring plan and acknowledgement from the government. There was no report of intervention.

On 8 March 2021, around 1,000 people gathered in the Esquilino area of Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to mark International Women's Day protesting in support of women's rights and against gender-based violence. Non Una di Meno organized the demonstration with the support of the students' unions LINK and UDU. At the same time other Non Una di Meno activists gathered in front of the Ministry of the Economic Development in Rome to demand to allocate part of the Recovery Plan on gender equality.

Around 9 March 2021 (as reported), parents of school students affiliated with the first didactic circle gathered in Pompei (Napoli, Campania) to protest against new distance learning schedules introduced amidst rising coronavirus infections concerns.

On 13 March 2021, over 100 parents, students and teachers gathered in Imola (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against distant learning and school closures due to the tightening up of coronavirus restrictions. Priority to School organized the demonstration.
On 14 March 2021, people staged a flash mob in Ancona to protest against distant learning implemented in order to stop the spread of coronavirus. Priority to School organized the demonstration.

On 15 March 2021, between 400 and 500 restaurant and business owners and people working in the gym and tourism industries gathered in Genova under the banner #protestaligure to protest against coronavirus restrictions, which severely hit their businesses. They also demanded financial aid from the public authorities. The demonstrators blocked the traffic. The protest wasn't allowed.

On 15 March 2021, Priority to School activists gathered in IV Novembre square in Perugia and placed there hundreds of shoes to protest against distant learning and school closures due to the tightening up of the coronavirus restrictions.

On 15 February 2020, about 60 people, including women and Non Una di Meno affiliates, took part in a dancing flash mob in Santa Chiara park in Sora to protest against violence against women. The protest was organised as part of the 'One Billion Rising' initiative, and was backed by the municipality.

On 17 March 2021, San Giacomo annex elementary school students, encouraged by their parents, followed their remote lessons on the street in front of their school on the hills of Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against the reintroduction of distance learning amidst rising coronavirus infections concerns.
On 22 March 2021, health workers (OSS) gathered outside Lecce Prefecture to protest against the lack of personnel. The labor union COBAS supported the demonstration.

On 26 March 2021, amusement park, circus and fair operators gathered in Mercato square in Marghera (Venezia, Veneto) to protest against coronavirus restrictions to their sector, demand greater relief measures from public authorities and to be allowed to resume their work with security guarantees. The event was part of a day of protest called by the amusement, circus and fair sector on that day.

On 26 March 2021, students, parents, teachers and school personnel gathered in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to protest against the recent reintroduction of distance learning amidst rising coronavirus infections concerns and demand the reopening of schools with sufficient security guarantees and greater public investments. The event was part of a day of protest called jointly by the Priority to School committee and the COBAS trade union.

On 21 March 2021, around 600 people, among them teachers, gathered in Varese to protest against distant learning and school closures due to the tightening up of the coronavirus restrictions. They demanded to reopen schools. The Mayor of Varese took part in the demonstration.

On 24 March 2021, around 40 community service workers backed by the UIL trade union took part in a silent sit-in in an inner yard of the town hall of Manfredonia (Foggia, Puglia) to protest against their precarious status and demand a stabilization of their contract from public authorities.

On 26 March 2021, food delivery riders gathered in Foggia (Foggia, Puglia) to demand more rights and dignity for their category and denounce piece-work remuneration contracts offered by food delivery platforms. The event, which was supported locally by NIDIL-CGIL, CISL and UILTEMP, was part of a national day of protest called by food delivery riders.

On 30 March 2021, Alitalia and Cityliner airline workers gathered, at the call of FILT CGIL, FIT CISL, Uiltrasporti and UGL, outside the Ministry of Economic Development in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to demand guarantees regarding the extension of funds for their partial unemployment status, precipitated by the coronavirus emergency.

On 31 March 2021, an orchestra conductor and his orchestra professional musicians gathered and played a waltz outside the Lombardia Region headquarters in Milano - Municipio 9 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the regional government's management of the vaccination campaign against coronavirus and demand more bureaucratic efficiency in the process.

On 3 April 2021, 2,000 restaurant and business owners gathered in Maggiore square in Bologna under the banner 'I Open' (Io Apro) to protest against the closure of their businesses due to coronavirus restrictions. They demanded to reopen their activities.

On 6 April 2021, street and market vendors gathered, at the call of the GOIA association, in front of the Palace of Justice of Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against the shutdown of their activities due to the coronavirus emergency.

On 3 April 2021, hundreds of No TAP activists gathered in Lecce to protest in solidarity with some activists sentenced by the Lecce courthouse for actions perpetrated while protesting against the construction of the Trans Adriatic Pipeline (TAP).

On 15 April 2021, representatives of various categories depending on the wedding industry (clothing, catering and entertainment) set up wedding tables and staged a series of performances in Pescara (Pescara, Abruzzo) to protest against continued coronavirus restrictions to their activities and demand a clear reopening roadmap from authorities. The protest was organized by Confcommercio.

On 13 April 2021, about 800 hospitality industry workers from across the country gathered in Circo Massimo in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to denounce the recourse to violence during protests and demand answers regarding the reopening of their businesses following months of shutdowns due to the coronavirus emergency. The protest, which was organized by 'Rome More Beautiful' ('Roma piu bella'), TNI, the Italian Hospitality Network (IHN) and Lupe Roma, saw episodes of verbal tension with DIGOS police when some protesters sought to march towards the Chambers of Deputies, but no violence.
Around 11 April 2021 (as reported), people gathered in Reggio Emilia (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to protest against the construction of 25 residential units on the Quinzio green area.

On 14 April 2021, about 20 'Calabrian citizens for public healthcare' ('Cittadine e cittadini calabresi per la sanita pubblica') group affiliates occupied the roof of the Cosenza Province healthcare department building in Cosenza (Cosenza, Calabria) to denounce the alleged deficiencies of public healthcare in the Calabria region, further exacerbated by the coronavirus emergency, and demand the immediate intervention of the Minister of Health.

On 23 April 2021, market vendors, among them FIVAG CISL, UGL Terziario, ANVA Confesercenti, ALI, CARI, Federcommercio, GOIA and FIVA Confcommercio affiliates, gathered outside the Puglia Region headquarters in Bari (Bari, Puglia) to demand to be able to resume their work after weeks of shutdowns of their activities due to the coronavirus emergency and ask for clearer guidelines from regional authorities.

On 30 April 2021, FFF activists gathered in Rome (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the alleged lack of funding allocated to the green economy and the ecological transition in the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) investment program submitted by Italy to the European Commission in the framework of the EU coronavirus recovery fund.

On 6 May 2021, public car removal service workers affiliated with the SGB trade union continued to occupy a tow truck depot in Monastir street in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to protest against repetitive failures by external companies to contractualize them and denounce their resultant reliance on unemployment funds. Protesters reportedly blocked the street, created traffic congestion. No intervention was reported.

On 7 May 2021, Regina Elena primary school students gathered in Puglia street in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to call for the pedestrianization of the street. The protest was supported by students' parents, Legambiente, WWF and the Municipality of Rome.

On 11 May 2021, Greenpeace activists brandished banners on a reproduction of a melting iceberg and kayaks on the pond in front of ENI headquarters in Rome - Europa (Roma, Lazio) to denounce the oil and gas multinational company's alleged greenwashing and its impact and call for more effective climate action. The protest was staged while the company was holding its shareholders' meeting.

On 7 May 2021, people staged a flash mob in the Galluzzo forest of Licata (Agrigento, Sicilia) to call for the preservation of the Sicilian environmental heritage and urge authorities to adopt measures for preventing wildfires. The protest, dubbed 'Facemu scruscio' ('Let's make some noise'), was organized by WWF, Legambiente, Our Italy and other environmental associations.

On 18 May 2021, about 100 hospital cleaning and multi-service employees gathered, alongside CGIL, CISL and UIL trade unionists, outside the Marino Hospital in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to demand healthcare authorities to stabilize and revalue their contracts, notably in light of their role in the coronavirus emergency.

On 19 May 2021, at least 200 taxi drivers gathered, at the call of the UGL Taxi, Federtaxi-CISAL, UILTrasporti Lazio, FIT-CISL Taxi, USB, UTI, ATI-Taxi and ATLT - ' Taxi Legal Protection Association' ('Associazione Tutela Legale Taxi'), in Campidoglio square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to demand more transparency from the Municipality and ask for an emergency meeting with the deputy mayor in charge of transportation to address a new plan tabled by municipal authorities. Some taxi drivers insulted and repeatedly shoved Rome's deputy mayor in charge of transportation.

On 20 May 2021, LGBT rights activists staged a delivery of petition signatures outside the Senate in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against alleged obstructionism of right-wing political forces to a bill sanctioning homotransphobic acts (DDL Zan) and urge politicians to approve the bill.

On 21 May 2021, health workers and USB health section trade unionists gathered in Indipendenza square in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) to demand universal and free public healthcare, a suspension of 'numerus clausus' for nursing and medicine faculties, the recruitment of additional health personnel and call for a waiver on coronavirus vaccines' patents. The event, to which a No G20 delegation from Catania also took part, was part of a national movement of strike and protest called by USB on the day of the G20 Global Health Summit in Rome.
On 15 May 2021, people gathered in Duomo square in Siracusa and staged a flash mob to show a 'renewed desire to return to live peacefully without fear' after the coronavirus pandemic.
On 16 May 2021, around 10 homeless people refused to leave a gym in Perugia to protest against the municipality's decision not to host them in the gym anymore.

On 22 May 2021, hundreds of Stellantis workers gathered outside their company in San Nicola di Melfi (Potenza, Basilicata) to protest against the uncertainty of their future working conditions. CGIL, CISL, UIL, CONFSAL, and UGL organized the demonstration.

On 27 May 2021, in the morning, around 40 ex Obiettivo Lavoro administrative, maintenance, auxiliary and healthcare social workers contracted by Cosenza province hospitals gathered outside the Cosenza Province Healthcare Agency headquarters in Cosenza (Cosenza, Calabria) to demand the stabilization of their contracts and their affiliation with the public healthcare entity. FLAI CGIL organized the protest.

On 28 May 2021, Italmondo logistics, transport and digital service workers supported by the FIT CISL trade union branch went on strike and staged a picket outside their company's center in Arluno (Milano, Lombardia) to demand better wages and working hours.

On 26 May 2021, about a dozen activists from the Colombian community gathered outside the Colombian Embassy in Rome - Flaminio (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the head of mission's official narrative, which allegedly likened victims of the Colombian police crackdown to 'criminals' and 'guerrilla fighters'. The crackdown was orchestrated following a protest movement against tax reforms championed by the Colombian presidential administration.

On 25 May 2021, residents, entrepreneurs and representatives of local committees and associations gathered in Italia square in Perugia (Perugia, Umbria) to warn about the environmental impact of a 7.5-km road junction project near the city that should connect the Perugia fraction of Collestrada to Monte Castello di Vibio's Madonna del Piano fraction.

On 6 February 2021, Legambiente activists gathered in Caltanissetta (Caltanissetta, Sicilia) to protest against the felling of trees in Michelangelo street to construct a building and denounce the alleged unlawfulness of the move.

On 23 May 2021, around 35 Standing Sentinels gathered in Duomo square in Crema (Cremona, Lombardia) to protest against the adoption of the 'Zan Law', which criminalizes violence and hate speech against LGBT people, misogyny, and ableism. Around 10 Skinheads Front Veneto activists took part in the demonstration.
On 23 May 2021, people gathered in monte Faito street in Pescara to clean the surrounding lawns. They did so in protest against the Municipality's inaction in taking care of the lawns.

On 28 May 2021, in the evening, a few hundred people, including representatives of the Pakistani and other communities and members of civic and voluntary associations, gathered for a torchlight procession, in Unita d'Italia square, in Novellara (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to demand answers regarding the disappearance of an 18-year-old girl of Pakistani origins one month before. The protest was organized by the Municipality and saw the participation of the mayor of Novellara, other mayors from the region and other institutional representatives.

On 29 May 2021, migrants gathered outside AIA (hotel managers' association) offices in Rimini to protest against racism after the hotel managers declared that migrants could not stay in the touristic area. A representative of ADL COBAS took part in the demonstration.

On 2 June 2021, 'Equal Rights' ('Equi Diritti') local branch affiliates and members of committees for the right to housing gathered in Velletri (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the acquisition and demolition of illegal homes.

On 9 June 2021, people dressed as ghosts staged, with the support of the CISL Scuola trade union branch, a 'flash mob' protest in Castello square in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to ask the government to amend measures included in its latest coronavirus relief bill for education, notably to stabilize the contracts of precarious school workers. The event was part of a national day of protest called by school trade union branches and teachers' trade unions.

Around 12 June 2021 (as reported), students, teachers, parents, and school staff of Marconi high school gathered outside the Pescara province headquarters to protest against the uncertainties of the high school's future after the demolition of a part of the school.

On 15 June 2021, 'Shadow Line' ('Linea d'Ombra') volunteer organization affiliates gathered in Liberta square in Trieste (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to protest against alleged violations of the fundamental rights of migrants and refugees along the Balkan route.

On 19 June 2021, between 50 and 70 Pro Life and Family activists gathered in XX Settembre Square in Lecco to protest against the adoption of the 'Zan Law', which criminalizes violence and hate speech against LGBT people, misogyny, and ableism. They claimed that the law would restrict the freedom of expression. The Mayor of Pescate, a Bergamo council member, and an FI representative took part in the demonstration. On the same day, FdI activists organized a protest booth in Cermenati Square for the same reasons.

On 19 June 2021, people gathered outside the Baronissi town hall (Salerno, Campania) to protest against the pollution produced by the surrounding factories. Legambiente organized the demonstration. The Baronissi Mayor, a Baronissi council member, the Montoro Vice Mayor, and 'Salute e Vita' (Health and Life) activists took part in the event.

On 19 June 2021, people gathered in the Bosco di Sopra area of Canicattini Bagni (Siracusa, Sicilia) to protest against the Region's concession to a private company to build a photovoltaic system, which would cover 100 hectares, covering part of the Iblei National Park. The Mayors of Noto, Canicattini Bagni and Buscemi, a Siracusa council member, ANCI Sicilia Vice President, M5S national and regional MPs, Legambiente, Slow Food, ARCI, and local environmentalist associations took part in the demonstration.

On 12 March 2020, a group of workers on strike from the Emiliana Serbatoi manufacturing company affiliated with S.I. COBAS took part in a sit-in outside of their company's gates in Campogalliano (Modena, Emilia-Romagna) to demand better protection measures on their workplace against coronavirus. Workers reportedly blocked the entrance to trucks carrying industrial input, prompting the intervention of an anti-riot DIGOS police contingent. After asking workers to disband due to COVID-19 restrictions against gatherings, the police followed up by detaining two protesters. There was no report of violence.

Around 21 June 2021 (as reported), PaP activists gathered outside Lidl supermarket in the Belfiore area of Mantova to protest against the death of a S.I. COBAS trade unionist during a demonstration after a truck hit protesters.

On 30 June 2021, over 100 environmental hygiene workers and supporters, including CGIL, FLAI CISL, UILTrasporti (UIL) and RSU representatives, gathered, at the call of FILCTEM CGIL, FEMCA and FLAEI CISL, and UILTec UIL, outside the Prefecture in Trieste (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to call for a revamp of Article 177 of the new Procurement Code, which would allegedly prompt companies from the sector to externalize their services and increase the precariousness of workers following the expiry of application extensions at the end of the year. The event was part of a national day of protest called by trade union branches.

On 2 July 2021, hundreds of members of the '7 November' movement for the unemployed took to the streets and brought garbage bags they had previously filled after cleaning the streets outside San Giacomo Palace in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to demand the recruitment of some of them as part of the Municipality's environmental hygiene and waste collection company, ASIA.

On 30 June 2021, The Good Lobby committee affiliates and supporters gathered in Montecitorio square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to call on parliamentarians to adopt a law blocking lobbying on funds related to the coronavirus national recovery plan.
On 26 June 2021, LGBT activists gathered in Martina Franca (Taranto, Puglia) to protest in support of LGBT rights and against discrimination to mark the Gay Pride.

On 1 July 2021, people, including Non Una di Meno, migrants' rights and LGBT activists, gathered in Brescia (Brescia, Lombardia) to denounce alleged institutional and judiciary biases and 'patriarchal violence' against women and call for the observance of the 2011 Council of Europe Istanbul Convention.

On 5 July 2021, people working in Rome's public services gathered in Campidoglio in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the Municipality's management of the services and to demand permanent job contracts. Trade unions CGIL, CISL and UIL were involved.

On 6 July 2021, night and dance clubs owners and operators and trade unionists gathered, at the call of SILB-FIPE (Confcommercio), outside the RAI national broadcasting offices in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against the ongoing shutdown of their venues due to coronavirus restrictions. Protesters reportedly gathered to deliver pictures and footage of dance gatherings breaching COVID-19 restrictions to the broadcaster. The event was part of a national day of protest called by SILB-FIPE.

On 17 May 2021, protesters gathered in front of the Chinese embassy in Vilnius with Tibetan flags to denounce reported human rights abuses in Xinjiang, Tibet and Hong Kong, also calling upon the Lithuanian government and the European Union to take more action to counter these.

On 11 June 2021, approximately 10 supporters of an MP from the opposition Labour Party demonstrated in Vilnius to oppose the arrest of the politician by the Special Investigation Service on corruption charges, claiming the case was politically motivated.

On 28 September 2021, approximately 50 protesters gathered in Klaipeda to oppose a new general plan for the development of the city, denouncing in particular plans to enlarge a port in the city center and cut down forests for a railway.
On 24 February 2022, a group of people protested in Mazeikiai, Lithuania calling against Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

On 12 September 2022, about 10-15 high school teachers protested in front of the Ministry of Education, Science and Sports in Vilnius, Lithuania calling for at least a 30 percent increase in their salaries.

On 11 January 2020, an unidentified number of protesters including a Catholic Bishop and a representative of the Center Party, demonstrated in Vilnius against previous police intervention in a protest on 3 January.

On 28 April 2023, around 50 protesters protested outside of the Presidential Palace in Vilnius, Lithuania, calling against the Seimas' legalisation of the migrant pushback law if there is a state of emergency declared in the country.

On 8 January 2024, Lithuanian farmers set up bonfires in the Kupiskio district, Panevezio region (coded to Kupiskis), calling against unfavourable conditions for farming in the country. On this day, farmers all over Lithuania held protest actions by setting up bonfires.

On 12 January 2024, around 30 people protested at the Lukiski Square in Vilnius, Lithuania, demanding not to remove the monument of partisan Juozas Krikstaponis in Ukmerge, to erect a monument to Vytis in the capital and to perpetuate the memory of President Antanas Smetona.
On 17 May 2024, the Coordination Council of the Opposition of Kazakhstan protested in Vilnius, Lithuania, calling against the policies of the President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

On 25 March 2025, several hundred Belarusians living in Lithuania, joined by opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, gathered at Lukiskes Square in Vilnius, Lithuania, in celebration of Belarusian Freedom Day. They later went to the Belarusian Embassy, calling against the Lukashenko's regime.
On 29 March 2025, about 100 people protested in Vilnius, Lithuania, expressing support for Palestine and protesting against the Lithuanian government's support for Israel.
On 7 June 2025, teenagers threw eggs at the LGBTQ+ march in several locations in Vilnius. Seven teenagers were detained, all minors, and later released to their parents.

On 14 July 2025, human rights activists and representatives of the #FreeViasna movement protested in Vilnius, Lithuania, in support and solidarity with their colleagues who were imprisoned for political reasons in Belarus.

On 24 February 2023, an unknown number of people assembled at the Polish embassy in Luxembourg to mark the anniversary of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The protest was an initiative of LUkraine, an organization of Ukrainians residing in Luxembourg.

Around 1 June 2023 (week of), an unknown number of affiliates of the party The Left protested in Petange (Esch-sur-Alzette), against the Luxembourgish government's housing policy and the number of unused buildings in the country.

On 2 November 2024, between 200 to 250 people, including local officials from Schengen and Perl, participated in a protest against border controls, marching from Apach in France to Schengen (Remich), Luxembourg, via Germany. The demonstration, supported by various parties and civil society organizations like Volt and Young European Federalists ('Jeunes Europeens federalistes'), advocated for a Europe without borders.
