On 5 February 2023, hundreds of people joined a protest march in Den Haag, marching to Koekamp Park, to denounce anti-Muslim sentiments in the Netherlands, following the destruction of a Quran book by the Dutch PEGIDA leader two weeks before. The protest was an initiative of the FIO (Federatie Islamitische Organisatie) and SIORH (Samenwerkingsverband Islamitische Organisaties Regio Haaglanden) Muslim organizations, and was attended by representatives of the DENK party.
On 13 February 2023, around 500 municipal maintenance workers staged a protest on the Grote Markt in Groningen to demand higher wages. The action was an initiative of FNV.
On 1 March 2023, an unknown number of health personnel of the Anna hospital in Geldrop staged a protest in front of the hospital to demand a better collective labor agreement.

On 14 June 2020, between 350 and 400 people, among whom ADO and Feyenoord football supporters, staged a protest on the Plein in Den Haag against the post-coronavirus protection measures imposed by the Dutch government and against 'Antifa' and the recent Black Lives Matter protests.
On 5 March 2023, 10 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action at Rembrandt's De Nachtwacht painting in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam to raise awareness for climate change.
On 5 March 2023, around 20 people staged a protest action in Wageningen, jumping into the Rhine to denounce a pipeline project in the river.

On 12 April 2023, about 150 employees of a supported employment enterprise and representatives of trade union FNV staged a protest in Vlissingen, to demand higher wages for employees of the supported employment enterprise and more generous travel costs reimbursements.

On 8 May 2023, hundreds of people protested in Born, to demand a better redundancy scheme for workers of the VDL Nedcar factory, which will have to close its doors in a year's time. Among the protesters were representatives of the Dutch union CNV and the Belgian unions ABVV-FGTB and ACV-CSC.

On 12 May 2023, at the call of the action group 'We Refuse the Rent Increase', an unknown number of people protested in Leeuwarden (Friesland) against rent increases and to demand that rents be frozen. Representatives of the action groups Platform Een- en tweepersoonshuishoudens Leeuwarden and ROOD and the anarchist group Anarcho's Leeuwarden were present.

On 3 September 2023, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists assembled in Arnhem (Gelderland) to start their 6-day-long foot march to Den Haag, where they would join the protest occupation of the A12 highway on Saturday 9 September 2023.

On 23 September 2023, hundreds of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway for traffic to demand a stop to government funding of fossil fuel companies. Police forces intervened with the water cannon and arrested 552 people.

On 28 June 2020, a few hundred of people staged a protest at the Malieveld in Den Haag against the post-coronavirus protection measures of the Dutch government and the subsequent prohibition of protests in different locations. The protest was organized by Viruswaarheid and prohibited by the municipal authorities. Police forces intervened and arrested 37 people who refused to follow their request to vacate the field. The chairman of PEGIDA was present during the protest.

On 2 December 2023, in the afternoon, at the call of Comite 21 Maart and 'the*movement' ('de*beweging'), between 100 to 200 people, including activists from XR, FNV, and PSR, gathered at Dam Square in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) and walked to the JD Meijerplein, to protest against PVV leader Geert Wilders. The protest focused on issues like racism, climate change, and discrimination, with the motto 'Not my prime minister'. Demonstrators held signs, chanted slogans like 'Free Palestine,' and expressed concerns about fascism and neoliberal policies.

On 7 December 2023, in the morning, at the call of Christians for Israel (Christenen voor Israel) and the Center Information and Documentation Israel (Centrum Informatie en Documentatie Israel - CIDI), between 600 and 700 people marched in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to draw attention to the fate of the hostages held by Hamas in the context of the Israel-Hamas war. The protests gathered at the Koekamp, marching in silence past the Parliament and the Red Cross, ending the march at the Malieveld.

On 16 December 2023, an unknown number of residents marched in Tolbert (Groningen) against the municipality's plan to transform a natural reserve into a residential zone, citing environmental concerns.
On 2 July 2020, dozens of farmers staged a protest procession through Breda against newly proposed fodder regulations of the Dutch government to reduce agricultural nitrogen emission.

On 16 March 2024, several dozen activists planted trees in the Sterrebos forest in Born (Limburg) to denounce that local trees had previously been cut to make room for the development of the Nedcar automotive manufacturing factory, which did not expand. The activists also feared that another 350 trees were at risk of being cut, as part of a project to relocate a road and make the factory even more accessible. The action was organized by Save the Sterrebos (Red het Sterrebos) and XR activists, who asked the province to drop the plan and invest in nature restoration instead.

On 13 April 2024, an unknown number of XR activists protested in Groningen (Groningen) against the Groningen Eelde Airport and in favor of a new train connection between Lelystad and Groningen, citing environmental concerns.

On 2 May 2024, 25 activists protested at the Dutch radio and television broadcaster AVOTROS building in Hilversum (Noord-Holland) against the participation of Israel to the Eurovision song contest. They denounced that the contest allowed Israel to spread lies and propaganda.

On 22 May 2024, dozens of pro-Palestinian protesters gathered and disrupted a conference at the University of Wageningen in Wageningen (Gelderland) to express solidarity with Palestinians and denounce the presence of companies that invest in occupied parts of Palestine, such as the bank Rabobank, that, according to the protesters, invested in illegal Israeli settlements.

On 2 June 2024, student demonstrators taking part in a pro-Palestine encampment on the Woudestein campus of Erasmus University chased a student carrying an Israeli flag in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland), in support of Palestine and opposition to Israel. There was no report of an interaction between both groups.

On 7 June 2024, an unknown number of XR and Quit with Coal activists blocked the N205 road in front of the province hall in Haarlem (Noord-Holland) to demand the closure of the Tata Steel Factory, citing environmental concerns, while supporters also gathered at the nearby parc of Haarlemmerhout. According to the activists, when they installed their tents, police cleared them and proceeded to arrest some of the participants.

On 4 August 2024, an unknown number of XR activists protested in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) against the fast fashion industry. According to the protesters, the fast fashion industry had to be held responsible for climate and human rights violations.

On 11 August 2024, about 8 XR activists blocked a canal lock in Ijmuiden (Noord-Holland) by chaining or gluing themselves to the lock, to prevent a large cruise ship from entering Amsterdam's waterways. The protesters argued cruise ships exacerbated the climate crisis. The police intervened and physically removed the activists, though there was no report of arrests.

On 6 July 2020, around 50 farmers staged a protest at the Jaarbeurs in Utrecht, where the CDA local party leader debate was taking place, against new fodder regulations of the Dutch government (of which CDA is part) aiming at reducing the nitrogen emission in the agricultural sector. The action was organized by Farmers Defence Force.

On 22 September 2024, at the call of the PSR and various social organizations and under the motto 'Don't give hate power', nearly 1,000 people gathered at Spui and marched to the Dokwerker monument in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to protest against the new government, which they labeled as 'extreme right-wing.' The protesters voiced their opposition to the government's approach to asylum seekers. Protesters carried signs and flags, and some expressed solidarity with Palestine.

On 16 October 2024, around 800 pharmacy assistants from Utrecht and Gelderland went on strike and staged a protest in Zeist (Utrecht) to demand better wages and reduced workload. The assistants are protesting stalled negotiations for a collective labor agreement, where the pharmacy companies proposed only a 2% pay increase, while unions are calling for a 6% raise and a minimum wage of 16 euro per hours.

On 13 November 2024, around 300 pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered on the Dam in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), despite the municipal ban that was put in place after the riots a few days earlier. The gathering was organized by six pro-Palestinian groups, and although the authorities designated Westergasterrein as the approved location, the 300 demonstrators assembled on the Dam. The police, in large numbers, attempted to disperse the group. The remaining demonstrators were surrounded, arrested, and placed on buses. Three buses were used to transport protesters to various locations, including the Westelijk Havengebied, where video footage released shows members of the Mobile Unit of the police using batons against demonstrators, leading to injuries, including one individual who was hospitalized with severe bruises. An investigation into this use of force has been launched by the police and the Amsterdam municipality. Police arrested 281 individuals.

On 11 January 2025, more than 1,500 protesters from XR, supported by groups such as Christian Climate Action NL and 'Christian Collective' (Christelijk Collectief), and including international protesters, blocked the A12 Utrechtsebaan in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) and nearby intersections, including the Koningskade and Zuid Hollandlaan, demanding an end to fossil fuel subsidies. Police cleared the area using water cannons and stretchers, with some protesters chained to objects. The demonstration caused traffic disruptions, including rerouted ambulances and two vehicle collisions on the A12. The protest resulted in 700 arrests, with 12 individuals detained for offenses such as incitement and assault.

On 29 October 2023, in the evening, around 1,000 pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant) for a march against the suffering of children in Gaza. The event, initially intended as a 'silent march,' quickly escalated as participants chanted slogans like 'Free, Free Palestine!' and criticized Israel's actions. Organizers condemned the lack of action by the Dutch government, particularly its abstention from voting on a UN resolution for a humanitarian ceasefire. Apart from Palestinian, also Algerian, Syrian, and Kurdish flags were seen at the march.

On 9 February 2025, in the evening, at the call of the staff of the Hutchison Delta 2 container terminal, around 50 striking workers gathered outside their workplace in Maasvlakte Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) to protest the lack of financial guarantees for a new severance arrangement in their collective labor agreement.

On 10 February 2025, in the evening, at the call of the AZC Best NO action group, around 100 residents gathered outside the town hall in Best (Noord-Brabant) during a council meeting, protesting against the potential establishment of a refugee center (AZC) in the area. The protesters, who expressed concerns over the potential impact on the village's livability and safety, hung signs on the town hall with messages like 'Best says no to an AZC.'

On 15 March 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of XR, an unspecified number of climate activists gathered on the Botlekweg near the Welplaatweg in Botlek (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic to the Esso refinery and the chemical company Nouryon, to protest the fossil fuel industry in the area. The blockade caused tense confrontations as drivers attempted to break through, with some pushing into the crowd and one car bypassing the protest via the berm; police were present to de-escalate but no arrests were reported.

On 6 April 2025, around 12 pm, at the call of XR, approximately 40 people, including climate activists affiliated with XR, gathered on the Utrechtsebaan section of the A12 in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic by occupying the roadway leading out of the city, to protest fossil fuel subsidies. The demonstration was unannounced. The police arrested all participants around 15:00 for endangering road safety without issuing a dispersal order, citing the danger posed by the location in a tunnel. According to XR, one demonstrator was allegedly struck in the face by a police officer and briefly lost consciousness. The demonstrators were transported by bus to the police headquarters, and the road was cleared by 15:30.

On 16 April 2025, in the evening, around 150 people, including about 10 members of Freedom Fighters, demonstrated on the square before the Kruisherenkapel church in Uden (Noord-Brabant), against the establishment of an asylum seekers' center on the Boekelsedijk. The demonstration was mostly peaceful, but later in the evening, after most demonstrators had left, a group of youths started throwing fences, setting small fires, and confronting police. The riot police intervened and arrested nine people: seven for aggression, and two for public drunkenness and doxing.
On 24 September 2020, a few dozen historical saloon boats rode through the canals of Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to protest against the city's new permit system, set to limit traffic in the canals.

On 26 November 2020, an unknown number of truck drivers protested with lights and horns outside a Kanters restaurant on the A16 road in Moerdijk (Noord-Brabant) against the closure of roadside restaurants due to coronavirus containment measures. They complained that this meant staying permanently in their truck.

On 25 June 2021, hundreds of public workers, teachers, students and Fossil Free members staged a protest action at the offices of pension fund ABP in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to demand the end of investment of their fund in fossil fuels.

On 27 June 2021, a hundred residents protested in Oss (Noord-Brabant) against the city's plan to build 72 emergency houses on a soccer field. They denounced that this type of flexible housing, in which tenants cannot stay for longer than two years, brought people with problems. They feared for the safety, the traffic and the integration of the incoming tenants.

On 4 April 2024, an unknown number of members of the anti-racism association Den Bosch Can Do It (Den Bosch Kan Het) protested in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) at a town hall meeting about immigration to denounce racism and the recent arrival of a PVV member. The organizers and the police admitted the protesters into the assembly room where they chanted for three minutes, after which they had to leave the meeting.
On 22 December 2021, between 60 and 70 people protested in Apeldoorn (Gelderland) against the government policies, in particular the coronavirus measures in place.
On 18 December 2021, an unknown number of people protested in Ermelo (Gelderland) against the coronavirus measures of the Dutch government.

On 12 February 2022, hundreds of local residents staged a silent dancing protest action on the Markt square in Delft (Zuid-Holland) against the coronavirus measures that forbid nightclubs to open. The event was part of a larger national movement called The Night Rises (De Nacht Staat Op).

On 11 September 2022, overnight, four asylum seekers from Morocco rallied and spent the night on a roundabout in Goes (Zeeland) to denounce the fact that they were refused entry into the reception facility in the Zeelandhallen, an emergency shelter.
On 13 July 2022, about 80 farmers gathered in front of the municipal hall of Rucphen (Noord-Brabant) to protest against the new nitrogen regulations of the Dutch government.

On 16 March 2023, an unknown number of health workers at the Albert Schweitzer hospital protested in Dordrecht (Zuid-Holland) to demand better working conditions and higher wages. The protest was organized by unions, including FNV, and was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement in hospitals across the country.

On 12 June 2023, dozens of residents protested in Hoevelaken (Gelderland) against the arrival of an asylum center in the neighborhood. The protesters were of the opinion that the number of 350 asylum seekers was too high for a village of 10,000 people. PVV and Senate member Marjolein Faber was present at the protest.

On 14 November 2024, hundreds of students and faculty members from Radboud University and the University of Applied Sciences or Arnhem and Nijmegen (HAN) protested in Nijmegen (Gelderland) against government budget cuts to education and science. Protesters gathered at the Linnaeus building to listen to speeches from the Federation of Dutch Trade Unions (FNV) and the University of Applied Sciences or Arnhem and Nijmegen (HAN). There were occasional pro-Palestine chants during the protest.

On 13 December 2024, 100 activists from Bite Back protested at the Social Deal headquarters in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) against the sale of Dolfinarium tickets. The demonstrators used banners, megaphones, and slogans to urge Social Deal to stop selling these tickets due to concerns over the ethical treatment of dolphins at the Dolfinarium.

On 28 October 2023, a small group of protesters gathered outside the police headquarters in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), where they pasted dozens of post-its on the windows. The post-its contained messages about police violence during protests, arguing that the police used excessive force against anti-government protests while allowing pro-climate protests to occur with less resistance. Along with the post-its, the group carried signs displaying images of police actions and text criticizing the discrepancies in policing. Police officers directed them to move their protest to a grassy area across from the building.

On 24 September 2024, a small group of activists protested outside the city council in Dordrecht (Zuid-Holland) against a potential settlement for Chemours, arguing it would not be proportionate to the environmental damage caused by the company. They also opposed new permits for discharging substances like Trifluoracetic acid (TFA) and other PFAS, which Chemours recently applied for, and which several municipalities had already advised against.

On 26 November 2023, in the afternoon, at the call of local organizers, an unspecified number of protesters gathered in Groningen (Groningen) to walk through the city center to promote inclusivity and unity following the Dutch election results where the right-wing PVV was the biggest winner. The organizers emphasized that the event was not a political demonstration but a peaceful gathering to show that everyone in the Netherlands is valued and accepted regardless of background or beliefs.

On 25 April 2025, at the call of Greenpeace Nederland, activists, including Bonaire residents, gathered outside the Catshuis (the official residence of the Dutch PM) in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), with a big banner saying 'See you in Court!', to remind the government of the climate lawsuit filed in January 2024 by eight residents of Bonaire and Greenpeace against the Dutch state, demanding more protection against the effects of climate change and a faster reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.

On 23 January 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the Foundation Tibetan Community of The Netherlands (Stichting Tibetaanse Gemeenschap Nederland), the Falun Gong movement, Uyghur groups, Hong Kong dissidents, and Students for a Free Tibet Nederland, around 30 people gathered at the intersection of Churchilllaan and World Forum in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), protesting the visit of Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang. The protesters called for independence for East Turkestan and Tibet and denounced the Chinese Communist Party's actions, such as erasing Uyghur culture. About 30 protesters supporting the premier from the Student Foundation of Chinese Students in The Netherlands had a prominent spot in front of the Catshuis from which the motorcade of the premier passed. Some members of the opposing protest felt that they were intentionally hidden from the visiting officials.

On 3 May 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of local boat owners, over thirty boats longer than 12 meters and many smaller vessels gathered on the Lakes of Vinkeveen in Vinkeveen (Utrecht), sounding horns during a two-hour sailing protest, to protest new restrictions on boat sizes and permanent mooring. Protesters, who felt excluded from the planning process, criticized the sudden changes, and expressed concerns about potential harm to their investments and recreational use of the area.

On 3 July 2025, XR held a sit-in protest inside the lobby of the public Dutch broadcaster (NOS) building in Hilversum (Noord-Holland), with additional activists demonstrating outside holding a banner reading: 'NOS, Be Honest!', accusing NOS news of providing a biased and unfair portrayal of critical issues such as the climate and ecological crisis, migration, and what they call the 'genocide' of Palestinians by Israel, and called for an end to what they described as unfair reporting.

On 7 July 2025, in the late afternoon, around 350 people, including local residents, refugee aid organizations, and city officials, demonstrated in front of the city hall in Wageningen (Gelderland) to protest two newly passed anti-asylum laws they described as inhumane and degrading to refugees, permit holders, and undocumented migrants. Protesters gathered under banners reading 'Refugees Welcome' to oppose criminalizing support for undocumented people and ending housing priority for recognized refugees. The demonstration was organized by local activists including a GreenLeft city councilor, with support from groups such as Refugee Under Shelter (Vluchteling Onder Dak), Refugee Council (VluchtelingenWerk), the Salvation Army, churches, and care providers. The mayor (VVD) and an alderwoman (D66) addressed the crowd, stating the local administration strongly disagreed with the legislation.

On 18 August 2025, dozens of Terneuzen to the Core (Terneuzen tot de Kern) group members protested with signs along the N61 highway near Terneuzen (Zeeland) to oppose the potential construction of two new nuclear power plants in the region. The protesters aimed to highlight the negative impact on the Paulinapolder, including land expropriation, dust and noise pollution for nearby villages.

On 29 August 2025, in the evening, around 150 people, including supporters of FC Den Bosch and members of We are Den Bosch, marched through the Bossche kermis in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) to protest against Syrian youths allegedly involved in recent violent incidents in the city. The protesters chanted slogans like 'AZC, away with you' while moving between the Parade, Kerkstraat, and Markt, temporarily disrupting the fair. Around 50 police officers, including units from the Mobile Enforcement and six mounted officers, monitored the demonstration, resulting in one arrest in the Korte Putstraat for public order violations.

On 25 June 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of FNV, about 20 people, including temporary workers at the Albert Heijn distribution center, gathered outside the distribution center in Geldermalsen (Gelderland), to protest for a better collective labor agreement and equal conditions compared to permanent staff.

On 22 May 2025, between 70 to nearly 200 demonstrators marched through the city center of Apeldoorn (Gelderland), from the Hoofdstraat street to the Marktplein square, to protest the violence committed by Israel in Gaza. Organized as a silent protest, some participants carried Palestinian flags in support of the Palestinian people, banners, and a blood-stained baby doll.

On 30 August 2025, at night, a couple hundred of people, mostly women, joined a bicycle-riding demonstration organized by the Dolle Mina feminist collective in Leeuwarden (Friesland) to demand greater safety for women and girls at night. The demonstration was motivated by recent cases of gender-based violence in the country, including the killing of a teenage girl in Abcoude. This was part of nationwide demonstrations called on by Dolle Mina against violence against women under the banner 'We claim the night.'

On 9 September 2025, in the evening, around 40 local residents protested outside the municipal hall and submitted a petition during the Overbetuwe municipal council meeting in Elst (Gelderland) to protest against plans to establish an asylum seekers' center (Azc) in their village.

On 3 October 2025, Dolle Mina group members set up a symbolic tent camp at Leidseplein in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to highlight and protest the shortage of safe shelter for women and children fleeing domestic violence in the Netherlands. This was part of a coordinated protest in twelve cities aimed at pressuring the government to expand shelter capacity.

On 5 October 2025, in the afternoon, around 250,000 people took part in a Red Line (Rode Lijn) protest in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to demand government action to stop the 'genocide' in Gaza. The demonstration was joined by members of 134 organizations including Amnesty International, Oxfam Novib, Extinction Rebellion, Rhythms of Resistance, Red Rebels, and Another Jewish Voice (Een Ander Joods Geluid), the FNV union, the Animal Party Second Chamber parliamentary leader, and Greenpeace, began at Museumplein with speeches and continued with a march through the city with demonstrators wearing red to represent the 'red line' crossed by Israeli actions in Gaza before returning to Museumplein. A smaller group of participants wore black instead of red to call for boycotts, divestments, and sanctions against Israel. Police briefly detained five people for public disturbances during the demonstration, including 2 Extinction Rebellion members.

On 7 October 2025, in the afternoon, several dozen pro-Palestine demonstrators sat on the floor inside the central train station in Leiden (Zuid-Holland) to protest Israeli actions in Gaza on the two-year anniversary of the Gaza war.

On 28 October 2025, in the afternoon, around 150 pro-Israel protesters and pro-Palestine counter-protesters gathered on the Woudestein campus of Erasmus University in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland), with one group of protesters supporting a law professor accused of posting anti-Palestinian content on social media, the other criticizing her. Pro-Israel demonstrators waved Israeli flags and banners denouncing what they called a 'witch hunt' against the professor, while pro-Palestine participants displayed a large Palestinian flag reading 'Stop the genocide by the Zionist regime in Palestine.'

On 20 November 2025, around 70 demonstrators, including members of Fok Fokker, Resistance Against War (Verzet tegen Oorlog - Veto), and the Rhythms of Resistance activist groups, gathered in front of the multi-purpose complex Ahoy in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) to protest against the annual arms fair and the production of F-35 aircraft parts allegedly destined for the Israeli military. Participants chanted slogans calling visiting exhibitors 'war criminals' and criticized companies profiting from drones, tanks, and other weapons, which they described as contributing to 'genocide' and 'global oppression.' Some demonstrators, with their faces covered, climbed a structure with advertising boards outside the designated protest zone and were arrested after refusing police orders to come down.

On 26 November 2025, from 7 to 8 pm, tens of residents protested on the Raadhuis square in Drachten (Friesland) against the high cost of the planned renovation of the square. Residents said they'd rather the 3.2 million euros be invested in other projects.
On 24 October 2020, around 20 activists of Direct Action Everywhere staged a protest action on the Grote Markt in Veghel against the opening of a store offering pig-derived products.

On 10 January 2026, protesters, among them members of Dolle Mina's, Queer040, and Eindhoven Pride gathered in the center of Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant) to protest the anti-LBTQIA+ rhetoric at events that were planned by the leader of Christian missionary organization Frontrunner Ministries, Tom van der Wal. Protesters denounced his claims that he could 'cure homosexuality'. Municipal council members from SP, Volt and Party of the Animals (PvdD) were present.
On 2 November 2020, an unknown number of activists of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest in Deventer to lament the ensuing climate crisis and loss of biodiversity.

On 18 May 2026, around 30 pro-Palestinian protesters gathered, while 10 occupied the roof of a TU University building on the Groene Loper in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant) to commemorate the Palestinian Nakba 77 years ago, and show solidarity with people in Gaza since 2023. Police ordered the group to leave after a few hours, which they did voluntarily, but when police asked students for their IDs in case they found any destruction on the roof, the group started running away from the police. One person was arrested.

On 22 May 2026, in the evening, around 50 activists from Active for Justice gathered at Roemer restaurant in Utrecht (Utrecht) to condemn the sale of foie gras at the restaurant. Participants called on the restaurant to end the sale, and on the government to ban all import and export of foie gras, as production has already been banned. During the demonstration, an unidentified person grabbed the megaphone of one of the activists and ran away with it, after which some activists followed him and a fight broke out. The police broke up the fight.

On 4 February 2020, a big number of farmers staged a protest action on the 318 highway in Winterswijk to put pressure on the negotiations between the Dutch government and farmer organisations over the nitrogen regulations.

On 4 February 2020, a number of farmers staged a protest at the A58 highway in Tilburg to put pressure on the negotiations between the Dutch government and farmer organisations over the nitrogen regulations.

On 22 February 2021, around 50 driving license instructors staged a car protest procession in Amsterdam to demand permission to resume their activities, which were suspended in the context of the coronavirus protection measures of the Dutch government.
On 27 February 2021, around 15 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest at the Paardenmarkt in Alkmaar to raise awareness for an imminent climate crisis.
On 5 March 2021, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a sit-in protest action at the city hall of Castricum to demand a municipal declaration of climate emergency.

On 27 February 2021, an unknown number of people staged a protest at a sports school in Druten to demand the reopening of sport schools, closed as a consequence of the coronavirus protection measures of the Dutch government. The protest action was organized across the country by gym owners.

On 11 March 2021, an unknown number of martial arts professionals staged a protest at the Koekamp in Den Haag to denounce the persistent ban on their activities in the context of the Dutch coronavirus regulations.
On 21 March 2021, around 500 people staged a protest at the Westerpark in Amsterdam against racism in the context of the UN International Day Against Racism and Discrimination.

On 3 April 2021, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Den Haag, evoking a snail race to denounce the slow tempo in which the Dutch government introduces climate security measures.

On 5 December 2022, environmental activists associated with Extinction Rebellion sat and blocked traffic in Trondheim to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand the declaration of climate emergency.

On 17 December 2022, around 50 people demonstrated in front of the Parliament of Norway in Oslo to protest the Russian invasion of Ukraine and advocate for the initiation of peace negotiations. Participants in the event included activists from the Red Party and the Norwegian Confederation of Trade Unions.

On 23 April 2022, people demonstrated in Bergen to oppose possible expansion of the US military presence and construction of new military bases on Norwegian soil. Activists from the Fight Committee took part in the event.
On 24 February 2023, around 100 people marched in Lillesand, Agder, to show support and solidarity with Ukraine on one year anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion.

Around 25 February 2023 (as reported), people gathered at Toraas fort near Tjome, Vestfold og Telemark, to show support and solidarity with Ukraine on one year anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion.

On 15 May 2020, people demonstrated in Bergen for a 'free Palestine' on Nakba Day, commemorating the Palestinian Catastrophe when many Palestinian Arabs were permanently displaced. Activists from the Struggle Committee participated in the event, among others.

On 18 June 2023, a sailboat with four Greenpeace activists blocked from leaving a chemical tanker in Mongstad, Vestland. Their goal was to protest against the Equinor oil company and its export of toxic oil waste to Denmark.

On 1 July 2023, Motvind Norge activists continued their blockade of Roan wind farm near Roan, Trondelag, to protest the continued operation of wind power mills in the Fosen district, despite a supreme court ruling that the license was invalid.
Around 19 July 2023, animal rights activists from Direct Action Everywhere movement demonstrated in Oslo to draw attention to animal rights violations and to promote animal welfare.

On 20 May 2023, activists from the Grandparents' Climate Action demonstrated in Tromso to draw attention to environmental problems and in support for the development of The Northern Norway Line, a prospective railway intended to traverse through Northern Norway.

On 17 July 2023, activists from the Grandparents' Climate Action demonstrated outside of the Parliament of Norway in Oslo to oppose the planned development of the Rosebank oil and gas field due to the environmental concerns. Activists from the United Kingdom took part in the event, among others.

On 7 September 2023, people demonstrated in Kristiansand to commemorate the 17th anniversary of the death of a Norwegian citizen of Nigerian origin who died while being apprehended after the 'choke hold' used by a police officer. Activists from the Struggle Committee (KK) and the Red Party took part in the event, among others.

On 20 September 2023, demonstrators, including various trade union activists, protested in Stavanger in support of the ban for hiring workers from temporary employment agencies, which had been adopted earlier by the Norwegian labor authorities. The demonstrations took place amidst a lawsuit against the Norwegian state by recruitment agencies and the intervention of the EFTA Surveillance Authority (ESA) in the context of compliance with EEA regulations.
On 8 November 2023, people demonstrated in Knarvik, Vestland, to oppose government plans to cut funding for private schools in the country.

On 16 December 2023, people demonstrated in Haugesund, Rogaland, to express their support and solidarity with Palestine. Their aim was to raise awareness about children and civilian casualties in Gaza, to advocate for compliance with international law and for the release of hostages held by Hamas.

On 16 December 2023, people demonstrated in Alstahaug Municipality (coded to Sandnessjoen), to express their support and solidarity with Palestine. Their aim was to raise awareness about children and civilian casualties in Gaza, to advocate for compliance with international law and for the release of hostages held by Hamas.
